The explicit model (c acting by v ⊗ w ↦ w ⊗ v for a fixed lift c of order 2) is its standard realization. The paper's caveat about the quadratic twist concerns identifying ad^0(r̄) with As(ρ̄) ⊗ ε^{k−1} or its twist. Neither library has tensor induction of representations.

items.name: ad^0 of an induced symplectic representation
items.statement: Let K/Q be imaginary quadratic, ρ̄ : G_K → GL2(F_p) with det ρ̄ = ε^{1−k}, and r̄ = Ind_K^Q ρ̄, which preserves a symplectic form. Then ρ̄^∨ ≅ ρ̄ ⊗ ε^{k−1} and (ρ̄^c)^∨ ≅ ρ̄^c ⊗ ε^{k−1}. Moreover ad^0(r̄)|G_K ≅ (ρ̄ ⊗ ρ̄^c) ⊗ ε^{k−1} ⊕ ad^0(ρ̄) ⊕ ad^0(ρ̄^c) and ad^0(r̄) ≅ As(ρ̄) ⊗ ε^{k−1} ⊕ Ind_K^Q ad^0(ρ̄), up to replacing As(ρ̄) by its quadratic twist.
items.note: This is a representation-theoretic decomposition for r̄ = Ind_K^Q ρ̄ with its symplectic form. Over K, ad^0(r̄)|G_K ≅ (ρ̄ ⊗ ρ̄^c) ⊗ ε^{k−1} ⊕ ad^0(ρ̄) ⊕ ad^0(ρ̄^c); over Q, ad^0(r̄) ≅ As(ρ̄) ⊗ ε^{k−1} ⊕ Ind ad^0(ρ̄). Induction and tensor induction are planned (R01.1, G7), but this identity, and the fact that the induction preserves a symplectic form, are planned nowhere. It depends on the missing GSp4 adjoint (adjoint-reps-ad-ad0).

items.name: Example 4.11(1): inductions from imaginary quadratic fields have big image
items.statement: Suppose p ≥ 5. Let K/Q be an imaginary quadratic field not contained in Q(ζ_p). Let ρ̄ : G_K → GL2(F_p) be a representation with determinant ε^{1−k} for some integer k. Suppose that, for any complex conjugation c ∈ Gal(Q̄/Q), the images of ρ̄ and ρ̄^c both contain SL2(F_p) and 'have totally disjoint fixed fields over K(ζ_p)'. The proof uses this in the form: the fields cut out by ρ̄|G_{K(ζ_p)} and ρ̄^c|G_{K(ζ_p)} are linearly disjoint over K(ζ_p), equivalently (ρ̄, ρ̄^c) maps G_{K(ζ_p)} onto SL2(F_p) × SL2(F_p). Then r̄ = Ind_K^Q ρ̄ preserves a symplectic form and has big image (Assumption 4.1).
items.note: This is a residual-image lemma. For p ≥ 5, inductions from imaginary quadratic K ⊄ Q(ζ_p) of ρ̄ with SL2(F_p) ⊂ images of ρ̄ and ρ̄^c and disjoint fixed fields satisfy H1–H3, via SL2(F_p) perfectness and the explicit element c·(g,h) with x = 2, y = 1. It is planned nowhere; the notion 'big image' itself is missing (assumption-4-1-big-image).

items.name: Example 4.11(2): image GSp4(F_p) implies big image
items.statement: Suppose p ≥ 5 and the image of r̄ is GSp4(F_p). Then r̄ has big image (Assumption 4.1).
items.note: This is Pilloni [56, Prop. 5.8]: image GSp4(F_p) with p ≥ 5 implies H1–H3. It is not planned; G7's verification lemmas cover adequacy and enormous image for GL_n only. External input: [56] V. Pilloni, Modularité, formes de Siegel et surfaces abéliennes, J. Reine Angew. Math. 666 (2012), Proposition 5.8

items.name: Serre's open image theorem (surjectivity mod p for large p)
items.statement: Let E be an elliptic curve without CM over a number field K. For all sufficiently large primes p, the mod p representation G_K → Aut(E[p]) ≅ GL2(F_p) is surjective.
items.note: No layer plans Serre's 1972 theorem for non-CM E over a number field K. FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.6 explicitly avoids it ('without requiring the full Serre open-image theorem'). HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.7 plans only 'the required open-image/cohomological bounds and their uniformity' for non-CM curves in its Heegner (over Q) setting. Planned inputs exist: Raynaud's (p,…,p) classification and tame inertia characters (R07.1, R07.5) and the GL2 subgroup classification (R01.4, whose reviewed Dickson node is in place). Neither library has it; the audit notes no Tate module in either. External input: [61] J.-P. Serre, Propriétés galoisiennes des points d'ordre fini des courbes elliptiques, Invent. Math. 15 (1972), 259–331

items.name: Faltings' isogeny theorem (Tate conjecture for abelian varieties)
items.statement: For abelian varieties A, B over a number field L and a prime ℓ, the natural map Hom_L(A,B) ⊗ Z_ℓ → Hom_{G_L}(T_ℓA, T_ℓB) is an isomorphism. In particular, if T_ℓA ⊗ Q ≅ T_ℓB ⊗ Q as G_L-representations, then A and B are isogenous over L.
items.note: The library audit marks R28.4 'not built' and records no Tate module of an abelian variety in either library. External input: [25] G. Faltings, Endlichkeitssätze für abelsche Varietäten über Zahlkörpern, Invent. Math. 73 (1983), 349–366

items.name: Group theory of SL2(F_p), PSL2(F_p), PGL2(F_p) for p ≥ 5
items.statement: For p ≥ 5: SL2(F_p) is perfect; PSL2(F_p) is simple, so the only nontrivial quotients of SL2(F_p) are PSL2(F_p) and SL2(F_p); and every automorphism of PGL2(F_p) is inner.
items.locator: §4, proofs of Example 4.11 and Remark 4.12, p. 818, 820
items.note: This is partly covered. ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4 plans 'the finite-subgroup facts of GL₂/PGL₂ used in the source arguments, including dihedral and exceptional images, normal subgroups'. Its reviewed Dickson node states 'PSL_2(F_0) is simple nonabelian as soon as |F_0| >= 4'. Perfectness of SL2(F_p) for p ≥ 5 and 'every automorphism of PGL2(F_p) is inner' are named in no layer. Neither library proves simplicity of PSL2(F_p): Tau Ceti has PSL points functors and IsSimpleGroup lemmas but no such theorem, and the CFSG statement roadmap's L3 explicitly 'does not prove ... simplicity'. Remark 4.12 (p. 820) uses three of these facts for p ≥ 5: PSL2(F_p) is simple, so the quotients of SL2(F_p) are as stated, and every automorphism of PGL2(F_p) is inner. Perfectness of SL2(F_p) is used separately, in the proof of Example 4.11 (p. 818), to get conditions H1 and H3 of Assumption 4.1. External input: Standard finite group theory (not cited by the paper)

items.name: Chebotarev density; finiteness of quadratic characters with bounded ramification
items.statement: (i) Chebotarev: for a finite Galois extension L/K of number fields, every conjugacy class of Gal(L/K) is the Frobenius class of infinitely many (a positive density of) primes of K. Hence two semisimple ℓ-adic representations with equal Frobenius traces at almost all primes are isomorphic. (ii) By class field theory, there are only finitely many quadratic characters of G_K unramified outside a fixed finite set of places.
items.locator: §4, Remark 4.12, p. 820 (Chebotarev also underlies Proposition 4.10 and the neatness prime of §6.3)
items.note: (i) Chebotarev and the recognition of semisimple ℓ-adic representations by Frobenius traces are planned (Layer 10 audited 'not built'). (ii) Quadratic characters unramified outside S have conductor dividing a fixed modulus, so they factor through a finite ray class group; that is CFT Layer 12, not built. Mathlib's Hermite theorem, NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Basic.lean:496), would also give (ii) once discriminants of such quadratic extensions are bounded, but that bound is not in either library. The precise form of (i): the primes of K unramified in L whose Frobenius class is a given conjugacy class C have natural density #C/[L:K]. Chebotarev is also used in §6.3, p. 840, for the existence of the auxiliary prime q. There L is the field cut out by r̄ × ε̄, and the class is that of the element σ from Assumption 4.2. The natural-density form is planned at Tau Ceti's Chebotarev layer 14. Tau Ceti has the Frobenius prime sets (NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet) but not the density theorem. External input: Chebotarev density theorem and global class field theory (not cited by the paper)

items.name: Remark 4.12: Example 4.11 applies to Res_{K/Q}(E) for a non-CM elliptic curve over an imaginary quadratic field
items.statement: Let K be an imaginary quadratic field and E/K an elliptic curve without CM. Hypothesis: E is not isogenous over K̄ to its Galois conjugate E^c (the paper prints "(over K̄)"). Equivalently, E^c is not K-isogenous to E or to any quadratic twist of E. Claim: for all sufficiently large p, Example 4.11(1) applies to ρ̄_p : G_K → GL_2(F_p), the dual of E[p], which has det ε^{−1}. That is, the images of ρ̄_p and ρ̄_p^c contain SL_2(F_p) and their fixed fields satisfy F ∩ F^c = K(ζ_p). Hence r̄ = Ind_K^Q ρ̄_p, the dual of A[p] for A = Res_{K/Q}(E), preserves a symplectic form and has big image. Argument, p. 820: (i) By Serre [61], for large p ≥ 5, ρ̄_p and ρ̄_p^c have image GL_2(F_p) and determinant ε^{1−2}. (ii) If H := F ∩ F^c ⊋ K(ζ_p), then Gal(H/K) is GL_2(F_p) or GL_2(F_p)/±I, because PSL_2(F_p) is simple for p ≥ 5, so the only nontrivial quotients of SL_2(F_p) are PSL_2(F_p) and SL_2(F_p). (iii) Every automorphism of PGL_2(F_p) is inner, so ρ̄_p ≅ ρ̄_p^c ⊗ χ_p with χ_p^2 = 1 (compare determinants). (iv) Take p unramified in K with E good above p. Finite flatness forces χ_p to be unramified above p, so χ_p is unramified outside N N^c, and class field theory leaves only finitely many such χ. (v) If (ii) happened for infinitely many p, a fixed χ with χ² = 1 would give a_v = χ(v) a_{v^c} for all conjugate pairs of good primes. Chebotarev and Faltings [25] then make E and E^c isogenous over the at most quadratic L/K cut out by χ. Since L ⊂ K̄, this contradicts the hypothesis whether or not χ is trivial.
items.locator: §4, Remark 4.12, pp. 819–820 (statement p. 819, argument concluded p. 820)
items.note: No layer plans the big-image argument for A = Res_{K/Q}(E). The argument compares the images of ρ̄_p and ρ̄_p^c using the simplicity of PSL2(F_p), the fact that every automorphism of PGL2(F_p) is inner, finite flatness at p, finiteness of quadratic characters unramified outside NN^c, Chebotarev and Faltings. Its two external inputs are separate items: ext-serre-open-image (missing) and ext-faltings-isogeny (planned R28.4). The class-field-theory finiteness is Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory material. Checked against the text of pp. 819–820. Step (iv) also relies, without saying so, on Raynaud's theory of finite flat group schemes: with p unramified in K and E good above p, it forces χ_p to be unramified above p. Finite flatness at p is planned at R07.

items.name: Parahoric subgroups P(x), Π(x) and Iwahori subgroup I(x)
items.statement: For each prime x, P(x), Π(x), I(x) ⊂ GSp_4(Z_x) are the inverse images under reduction GSp_4(Z_x) → GSp_4(F_x) of P(F_x), Π(F_x) and B(F_x). They are the Siegel parahoric, the Klingen parahoric and the Iwahori subgroup.
items.note: The Siegel parahoric, the Klingen parahoric and the Iwahori subgroup of GSp4(Z_x) are parahoric subgroups of the split group GSp4 over Q_x. RG2.3 plans parahoric group schemes in general, characterized by their integral points and the reduction map, so for a split group the preimages of parabolic subgroups of the special fibre are covered. This is the GSp4 instance. Nothing is in the libraries. The paper prints the Siegel parahoric as 'S(x)' in §5.2, p. 821.

items.name: The subgroup Π(x)^+ of the Klingen parahoric
items.statement: Π(x) contains a normal subgroup Π(x)^+ with Π(x)/Π(x)^+ ≅ (Z/xZ)^×, the isomorphism given by projection onto λ mod x. Here λ is the GL_1-coordinate of the Klingen Levi M_Π, the (1,1)-entry. So Π(x)^+ = {g ∈ Π(x) : g_{11} ≡ 1 mod x}.
items.note: Π(x)^+ = ker(Π(x) → (Z/x)^×, g ↦ λ mod x) is the Taylor–Wiles level subgroup. It is not a parahoric or pro-p congruence subgroup, and no layer names it. The analogous Taylor–Wiles level groups of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 (local-level-groups-Ux-Vx, level-subgroups-KQ-LQ) were also missing. The paper writes both Π(x)^+ and Π^+(x).

items.name: Paramodular group K(x)
items.statement: For each prime x, the paramodular group K(x) is the stabilizer in GSp_4(Q_x) of the lattice L = Z_x ⊕ Z_x ⊕ Z_x ⊕ xZ_x. Equivalently, K(x) consists of the g ∈ GSp_4(Q_x) with ν(g) ∈ Z_x^× (equivalently det g ∈ Z_x^×), g_ij ∈ Z_x (i, j ≤ 3), g_i4 ∈ x^{−1}Z_x (i ≤ 3), g_4j ∈ xZ_x (j ≤ 3) and g_44 ∈ Z_x. The entry conditions alone express only gL ⊆ L. K(x) is not contained in GSp_4(Z_x).
items.note: K(x) is the stabilizer of L = Z_x³ ⊕ xZ_x. Its multiplier is a unit, so it also stabilizes L^∨ = x^{-1}Z_x ⊕ Z_x³ (for the antidiagonal J), and L ⊂ L^∨ ⊂ x^{-1}L. So K(x) is the fixer of a non-special vertex of the GSp4 building, which RG2.3's 'fixer group schemes' covers generically. The matrix description is a routine unfolding. Source issue: §5.2 (p. 821) lists K(x) among the choices of 'K_x ⊂ GSp4(Z_x)', but K(x) has entries in x^{-1}Z_x and is not contained in GSp4(Z_x). This also affects the moduli reading of Y_K (see siegel-threefold-Y-K).

items.name: Level subgroups K and K_i(Q)
items.statement: S and Q are finite sets of primes of Q, disjoint, with p ∉ S ∪ Q. Q also denotes ∏_{x∈Q} x. For x ∈ S, K_x is one of P(x) (printed S(x)), Π(x), K(x), Π(x)^+, I(x), or the full congruence subgroup of level x. For x ∉ S, K_x = GSp_4(Z_x). Put K := ∏_x K_x ⊂ GSp_4(A^∞). For x ∈ Q put K_{x,0} = Π(x) and K_{x,1} = Π(x)^+. Then K_i(Q) := ∏_{x∉Q} K_x × ∏_{x∈Q} K_{x,i} for i = 0, 1.
items.locator: §5.2, p. 821 (recalled at the start of §6, p. 835, where Q = ∅ is allowed)
items.note: The specific levels are named nowhere: the menu of K_x for x ∈ S, and K_i(Q) with Klingen level Π(x) or Π(x)^+ at the auxiliary primes x ∈ Q. ShimuraData D5 plans compact open levels, neatness and the Siegel data in general. The CG18 precedent is that paper-specific Taylor–Wiles levels are missing and are routed with the R = T roadmap. The paramodular choice is not inside GSp4(Z_x) (see paramodular-group).

items.name: Neatness hypothesis on K
items.statement: Standing assumption: the open compact subgroup K ⊂ GSp_4(A^∞) is neat. This holds if S contains a prime x ≥ 3 at which K_x is the full congruence subgroup of level x.
items.note: Neatness of a compact open level is D5. The sufficient criterion (a full congruence subgroup of level x ≥ 3 at one prime) is the standard Serre lemma behind V0's existence of neat congruence subgroups.

items.name: Siegel moduli spaces Y_K, Y_{K_i(Q)} over O
items.statement: Y_K → Spec(O) and Y_{K_i(Q)} → Spec(O) denote the Siegel moduli spaces of level K and K_i(Q). They classify principally polarized abelian varieties (abelian surfaces) with K-level (resp. K_i(Q)-level) structure [57, §4.1]. In each case A denotes the universal abelian scheme.
items.note: This is the Siegel PEL moduli problem at a neat level prime to p (p ∉ S ∪ Q), over O. Its representability and universal abelian scheme are M2, and the Siegel case is M5. Caveat (E33): for paramodular K_x ⊄ GSp4(Z_x), the phrase 'principally polarized abelian varieties with K-level structure' must be read through M1's prime-to-p quasi-isogeny formulation. The equivalent reading is (1,x)-polarized surfaces. M1 plans that comparison. Pilloni [57, §4.1] is the paper's reference. §1 uses the same spaces. Y_1(N), with N = N(r̄), on p. 802 is the open Siegel threefold at the level fixed in §5.2 and §6.3. (The paper says N is determined by r̄ 'as in Section 5', but the level is that of §6.3; see E2.) X_1(N), on p. 803, is a smooth toroidal compactification of it. The compactification is covered by toroidal-compactification-hodge-bundle. The claim that coherent cohomology does not depend on the choice of compactification is covered by coherent-cohomology-independent-of-compactification. AutomorphicBundles:B3 and ShimuraCompactifications:C5 are also part of the mapping. External input: V. Pilloni, Sur la théorie de Hida pour le groupe GSp_{2g}, Bull. Soc. Math. France 140 (2012) [57], §4.1

items.name: Toroidal compactification X and the Hodge bundle E
items.statement: For Y one of the spaces Y_K, Y_{K_i(Q)}, choose a smooth projective toroidal compactification X → Spec(O) of Y. The universal abelian scheme extends to a semi-abelian scheme π : A → X, and E := π_*Ω^1_{A/X} is a locally free O_X-module of rank 2.
items.note: C5 plans the integral toroidal compactifications with their universal semi-abelian extension; Lan [51] is the source. E = π_*Ω^1 is the Hodge bundle, whose determinant is C5's Hodge line. C3 plans the refinements and level maps. One caveat for the blueprint: C5 names properness and projectivity of the minimal compactification, but not projectivity of the integral toroidal compactification (Lan, Thm 7.3.3.4). C2 plans projectivity only in characteristic 0 and for projective fans. External input: Faltings–Chai toroidal compactifications, in the PEL generality of K.-W. Lan, Arithmetic Compactifications of PEL-Type Shimura Varieties (2013) [51]

items.name: Automorphic vector bundles ω(a,b) and ω(a,b)_M
items.statement: For integers a ≥ b, ω(a,b) := Sym^{a−b} E ⊗ det^b E. Also ω := det E, so ω(a,a) = ω^a is a line bundle. For an O-module M, ω(a,b)_M := ω(a,b) ⊗_O M. ω(a,b)(−∞) denotes the subcanonical extension, i.e. ω(a,b) tensored with the ideal sheaf of the boundary.
items.note: ω(a,b) = Sym^{a−b}E ⊗ det^b E is built functorially from C5's integral Hodge bundle. B4 plans the Siegel Schur-functor weights, and B3 plans the subcanonical twist by the reduced boundary. AutomorphicBundles' completion condition requires classical forms over integral PEL models. The M-coefficient version ⊗_O M is formal. Identifying these bundles with Lan–Suh's W^can_µ integrally is a separate, missing item (W-can-is-omega). §1 introduces the case used in the main theorem, ω(j,2) = Sym^{j−2}E ⊗ det^2 E (p. 802). Its complex sections are the Siegel modular forms of weight (j,2). §1 (pp. 803–804) also writes ω(j,2)^can for ω(j,2) on X, and ω(j,2)^sub = ω(j,2)^can ⊗ O(−D) = ω(j,2)(−∞), with D the boundary. H^0(X, ω(j,2)^sub) is the space of cusp forms. The Hodge line bundle ω = det E is PELModuli:M6.

items.name: Coherent cohomology is independent of the toroidal compactification
items.statement: The coherent cohomology groups H^i(X, ω(a,b)_M) do not depend on the choice of toroidal compactification X of Y.
items.note: Independence of H^i(X, ω(a,b)_M) from the integral toroidal compactification, for all i and every O-module M, is not planned. It needs Rf_*O = O for refinements and the projection formula (Lan, Lemmas 7.1.1.4–7.1.1.5). B3 plans only independence of sections, in characteristic 0. C3, as narrowed by RS-32, keeps the structure-sheaf pushforward and 'separately stated higher-direct-image vanishing for the exact coefficient sheaves ... used by consumers', but on the characteristic-zero arithmetic models; C5 does not mention refinements. External input: K.-W. Lan, Arithmetic Compactifications of PEL-Type Shimura Varieties [51], Lemma 7.1.1.4 and the proof of Lemma 7.1.1.5

items.name: Koecher principle
items.statement: For every O-module M there is an isomorphism H^0(Y, ω(a,b)_M) ≅ H^0(X, ω(a,b)_M).
items.note: The Siegel (g = 2) Koecher principle H^0(Y, ω(a,b)_M) ≅ H^0(X, ω(a,b)_M), for every O-module M including torsion, is planned nowhere. C6 plans Koecher only for Hilbert sections. V2 says only that any use of Koecher must prove its boundary-codimension hypothesis, in the analytic characteristic-zero proof. The paper gives no reference; standard sources are Faltings–Chai V.1.5 and Lan's 'Higher Koecher's principle' (2016). PAPER-LI-23 marked Koecher planned via C2/C6 for its setting, which does not cover integral Siegel coefficients. External input: Koecher principle for Siegel modular forms (g = 2); the paper gives no reference (standard, e.g. Faltings–Chai Ch. V, or Lan's work on Koecher's principle)

items.name: Compatible compactifications X_{K_0(Q)} → X_K and the subgroup H
items.statement: Toroidal compactifications X_K and X_{K_0(Q)} are chosen so that the natural map Y_{K_0(Q)} → Y_K extends to X_{K_0(Q)} → X_K. The universal subgroup H ⊂ A[Q] over Y_{K_0(Q)} (Klingen level at x ∈ Q) extends to X_{K_0(Q)} [57, §4.1.2].
items.note: C3 plans choosing compatible fans so that the level map Y_{K_0(Q)} → Y_K extends, and C5 plans the integral models at prime-to-p level. C4 plans the comparison of level structures across boundary charts in PEL generality, which is where the extension of the Klingen subgroup H ⊂ A[Q] belongs. Pilloni [57, §4.1.2] should be added to C4/C5 as a source for this specific extension. CG18's lan-toroidal-hecke-correspondence was accepted as planned via C3 + C5 on the same basis. External input: V. Pilloni [57], §4.1.2

items.name: The cover X_{K_1(Q)} = Isom(Z/Q, H) with group Δ_Q
items.statement: X_{K_1(Q)} := Isom_{X_{K_0(Q)}}(Z/Q, H). The map X_{K_1(Q)} → X_{K_0(Q)} is finite étale and Galois with group Δ_Q := (Z/Q)^× = ∏_{x∈Q}(Z/x)^×. This defines the toroidal compactification of Y_{K_1(Q)}.
items.note: The claim is specific: Isom(Z/Q, H) over X_{K_0(Q)} is a toroidal compactification of Y_{K_1(Q)} and is finite étale Galois with group Δ_Q over the whole compactification, boundary included. No layer names it. C4 itself warns that étaleness away from the cusps does not give étaleness at the boundary. The claim needs H to extend as a finite étale subgroup scheme (Pilloni §4.1.2).

items.name: Lan–Suh vanishing theorem for subcanonical automorphic bundles (as applied)
items.statement: Lan–Suh [53, Corollary 7.24, part 2], in the form the paper applies. Let X be a smooth projective toroidal compactification, level prime to p, of the Siegel threefold over O, of relative dimension d = 3, and assume 2 < p. Let µ ∈ X^{+,<_re p}_{G_1}, let ν ∈ X^{+,<p}_{M_1} be positive parallel, and let w ∈ W^{M_1} (the Kostant representatives w̃_0, …, w̃_3) have length ℓ(w). Then H^i(X, (W^∨_{w·µ−ν})^sub ⊗_O k) = 0 for i > d − ℓ(w), where w·µ = w(µ+ρ) − ρ.
items.note: Lan–Suh's torsion vanishing theorem for subcanonical automorphic bundles on PEL toroidal compactifications is planned nowhere; an atlas search for 'Lan–Suh' has no hits. Its proof needs integral automorphic bundles from Levi representations, Faltings' dual BGG complex over Z_(p) with Kostant representatives, the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism, and Deligne–Illusie/Esnault–Viehweg-type vanishing in characteristic p. The only Deligne–Illusie mention is a caveat in DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.3, and the only BGG hit is Tau Ceti LieHighestWeight L6 (characteristic 0). External input: K.-W. Lan and J. Suh, Vanishing theorems for torsion automorphic sheaves on general PEL-type Shimura varieties, Adv. Math. 242 (2013) [53], Corollary 7.24; definitions from Lan–Suh, Duke Math. J. 161 (2012) [52]

items.name: Unwinding the Lan–Suh weight conditions for GSp_4
items.statement: Use Lan–Suh's notation with G_1/R_1 := G/O, M_1 ⊂ P_1 ⊂ G_1 the Siegel Levi and parabolic, X^+_{G_1} = X*(T)^+_G, X^+_{M_1} = X*(T)^+_M, |µ|_L = a + b and d = dim_O X = 3. (i) X^{+,<_re p}_{G_1} ([52, Def. 6.3]) consists of the µ = (a,b;c) ∈ X*(T)^+_G with ⟨µ+ρ, ±α_i^∨⟩ ≤ p for i = 1, …, 4 and a + b + 3 < p. The largest ⟨µ+ρ, ±α_i^∨⟩ is ⟨µ+ρ, α_3^∨⟩ = a+b+3, so this set is {(a,b;c) : a ≥ b ≥ 0, a + b < p − 3}. (ii) X^{+,<p}_{M_1} = {(a,b;c) ∈ X*(T)^+_M : (a+2) − (b+1) ≤ p} ([52, Def. 2.29]). (iii) A weight (a,b;c) lies in X^{+,<p}_{M_1} and is positive parallel iff a = b > 0 ([52, Lemma 7.2, Def. 7.14, Prop. 7.15]). (iv) Lan–Suh's condition max(2, r_τ) < p (τ = τ∘c) reduces to 2 < p.
items.note: This unwinds Lan–Suh's p-small weight sets for GSp4: X^{+,<_re p}_{G_1} = {a ≥ b ≥ 0, a+b < p−3}; X^{+,<p}_{M_1} = {(a+2)−(b+1) ≤ p}; positive parallel means a = b > 0; and max(2, r_τ) < p reduces to 2 < p. I checked it against pp. 822–823. It depends on the missing Lan–Suh framework.

items.name: Lan–Suh automorphic bundles W^can_µ, W^sub_µ
items.statement: A weight µ = (a,b;c) ∈ X*(T)^+_M is the highest weight of the algebraic representation (Sym^{a−b} S_2 ⊗ det^b S_2) ⊗ S_1^{⊗c} of M ≅ GL_2 × GL_1 over O, where S_i is the standard representation of GL_i. Lan–Suh [53, Def. 4.12] attach to it vector bundles W^can_µ ⊃ W^sub_µ on X, the canonical and subcanonical extensions of the automorphic bundle on Y.
items.note: The integral automorphic bundles W^can_µ ⊃ W^sub_µ attached to O-representations of the Siegel Levi M (Lan–Suh Def. 4.12, via the functor E_{M_1}) are planned nowhere. B2/B3 build automorphic bundles and their extensions over canonical models in characteristic 0. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 recorded the same gap (coherent-setup; lan-automorphic-bundle-hecke-iso, missing). External input: K.-W. Lan and J. Suh [53], Definition 4.12 (via the functor E_{M_1} of [52])

items.name: W^can_µ ≅ ω(a,b); ω(a,b) = W_{(a,b;−a−b)} for the natural Hecke action
items.statement: For µ = (a,b;c) ∈ X*(T)^+_M, W^can_µ ≅ ω(a,b) as vector bundles on X. The parameter c does not change the bundle; it changes the Hecke action on cohomology by a power of the similitude character. Proof: let L be the standard representation of G and L_0^∨(1) ⊂ L the span of the first two basis vectors, the M-representation of weight (1,0;0). Then L_0 = (L_0^∨(1))^∨(1) has weight (0,−1;1). By [52, Example 1.22], W_{(0,−1;1)} = E_{M_1}(L_0) = Lie_{A/Y} = E^∨ = ω(0,−1). Hence W^can_{(0,−1;1)} ≅ ω(0,−1) and ω(a,b) = (Sym^{a−b} ⊗ det^b)(ω(1,0)) = W_{(a,b;−a−b)}, for the natural Hecke action.
items.note: The comparison W^can_µ ≅ ω(a,b) needs Lan–Suh's functor, with E_{M_1}(L_0) = Lie_{A/Y} = E^∨ from [52, Ex. 1.22], and its compatibility with the Hecke twist by c. Both are missing. Checked on p. 823: W_{(0,−1;1)} ≅ ω(0,−1) and ω(a,b) = W_{(a,b;−a−b)}.

items.name: Theorem 5.1(1): vanishing above degree 2
items.statement: Let X be one of the toroidal compactifications of §5.2 (of Y_K, Y_{K_0(Q)} or Y_{K_1(Q)}), and k the residue field of O. If a ≥ 3 and 2 ≤ a − b ≤ p − 2, then H^i(X, ω(a,b)(−∞)_k) = 0 for all i > 2.
items.note: Mod-p vanishing for i > 2 when a ≥ 3 and 2 ≤ a−b ≤ p−2. It follows from Lan–Suh Cor. 7.24 with w̃_1: (W^∨)^sub = ω(β+2+t, −α+t)(−∞), per the p. 824 image; the text layer loses the sign. It depends on ext-lan-suh-vanishing, which is missing. The parameter ranges check out: β = 0, α = a−b−2, t = a−2.

items.name: Theorem 5.1(2): vanishing above degree 1
items.statement: With X and k as in Theorem 5.1: if a + b ≥ 6 and 2 ≤ a − b ≤ p − 2, then H^i(X, ω(a,b)(−∞)_k) = 0 for all i > 1.
items.note: Vanishing for i > 1 when a+b ≥ 6 and 2 ≤ a−b ≤ p−2, via w̃_2: ω(α+3+t, 1−β+t)(−∞). I checked that the stated range is exactly what the parametrization gives (t between max(1, b−1) and (a+b−4)/2). It depends on Lan–Suh, which is missing. The paper also uses this result in §1 (p. 803) and §1.2 (p. 804, 'the only point … we use j ≥ 4'). There the case is (a,b) = (j,2) with 4 ≤ j ≤ p: the subcanonical extension ω(j,2)^sub has cohomology only in degrees 0 and 1, and by dévissage the same holds with O/ϖ^n coefficients. It is applied again in §8.4, proof of Theorem 8.11 (p. 863), with (a,b) = (m+p, m+p+2−j) and m = (p^2−1)/2.

items.name: Theorem 5.1(3): vanishing in positive degree
items.statement: With X and k as in Theorem 5.1: if b ≥ 4 and 0 ≤ a − b ≤ p − 4, then H^i(X, ω(a,b)(−∞)_k) = 0 for all i > 0.
items.note: Vanishing for i > 0 when b ≥ 4 and 0 ≤ a−b ≤ p−4, via w̃_3: ω(α+3+t, β+3+t)(−∞). The parameter ranges check out. It depends on Lan–Suh, which is missing.

items.name: Complex uniformization of Y(C)
items.statement: Y(C) = G(Q)\(G(R)/K^h × G(A^∞)/U), where U ⊂ G(A^∞) is the open compact subgroup defining Y and K^h is the compact-mod-centre centralizer of h in G(R) (§2.2).
items.note: V1 plans the analytic double quotient G(Q)\(X × G(A^∞)/U), M3 compares the PEL moduli space with it, and A5 constructs the Siegel universal family. For GSp4 the ker^1 obstruction that M3 retains is trivial (Hasse principle for GSp), so Y(C) is a single Shimura variety. G(R)/K^h is the Siegel double half-space X^±. External input: Standard complex-analytic uniformization of Siegel modular varieties (no reference given)

items.name: Automorphic vector bundles V_σ over C and their extensions
items.statement: To a finite-dimensional C-representation (σ, V_σ) of K^h_C, [9, Def. 1.3.2] associates a vector bundle V_σ on Y(C). It has extensions V^sub_σ ⊂ V^can_σ to X(C), with V^can_σ = Ṽ_σ in [9] and V^sub_σ = V^can_σ(−∞). For a dominant µ ∈ X*(H_C)^+_{K^h_C}, V_µ denotes the bundle attached to the irreducible representation W_µ of highest weight µ.
items.note: BHR's V_σ is the descent of G(C) ×_{Q^−} V_σ from the compact dual at neat level (B0), compared with the algebraic bundle in B2. Its canonical and subcanonical extensions, with V^sub = V^can(−D), are B3; the reviewed B3 node covers them. Harris's and Milne's papers, which B0/B1 cite, are the sources; BHR [9] Def. 1.3.2 should be added. External input: D. Blasius, M. Harris and D. Ramakrishnan, Coherent cohomology, limits of discrete series, and Galois conjugation, Duke Math. J. 73 (1994) [9], Definition 1.3.2

items.name: Interior cohomology H̄^i and the limits H̃^i
items.statement: For i ≥ 0, H̄^i(X(C), V_σ) := Im(H^i(X(C), V^sub_σ) → H^i(X(C), V^can_σ)). H̃^i(V^sub_σ) and H̃^i(V^can_σ) are the direct limits over all levels K of H^i(X(C), V^sub_σ) and H^i(X(C), V^can_σ). H̄^i(X(C), V_σ), also written H̄^i(V_σ), is the corresponding limit of the H̄^i.
items.note: Interior coherent cohomology H̄^i (the image of H^i(V^sub) → H^i(V^can)) and its limits over all levels are planned nowhere. CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.7 defines completed interior cohomology only for Betti towers. The proof of Theorem 7.11 (§7.2, p. 854) recalls the definition at level X_0(Q), over K or C. There H̄^i(X_0(Q), ω(a,b)) is the image of H^i(X_0(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)) in H^i(X_0(Q), ω(a,b)).

items.name: L²- and cuspidal (Lie Q^−, K^h)-cohomology H^i_{(2),σ}, H^i_{cusp,σ}
items.statement: A_(2)(G) is the space of automorphic forms on G(Q)\G(A) square-integrable modulo Z_G(A), and A_0(G) ⊂ A_(2)(G) the cusp forms. For (σ, V_σ) as above and i ≥ 0: H^i_{(2),σ} := H^i(Lie Q^−, K^h; A_(2)(G) ⊗ V_σ) and H^i_{cusp,σ} := H^i(Lie Q^−, K^h; A_0(G) ⊗ V_σ). Here Q^− = K^h_C P^− ⊂ G(C) is the stabilizer of V^−, with Lie Q^− = k^h_C ⊕ p^− (§2.2).
items.note: AF.1 plans (g,K)-cohomology via Hom_K(∧^q(g/k), V), AS.4 the discrete L² spectrum, and AF.3 cusp forms. The (Lie Q^−, K^h)-cohomology of Harris/BHR, the '∂̄-cohomology' relative to the parabolic subalgebra k_C ⊕ p^−, is not planned. Source issue: the proof of Theorem 5.5 (p. 828) writes 'Lie P^−' for the 'Lie Q^−' of this definition.

items.name: Theorem 5.2 (Harris): comparison maps
items.statement: For (σ, V_σ) and i ≥ 0 there are canonical maps H^i_{cusp,σ} → H^i_{(2),σ}, H^i_{cusp,σ} → H̃^i(V^sub_σ), H^i_{(2),σ} → H̃^i(V^can_σ) and H̃^i(V^sub_σ) → H̃^i(V^can_σ). They form a commutative square.
items.note: Harris's comparison maps between cuspidal and L² (Lie Q^−, K^h)-cohomology and coherent cohomology of the canonical and subcanonical extensions (Harris 1990, Thm 2.7, Prop. 3.2.2) are planned nowhere. AS.5 is the Betti analogue only. External input: M. Harris, Automorphic forms and the cohomology of vector bundles on Shimura varieties (Ann Arbor 1988), Perspect. Math. 11 (1990) [37], Theorem 2.7 and Proposition 3.2.2

items.name: Theorem 5.2(1): cuspidal cohomology injects into interior cohomology
items.statement: The composite H^i_{cusp,σ} → H̃^i(V^sub_σ) → H̃^i(V^can_σ) lands in H̄^i(V_σ). The resulting map H^i_{cusp,σ} → H̄^i(V_σ) is injective for all i, and an isomorphism for i = 0 and i = 3.
items.note: This part says the map from cuspidal cohomology to interior coherent cohomology is injective, and bijective for i = 0, 3. It depends on Harris's theory, which is missing. External input: M. Harris [37], Theorem 2.7, Proposition 3.2.2

items.name: Theorem 5.2(2): L² cohomology surjects onto interior cohomology
items.statement: The image of H^i_{(2),σ} in H̃^i(V^can_σ) contains H̄^i(V_σ).
items.note: This part says the image of L² cohomology contains interior cohomology. It depends on Harris [37], which is missing. External input: M. Harris [37], Theorem 2.7, Proposition 3.2.2

items.name: Subspaces H̃^i(V^can_σ)_cusp and H̃^i(V^can_σ)_(2)
items.statement: For * ∈ {cusp, (2)}, H̃^i(V^can_σ)_* is the image of H^i_{*,σ} in H̃^i(V^can_σ). By Theorem 5.2, H^i_{cusp,σ} ≅ H̃^i(V^can_σ)_cusp ⊂ H̄^i(V_σ) ⊂ H̃^i(V^can_σ)_(2).
items.note: These are definitions of images inside H̃^i(V^can_σ). They depend on the missing Harris comparison and the interior cohomology item.

items.name: Tempered parts A_*(G)_temp, H^i_{*,σ,temp} and H^i(X(C), V^can_σ)_{*,temp}
items.statement: For * ∈ {cusp, (2)}, A_*(G) is semisimple as a G(A)-representation: A_*(G) = ⊕_π m_*(π) π^∞ ⊗ π_∞. A_*(G)_temp := ⊕ m_*(π) π^∞ ⊗ π_∞ over those π with π_∞ essentially tempered. H^i_{*,σ,temp} ⊂ H^i_{*,σ} is defined by replacing A_*(G) with A_*(G)_temp. H̃^i(V^can_σ)_{*,temp} ⊂ H̃^i(V^can_σ)_* is the image of H^i_{*,σ,temp} → H̃^i(V^can_σ). Taking K-invariants (K the level of X(C)) gives H^i(X(C), V^can_σ)_{*,temp} ⊂ H^i(X(C), V^can_σ)_*.
items.note: AS.4 plans the discrete-spectrum decomposition with finite multiplicities, and SR.3 plans temperedness only for p-adic groups. Essentially tempered archimedean components, the 'temp' parts of (Lie Q^−, K^h)-cohomology and their images in coherent cohomology are planned nowhere.

items.name: V_σ does not depend on the central parameter c
items.statement: Let (σ, V_σ) be the irreducible K^h_C-representation of highest weight (a,b;c) ∈ X*(H_C), and (τ, V_τ) the one of highest weight (a,b;c+2). Then τ = σ ⊗ ν, where ν is the similitude character, of weight (0,0;2). The automorphic vector bundles V_σ and V_τ on Y(C) are isomorphic. The map G(C) ×_{Q^−} V_σ → G(C) ×_{Q^−} V_τ, (g,w) ↦ (g, ν(g)^{−1}w), is well defined, but it is G(Q)-equivariant only up to the scalar ν(γ)^{−1}. Multiplying also by |ν(h^∞)|_{A^∞}^{−1} on the finite-adelic coordinate gives a G(Q)^+-equivariant, right-U-invariant isomorphism, which descends to Y(C) = G(Q)^+\(X^+ × G(A^∞)/U). Equivalently, the line bundle attached to ν is trivial. The Hecke actions on cohomology differ by a twist by a power of the similitude character.
items.note: B0 plans descent through the ineffective centre, not this twist. Source issue (p. 826; affects nothing): the displayed map (g,w) ↦ (g, ν(g)^{-1}w) is equivariant for G(Q) only up to the character ν(γ)^{-1}, since φ(γg,w) = ν(γ)^{-1}·γφ(g,w). So it is not an isomorphism of G(Q)-equivariant bundles as claimed. On Y(C) = G(Q)\(X × G(A^∞)/U) it can be corrected by the scalar s(x,h) = sign(ν(g_∞))‖ν(h)‖^{-1}, which satisfies s(γx,γh) = ν(γ)s(x,h). That factor is exactly the |ν|-twist of the Hecke action the paper mentions, so the conclusion V_σ ≅ V_τ stands. I checked this on the page image.

items.name: Definition 5.3: W_µ and W^sub_µ
items.statement: For µ = (a,b;c) ∈ X*(T)^+_M, W_µ := W^can_µ (the Lan–Suh canonical extension) and W^sub_µ := W_µ(−∞). As vector bundles over X, W_µ ≅ ω(a,b); the Hecke action on the cohomology of W_µ depends on c.
items.note: W_µ := W^can_µ and W^sub_µ := W_µ(−∞) are Lan–Suh's integral bundles, which carry the c-dependent Hecke action. They depend on lan-suh-automorphic-bundles, which is missing. As bundles, W_µ ≅ ω(a,b), and ω(a,b) itself is planned. §7.1 (p. 847) recalls the notation for μ = (a,b): W_μ = ω(a,b) and W^sub_μ = ω(a,b)(−∞). It also sets W^sub_{μ,M} := W^sub_μ ⊗_O M for an O-module M (k, O/ϖ^n, K/O or K). The same notation is used on X_0(Q), X_1(Q), X_Δ(Q) and on the nonordinary loci. As bundles, W_μ = ω(a,b) and its subcanonical twist are planned (AutomorphicBundles:B3, B4; ShimuraCompactifications:C5). Only Lan–Suh's W^can_µ, with its c-dependent Hecke action, is missing.

items.name: De Rham homology sequence in terms of automorphic bundles (Lan–Suh, Milne)
items.statement: (i) [52, Example 1.22], with the Poincaré pairing H^dR_1(A/Y) ⊗ H^dR_1(A/Y) → O_Y(1) of [52, §1.2]. The Hodge sequence 0 → Lie^∨_{A^∨/Y} → H^dR_1(A/Y) → Lie_{A/Y} → 0 is 0 → W_{(1,0;0)} → H^dR_1(A/Y) → W_{(0,−1;1)} → 0, and O_Y(1) = W_{(0,0;1)}. (ii) [54, Example III.2.4], with base point o = h(i) = J ∈ X̌. Over Y(C) the sequence is 0 → V_{(0,−1;1)} → H^dR_1(A/Y) → V_{(1,0;1)} → 0 and O_Y(1) ≅ V_{(0,0;2)}. Here the isotropic subspace corresponds to V^−, V/W to V^+, V^− = W_{(0,−1;1)} and V^+ = W_{(1,0;1)} as K^h_C-representations, and the similitude has weight (0,0;2).
items.note: Part (i) is the integral Lan–Suh translation of the Hodge sequence 0 → Lie^∨_{A^∨} → H^dR_1 → Lie_A → 0 into W-bundles, with O_Y(1) = W_{(0,0;1)}. It is missing, like all integral Lan–Suh bundles. Part (ii) is Milne's characteristic-0 identification. It is covered in substance by B2 (the de Rham bundle of a G-representation with its Hodge filtration) and B4 (the Siegel Hodge bundle), but the weight bookkeeping V_{(0,−1;1)}, V_{(1,0;1)}, V_{(0,0;2)} is not named. Because (i) is missing, the item is missing. External input: K.-W. Lan and J. Suh [52], Example 1.22 and §1.2; J. S. Milne, Canonical models of (mixed) Shimura varieties and automorphic vector bundles (1990) [54], Example III.2.4 (H_dR there is de Rham homology, [54, §I.3])

items.name: Lemma 5.4: comparison W_{(a,b;c)} ≅ V_{(−b,−a;a+b+2c)}
items.statement: Let µ = (a,b;c) ∈ X*(T)^+_M. Over X(C), W_{(a,b;c)} ≅ V_{(−b,−a;a+b+2c)}, compatibly with the Hecke actions on cohomology.
items.note: The comparison W_{(a,b;c)} ≅ V_{(−b,−a;a+b+2c)} over X(C), with Hecke compatibility, needs the analytification of Lan–Suh's integral bundles compared with the BHR/Milne bundles. It is planned nowhere. I checked the formula on the p. 827 image.

items.name: Harish-Chandra parameterization of (limits of) discrete series of GSp_4(R)
items.statement: Discrete series and limits of discrete series of G(R) are written π(λ, C), with C ∈ {C_0, …, C_3} a Weyl chamber and λ ∈ C ∩ (X*(H_C) + ρ) (ρ = (2,1;0), the half-sum of Φ^+). The contragredient is π(λ, C)^* = π(−w_0(λ), −w_0(C)).
items.locator: §5.3, proof of Theorem 5.5, p. 828; Theorem 5.6(3), p. 829
items.note: Harish-Chandra's parameterization π(λ, C) of (limits of) discrete series of GSp4(R), and the contragredient formula, are planned nowhere. AF.1 plans only (g,K)-module foundations. ET.1 plans discrete-series pseudocoefficients 'in the unitary cases used below'. External input: Harish-Chandra's classification of (limits of) discrete series, in the conventions of Blasius–Harris–Ramakrishnan [9, §2.4] (no separate reference given)

items.name: Mirković: tempered representations with (Lie Q^−, K^h)-cohomology are (limits of) discrete series
items.statement: Harris [37, Theorem 3.5], as used (a result often credited to Mirković; the paper names no such source). Let π = π^∞ ⊗ π_∞ occur in A_(2)(G)_temp, so π_∞ is essentially tempered, and suppose H^i(Lie Q^−, K^h; π_∞ ⊗ V_σ) ≠ 0 for some i. Then π_∞ is a discrete series or a limit of discrete series representation.
items.locator: §5.3, proof of Theorem 5.5, p. 828 (cited as [37, Theorem 3.5]); reused in Theorem 5.6(3), p. 829
items.note: Mirković's theorem, as quoted in Harris [37, Thm 3.5], says a tempered π_∞ with nonzero (Lie Q^−, K^h)-cohomology is a (limit of) discrete series. It is planned nowhere. It is the coherent analogue of the Borel–Wallach degree statement, which PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 routed to AF.1/AF.4. External input: M. Harris [37], Theorem 3.5 (a theorem of Mirković, named in arXiv:1907.08691v1)

items.name: Blasius–Harris–Ramakrishnan: (Lie Q^−, K^h)-cohomology of (limits of) discrete series
items.statement: [9, Theorem 3.2.1], as used. Let σ ∈ X*(H_C)^+_{K^h_C} with central coordinate σ_0, and let π_∞ = π(λ, C)^* be a (limit of) discrete series with H^i(Lie Q^−, K^h; π_∞ ⊗ V_σ) ≠ 0. Then λ = ((σ+ρ)|_{Sp_4(R)}; −σ_0) and i = #(Φ(C)^+ ∩ Φ^+_n). Moreover any π_∞ with such nonvanishing cohomology has infinitesimal character χ_{((−σ−ρ)|_{Sp_4(R)}; σ_0)}.
items.note: BHR Thm 3.2.1 computes the (Lie Q^−, K^h)-cohomology of (limits of) discrete series: the parameter λ, the single degree i = #(Φ(C)^+ ∩ Φ_n^+), and the infinitesimal character. It is planned nowhere. External input: D. Blasius, M. Harris and D. Ramakrishnan [9], Theorem 3.2.1

items.name: Theorem 5.5: vanishing of tempered L² coherent cohomology outside the chamber degrees
items.statement: Let µ = (a,b;c) ∈ X*(T)^+_M. Then H^i(X(C), W_µ)_{(2),temp} = 0 for every 0 ≤ i ≤ 3 such that (a−1, b−2; c) ∉ C_i.
items.note: H^i(X(C), W_µ)_{(2),temp} = 0 unless (a−1, b−2) ∈ C_i. The proof combines Harris, Mirković and BHR, all missing. I checked the page image: λ = (2−b, 1−a; −a−b−2c) and w_0(λ) = (a−1, b−2; ·). The statement's 'µ = (a−1, b−2; c) ∉ C_i' misuses the letter µ.

items.name: Infinitesimal character of the transfer of π_∞ to GL_4(R)
items.statement: As used: if π_∞ has infinitesimal character with parameter (λ_1, λ_2; λ_0) (λ_0 the central coordinate), its transfer π̃_∞ to GL_4(R), via the spin representation of the dual group GSp_4, has infinitesimal character χ_τ with τ = ((λ_1+λ_2+λ_0)/2, (λ_1−λ_2+λ_0)/2, (−λ_1+λ_2+λ_0)/2, (−λ_1−λ_2+λ_0)/2).
items.note: This is the infinitesimal character of the transfer of π_∞ from GSp4(R) to GL4(R) through the spin representation (Sorensen §2.1.2). Archimedean local Langlands for GSp4(R) and the GSp4 → GL4 transfer are planned nowhere. ML.4 only registers 'Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs'. External input: C. M. Sorensen, Galois representations attached to Hilbert–Siegel modular forms, Doc. Math. 15 (2010) [64], §2.1.2

items.name: Theorem 5.6(1): infinitesimal character of π_∞
items.statement: Let µ = (a,b;c) ∈ X*(T)^+_M, w := −(a+b+2c) and σ := (−b,−a; a+b+2c) = (−b,−a;−w) ∈ X*(H_C). Suppose π = π^∞ ⊗ π_∞ in A_(2)(G) contributes to H^i(X(C), W_µ)_(2) ≅ H^i(X(C), V_σ)_(2). Then, under the Harish-Chandra isomorphism, the infinitesimal character of π_∞ is χ_{((−σ−ρ)|_{Sp_4(R)}; −w)} = χ_{(a−1, b−2; −w)}.
items.note: This part says the infinitesimal character of π_∞ is χ_{(a−1, b−2; −w)}. It follows from BHR Thm 3.2.1, which is missing.

items.name: Theorem 5.6(2): infinitesimal character of the transfer to GL_4(R)
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 5.6, let π̃_∞ be the transfer of π_∞ to GL_4(R). Its infinitesimal character is χ_τ, τ = ((a+b−3−w)/2, (a−b+1−w)/2, (−a+b−1−w)/2, (−a−b+3−w)/2).
items.note: This part gives the infinitesimal character of the GL4(R) transfer. It depends on ext-sorensen-transfer-infinitesimal-character, which is missing.

items.name: Theorem 5.6(3): tempered contributors are (limits of) discrete series with explicit parameter
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 5.6, if moreover π_∞ is tempered, then π_∞ is a discrete series or limit of discrete series representation, and π_∞ ≅ π((a−1, b−2; −w), C_i) in the Harish-Chandra parameterization (i the cohomological degree).
items.note: This part says tempered contributors are (limits of) discrete series π((a−1, b−2; −w), C_i). It is established in the proof of Theorem 5.5 and depends on Harris, Mirković and BHR, all missing.

items.name: Definition 5.7: discrete series (regular) and limit of discrete series (nonregular) weights
items.statement: A weight µ = (a,b;c) ∈ X*(T)^+_M is a discrete series weight (regular weight) if (a−1, b−2; c) lies in the interior of a unique Weyl chamber C_i. It is a limit of discrete series weight (nonregular weight) if µ − w_0(ρ) lies in the intersection of exactly two of the chambers C_i.
items.note: Regular (discrete series) versus nonregular (limit of discrete series) weights for GSp4 are planned nowhere. This is the analogue of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18's 'Coherent' context (places where π_v is a non-degenerate limit of discrete series), which it routed to AF.1/AF.4. The two conditions agree because µ − w_0(ρ) = (a−1, b−2; c).

items.name: The three families of limit of discrete series weights
items.statement: The limit of discrete series weights are exactly: (1) µ = (a, 2; c) with a ∈ Z_{≥2} (shift (a−1, 0) ∈ C_0 ∩ C_1); (2) µ = (a, 3−a; c) with a ∈ Z_{≥2} (shift ∈ C_1 ∩ C_2); (3) µ = (1, b; c) with b ∈ Z_{≤1} (shift ∈ C_2 ∩ C_3).
items.note: The three families (a,2) with a ≥ 2, (a, 3−a) with a ≥ 2, and (1,b) with b ≤ 1 are correct. I checked them from the chamber inequalities (for example, C_0 ∩ C_1 forces b = 2, and a ≥ 2 excludes the origin). They depend on the chamber and weight items, which are missing.

items.name: Canonical bundle of the toroidal Siegel threefold: det Ω^1_{X/O} ≅ ω(3,3)(−∞)
items.statement: On a smooth toroidal compactification X of the Siegel threefold over O, det Ω^1_{X/O} ≅ ω(3,3)(−∞) = ω^3(−∞). This follows from the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism Ω^1_{X/O}(log D) ≅ Sym^2 E = ω(2,0), D the boundary.
items.locator: §5.3, p. 830 and proof of Corollary 5.8, p. 831
items.note: The Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism Ω^1_{X/O}(log D) ≅ Sym^2 E on integral PEL toroidal compactifications, and its consequence det Ω^1 ≅ ω^3(−∞), are not planned for Siegel/PEL varieties. The atlas mentions Kodaira–Spencer only in C4, in dimension one. The modular-curve version is R15.1, per the CG18 extraction. Lan [51] Thm 6.4.1.1 and Faltings–Chai are the standard sources. §7.2 (p. 851) states the same fact for X_Δ(Q): 'ω^3(−∞) is the dualizing sheaf on X_Δ(Q)'. External input: Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism for toroidal compactifications (Faltings–Chai; Lan [51]); used without citation

items.name: Serre duality for ω(a,b) on X
items.statement: For 0 ≤ a−b ≤ p−1 (no restriction in characteristic 0): ω(a,b)^∨ ≅ ω(−b,−a) and det Ω^1_{X/O} ≅ ω(3,3)(−∞), so ω(a,b)^∨ ⊗ det Ω^1_{X/O} ≅ ω(3−b, 3−a)(−∞). Hence, by Serre duality on the smooth proper threefold X_k, for 0 ≤ a−b ≤ p−1, H^i(X, ω(a,b)_k) is dual to H^{3−i}(X, ω(3−b,3−a)(−∞)_k). For a−b ≥ p, ω(a,b)^∨ = Γ^{a−b}(E^∨) ⊗ det^{−b}E instead. Under ω(a,b) ↦ ω(3−b,3−a), which interchanges the canonical and subcanonical extensions, the limit of discrete series families (a,2) and (1,b) are interchanged and the family (a,3−a) is stable.
items.note: Serre duality on smooth proper threefolds over k is not planned: coherent duality is planned only for curves (Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer B, SF.3). PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 routed its general-dimension duality to A0-extension. Caveat for a formalisation over O or k (the remark on p. 830 is made in characteristic 0, where it holds as printed): integrally, (Sym^n E)^∨ ≅ Γ^n(E^∨) (divided powers), so ω(a,b)^∨ ≅ ω(−b,−a) needs a−b < p (or characteristic 0). Corollary 5.8(2) uses a−b = 2a−3 ≤ p−2, which is within that range. The displays on pp. 830–831 are correct on the images: ω(a,3−a)^∨ ⊗ det Ω^1 = ω(a−3, −a) ⊗ ω(3,3)(−∞) = ω(a, 3−a)(−∞). The proof of Theorem 8.11 (§8.4, p. 863) uses the same duality with coefficients in k = O/ϖ. There H^1(X, ω(j,2) ⊗ ω^{−m−(p−1)}) is dual to H^2(X, ω(m+p, m+p+2−j)(−∞)), which then vanishes by Theorem 5.1. Here a−b = j−2 < p, which is within the range where ω(a,b)^∨ ≅ ω(−b,−a).

items.name: Characteristic-0 vanishing for limit of discrete series weights
items.statement: For all a ≥ 2: H^i(X(C), ω(a,2))_{(2),temp} = 0 for i = 2, 3, and H^i(X(C), ω(a,3−a))_{(2),temp} = 0 for i = 0, 3. The Hecke action on ω(a,b) is to be normalized as in §5.5 before taking (2)/temp parts.
items.note: For weights (a,2), the (2),temp parts vanish in degrees 2 and 3; for weights (a, 3−a), in degrees 0 and 3. This is a direct consequence of Theorem 5.5, which is missing, after the §5.5 Hecke normalization.

items.name: Corollary 5.8(1): mod-p vanishing of H^2, H^3 for weight (a,2)
items.note: This follows from Theorem 5.1(2): a+b ≥ 6 and 2 ≤ a−2 ≤ p−2 give 4 ≤ a ≤ p, with vanishing for i > 1. It depends on Lan–Suh, which is missing.

items.name: Corollary 5.8(2): mod-p vanishing of H^0 and H^3 for weight (a, 3−a)
items.note: H^3 vanishing is Theorem 5.1(1) with a−b = 2a−3 ∈ [2, p−2]. H^0 vanishing then follows by Serre duality and Kodaira–Spencer. All three inputs are missing.

items.name: Deligne–Serre: weight-one eigenforms have finite-image (Artin) Galois representations
items.statement: A characteristic-0 weight-one Hecke eigenform (cuspidal, non-Eisenstein) has an associated Galois representation ρ : G_Q → GL_2(C) with finite image. Consequently, a mod-p weight-one eigenclass whose Galois representation r̄ has image containing SL_2(k') with #k' > 5, or a class new at x with r̄|_{I_x} unipotent of rank 2, does not lift to characteristic 0 (at minimal level in the second case).
items.note: The Deligne–Serre finite-image representation of weight-one eigenforms is planned in R19.1 and organized in ML.1. The non-liftability consequences in §5.4 (a heuristic discussion, not used later) also need Klein's classification of finite subgroups of PGL2(C), which is planned nowhere (atlas search for icosahedral / finite subgroups of PGL: no hits). That deduction would go to R19.1 if a formaliser wants it. External input: P. Deligne and J.-P. Serre, Formes modulaires de poids 1, Ann. Sci. ÉNS (4) 7 (1974) [23]

items.name: Grothendieck: inertia on a semistable abelian variety satisfies (σ−1)^2 = 0
items.statement: If an abelian variety has semistable reduction at x, then inertia at x acts on its ℓ-adic Tate module (ℓ ≠ x) unipotently with (σ − 1)^2 = 0 ('rank 2 unipotent').
items.note: This is Grothendieck's monodromy criterion (SGA 7 IX): semistable reduction holds exactly when inertia acts unipotently with (σ−1)^2 = 0 on V_ℓ. R11.3 plans it. External input: A. Grothendieck, SGA 7 I, Exposé IX [36]

items.name: Conjecture (heuristic, not used): weight-(2,2) Siegel eigenforms come from abelian varieties
items.statement: Conjecturally, Siegel modular eigenforms of weight (2,2) should be associated to abelian varieties M/Q of dimension 2n with an injection E → End_Q(M) ⊗ Q for some totally real field E of degree n. Suggested consequence: a modular r̄ of type U3 at some x should not admit minimal lifts to characteristic 0 in weight (2,2).
items.note: This is a heuristic conjecture (weight-(2,2) Siegel eigenforms ↔ abelian varieties of dimension 2n with real multiplication by a degree-n totally real field). It is not used in any proof. No layer registers it.

items.name: Exceptional isomorphism S_6 ≅ GSp_4(F_2)
items.statement: There is an isomorphism S_6 ≅ GSp_4(F_2) = Sp_4(F_2). It arises from the Galois group of A_2[2] over A_2, identified either with the symmetries of the 2-torsion of the universal abelian surface or with the action of S_6 on the (generically) six Weierstrass points of a genus-2 curve.
items.note: S6 ≅ Sp4(F2), via the 6 Weierstrass points of a genus-2 curve and J[2] = even subsets modulo complement, is planned nowhere and is in neither library. Tau Ceti SpinRepresentations Layer 6 plans only Spin5 ≅ Sp4 over C. It is used only in the illustrative example of §5.4. External input: J. Bergström, C. Faber and G. van der Geer, Siegel modular forms of genus 2 and level 2, IMRN 2008 [8]

items.name: Example: conjectural nonliftable mod-2 torsion class of weight (2,2) from a genus-2 Jacobian
items.statement: General recipe: if K/Q is a sextic field whose Galois closure has group G ⊂ S_6 containing an element of type (1,2,3,4)(5,6) and acting irreducibly on F_2^4, and p is an odd prime with p = 𝔭^4𝔮^2, then r̄ : Gal ↠ G ⊂ S_6 ≅ GSp_4(F_2) should give a type-U3 representation. Explicit example: let A = Jac(C), C : y² = x^5 − 2x^4 + 6x^3 − 8x^2 + 4x − 4, with good reduction outside 3·5·19. Claims: (i) r̄ : G_Q → GSp_4(F_2) has image S_5 ⊂ S_6. (ii) Inertia at 5 is conjugate to (1,2,3,4)(5,6); the correct class is (1,2,3,4) [printed (1,2,3,4)(5,6); sourceIssues E46, E44]. (iii) r̄ should give a mod-2 torsion class with trivial level outside 3·5·19, Iwahori level at 5 and paramodular level at 3 and 19. (iv) It should lift to characteristic 0 at some nonminimal level if A is modular (conductor of A = 3·5^3·19).
items.note: This is a conjectural illustrative example; nothing plans it. I verified by computation, with J[2] modelled as the even subsets of the 6 Weierstrass points modulo complement, that both S6 classes (1234) and (1234)(56) act as a single Jordan block of size 4: the images of (σ−1), (σ−1)², (σ−1)³ have F2-ranks 3, 2, 1. So the pp. 831–832 claim that the unipotent σ with (σ−1)² ≠ 0 'has conjugacy class (1,2,3,4)(5,6)' is incomplete (E44). The outer automorphism does fix both classes: order-4 elements of the transitive S5 ≅ PGL2(F5) have cycle type 4+1+1. In the Weierstrass model the image lies in the point stabilizer S5, so inertia at 5 must be of type (1234), as the item's correction (E46) says. This was checked by direct computation.

items.name: Theorem 5.9 (Buzzard): weight-(2,2) cusp forms are never Steinberg
items.statement: If π is a cuspidal automorphic representation associated to a Siegel modular form of weight (2,2), then π_x is not the Steinberg representation for any prime x [printed 'for any p'; sourceIssues E47].
items.note: Buzzard's argument needs several inputs, none planned: Galois representations for GSp4, local–global compatibility at x (Steinberg Weil–Deligne eigenvalues x^{(w±3)/2}, x^{(w±1)/2}), the U_{x,1}-eigenvalue on Iwahori-fixed vectors, and integrality of Hecke eigenvalues from q-expansions. AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII plans polarized and unitary GL_n only. Misprint (E47): 'for any p' should read 'for any prime x'.

items.name: Notation X, X_i(Q) and Hecke matrices β_{x,0}, β_{x,1}, β_{x,2}
items.statement: In §5.5, X := X_K and X_i(Q) := X_{K_i(Q)}, and M is an O-module. For a rational prime x: β_{x,0} = diag(x,x,x,x), β_{x,1} = diag(1,1,x,x), β_{x,2} = diag(1,x,x,x^2), regarded as elements of GSp_4(Q_x).
items.note: The GSp4 elements β_{x,0}, β_{x,1}, β_{x,2} generating the unramified double cosets are not named. SR.1 and SR.4 plan double-coset Hecke algebras and Satake generically, and IHG.3 fixes the GL_n normalization only ('Do not assert this GL_n polynomial for a general reductive group').

items.name: Hecke operators T_{x,i} and S_x on coherent cohomology
items.statement: For x ∉ S and j ∈ {0,1,2}, T_{x,j} := [Kβ_{x,j}K] acting on H^n(X, ω(a,b)_M). For x ∉ S ∪ Q, i ∈ {0,1} and j ∈ {0,1,2}, T_{x,j} := [K_i(Q)β_{x,j}K_i(Q)] acting on H^n(X_i(Q), ω(a,b)_M). These are defined as in [63, §1.1.6] or [68, §8], which applies when x ≠ p or when p is invertible on M. S_x := T_{x,0}. At x = p only T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2} are constructed, in degree 0 over K/O (Lemma 8.8).
items.note: B5 plans Hecke pullback, coefficient identification and trace, in characteristic 0 on canonical models. Its acceptance test compares 'a nonscalar Siegel representation'. Hecke operators on H^n(X, ω(a,b)_M) for n > 0 and torsion M over the integral models (Skinner–Urban §1.1.6, Tilouine §8) are planned nowhere. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 marked the same gap missing (coherent-hecke-operator-T-gamma, lan-automorphic-bundle-hecke-iso) and routed it to its proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes Part II. External input: C. Skinner and E. Urban, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 5 (2006) [63], §1.1.6; J. Tilouine, Formes compagnons et complexe BGG dual pour GSp_4, Ann. Inst. Fourier 62 (2012) [68], §8

items.name: Hecke operators at p: T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2}
items.statement: On H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)_{K/O}) (degree n = 0, M = K/O; Q = ∅ gives X), there are operators T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2} := (pT_{p,2} + (p+p³)S_p)p^{2−b}. They commute with the other Hecke operators and act on q-expansions by the formulas of Lemmas 8.3–8.4 (Lemma 8.8). They are therefore also defined on the subspace H^0(X_0(Q), …). The correspondence definition does not apply directly at x = p.
items.locator: §5.5, p. 833 (Q_2 defined p. 859, start of §8.4; existence Lemma 8.8, p. 860)
items.note: The existence of T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2} = (pT_{p,2} + (p+p³)S_p)p^{2−b} on H^0(X, ω(a,b)_{K/O}) at x = p is proved in Lemma 8.8 (§8). It is planned nowhere. §8.4 (p. 859) restates the operator as Q2 = (pT2 + (p+p³)S)p^{2−k} in weight (j,k), where k is the second weight index. The operator p^{k−2}Q2 = pT2 + (p+p³)S is the one whose eigenvalue should be the X²-coefficient of the characteristic polynomial of crystalline Frobenius (§8.5, p. 863; see hecke-polynomial-crystalline-frobenius-at-p).

items.name: Operators U_{x,i} at the auxiliary primes x ∈ Q
items.statement: For x ∈ Q, i ∈ {0,1} and j ∈ {0,1,2}, U_{x,j} := [K_i(Q)β_{x,j}K_i(Q)] acting on H^n(X_i(Q), ω(a,b)_M).
items.note: These are the operators U_{x,i} = [K_i(Q)β_{x,i}K_i(Q)] at the Klingen-level auxiliary primes, on integral coherent cohomology. The same gap applies as for T_{x,i}; PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18's hecke-U-x-coherent was also missing.

items.name: Diamond operators ⟨u⟩, u ∈ Δ_Q
items.statement: The Galois group Δ_Q = ∏_{x∈Q}(Z/x)^× of the finite étale cover X_1(Q) → X_0(Q) acts on H^n(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)_M). For u ∈ Δ_Q the corresponding operator is denoted ⟨u⟩.
items.note: The action of Δ_Q on H^n(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)_M) comes from functoriality along the deck transformations of X_{K_1(Q)} → X_{K_0(Q)}, which is itself missing. It is named nowhere for Siegel threefolds. CG18's modular-curve diamond operators counted as planned only because modular-curve owners exist (R14.1, R15.2).

items.name: Formal operators U_{p,1}, U_{p,2} on q-expansions
items.statement: U_{p,1} and U_{p,2} are formal operators on q-expansions (classically, Hecke operators with level structure at p), explicitly defined in Lemmas 8.3 and 8.4. Claimed key property: T_{p,1} and T_{p,2}/p^{k+j−6} act by U_{p,1} and U_{p,2} for large enough weights, including (j,k) plus any nontrivial multiple of (p−1, p−1), j ≥ k ≥ 2.
items.note: U_{p,1} and U_{p,2} on q-expansions (Lemmas 8.3–8.4), with the claim that T_{p,1} and T_{p,2}/p^{k+j−6} act by them in large weight, are planned nowhere. B5 plans only the generic q-expansion and Fourier–Jacobi expansions.

items.name: Remark 5.10: normalization of the Hecke action; ω(a,b) ≅ W_{(a,b;3−a−b)} ≅ V_{(−b,−a;6−a−b)}
items.statement: The paper's Hecke action is the natural one twisted by ν^{−3} (see [63, §1.1.6(a)]). For the natural action, ω(a,b) ≅ W_{(a,b;−a−b)} and over C ω(a,b) ≅ V_{(−b,−a;−a−b)}. For the paper's normalization, ω(a,b) ≅ W_µ and over C ω(a,b) ≅ V_σ, with µ = (a,b; 3−a−b) and σ = (−b,−a; 6−a−b).
items.note: This is the paper's normalization of the Hecke action on ω(a,b), twisted by ν^{-3}, giving ω(a,b) ≅ W_{(a,b;3−a−b)} and ≅ V_{(−b,−a;6−a−b)}. It depends on the missing Lan–Suh/BHR comparison and integral Hecke operators.

items.name: Remark 5.11: identifying Z^{2,+} with weights in X*(T)^+_M
items.statement: Z^{2,+} := {(a,b) ∈ Z² : a ≥ b} is identified with the subset {(a, b; 3−a−b)} of X*(T)^+_M. So one writes µ = (a,b) ∈ X*(T)^+_M.
items.note: This is a notational convention: (a,b) ↦ (a, b; 3−a−b). It is tied to Remark 5.10 and is used throughout §§6–8.

items.name: Remark 5.12: central character and GL_4 infinitesimal character in normalized weight (a,b)
items.statement: Let µ = (a,b) ∈ X*(T)^+_M and w := a+b−6. The Hecke operator [K diag(x,x,x,x) K] acts on the cohomology of ω(a,b) as x^w = x^{a+b−6}. If π = π^∞ ⊗ π_∞ in A_(2)(G) contributes to H^i(X(C), ω(a,b))_(2) ≅ H^i(X(C), W_µ)_(2) ≅ H^i(X(C), V_σ)_(2), σ = (−b,−a;−w), then the central character of π_∞ is x ↦ x^{−w}. By Theorem 5.6, the transfer of π_∞ to GL_4(R) has infinitesimal character χ_τ, τ = (0, −(b−2), −(a−1), −(a+b−3)) + (3/2)(1,1,1,1).
items.note: The central-character and GL4 infinitesimal-character bookkeeping, with w = a+b−6, depends on Theorem 5.6, which is missing. Misprint (E49): 'by Proposition 5.6' should be Theorem 5.6. The remark is stated for any integer x, so x = p is allowed. At x = p it says that S = S_p = [K diag(p,p,p,p) K] acts by p^{j+k−6} in weight (j,k). This uses the ν^{−3}-twisted normalization of the Hecke action (Remark 5.10) and trivial Nebentypus (Remark 8.2). This case is used in §8.5, proof of Lemma 8.12 (p. 864). It matches the constant term p^6 S_p^2 = p^{2j+2k−6} of the Hecke polynomial at p.

items.name: Definition 5.13(1): anemic Hecke algebra T^an_µ(Q)
items.statement: Let µ = (a,b) ∈ X*(T)^+_M with a ≥ b ≥ 2. T^an_µ(Q) ⊂ End_O(H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_{K/O})) is the O-algebra generated by the T_{x,i} for x ∉ S ∪ Q ∪ {p}.
items.note: This is the Hecke algebra generated by T_{x,i} on H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_{K/O}). It depends on the missing Siegel coherent Hecke operators. The analogue in PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 (T-empty-with-L-sigma) was also missing and went with its R = T Part II.

items.name: Definition 5.13(2): Hecke algebra T_µ(Q) and T_µ
items.statement: T_µ(Q) is the O-algebra generated over T^an_µ(Q) by the U_{x,i} for x ∈ Q and the ⟨u⟩ for u ∈ Δ_Q, acting on H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_{K/O}). When Q = ∅, T^an_µ(∅) = T_µ(∅) =: T_µ.
items.note: This algebra adds U_{x,i} and ⟨u⟩ to the anemic algebra. It depends on items that are missing.

items.name: Definition 5.13(3): Hecke algebra T̃_µ(Q) with operators at p
items.statement: T̃_µ(Q) is the T_µ(Q)-algebra generated by T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2} = (pT_{p,2} + (p+p^3)S_p)p^{2−b} (these exist by Lemma 8.8). T̃_µ := T̃_µ(∅).
items.note: This algebra adds T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2} (Lemma 8.8). It depends on items that are missing. T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2} exist on H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)_{K/O}) by Lemma 8.8 (p. 860). Here μ = (a,b) is read as (a,b;3−a−b) (Remark 5.11). Parts (1)–(2) of Definition 5.13 are def-5-13-1-anemic-hecke-algebra and def-5-13-2-hecke-algebra-T-mu-Q. The sentence saying these algebras preserve the X_0(Q)-subspace is hecke-algebras-preserve-X0Q-subspace.

items.name: The Hecke algebras preserve the X_0(Q) subspace
items.statement: The algebras T^an_µ(Q) ⊂ T_µ(Q) ⊂ T̃_µ(Q) preserve the subspace H^0(X_0(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_{K/O}) ⊂ H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_{K/O}).
items.note: The claim is that the Hecke algebras preserve the X_0(Q) subspace, H^0 pulled back from X_0(Q) inside H^0(X_1(Q)). It depends on the missing operators and on the Δ_Q-cover.

items.name: Ordinary idempotent e and ordinary part H^0(…)^ord
items.statement: e := lim_{n→∞} (T_{p,1}Q_{p,2})^{n!} is the ordinary idempotent of T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2}, considered only where the limit makes sense. For M = O, O/ϖ^m or K/O, H^0(X_0(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_M)^ord := e H^0(X_0(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_M). Then H^0(X_0(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_M) = H^0(…)^ord_M ⊕ (1−e) H^0(…)_M.
items.note: The construction e = lim (T_{p,1}Q_{p,2})^{n!} and the decomposition M = eM ⊕ (1−e)M are exactly L0a's group-independent projector. That covers finite modules (M = O/ϖ^m, where H^0 of a coherent sheaf on a proper scheme is finite) and inverse limits (M = O). K/O is the union of its finite ϖ^m-torsion submodules, each U-stable. The operators T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2} are missing (hecke-operators-T-p1-Q-p2). CG18's lemma-7-3 used L0a in the same way. A duplicate of this statement (p. 835) has been merged into this item. The paper writes the limit as lim_{→n} and calls it a direct limit; an ordinary limit is meant (E50). For M = O/ϖ^m the decomposition is the Fitting decomposition for U = T_{p,1}Q_{p,2} on a finite-length module. That is Mathlib's LinearMap.eventually_isCompl_ker_pow_range_pow (Mathlib/RingTheory/Artinian/Module.lean).

items.name: Definition 5.14: ordinary Hecke algebras T^an_μ(Q)^ord, T_μ(Q)^ord, T̃_μ(Q)^ord
items.statement: Let μ = (a,b) with a ≥ b ≥ 2. The ordinary Hecke algebras T^an_μ(Q)^ord (resp. T_μ(Q)^ord, T̃_μ(Q)^ord) are the images of T^an_μ(Q) (resp. T_μ(Q), T̃_μ(Q)) in End_O(H^0(X_0(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_{K/O})^{ord}). For Q = ∅ these are written T^{an,ord}_μ = T^ord_μ, etc.
items.note: The images of the missing Siegel Hecke algebras in End_O of the ordinary part. PadicFamilies:L0 plans ordinary Hecke algebras only for modular forms ('Construct p-adic modular forms from the ordinary tower …'). OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.1 applies projectors only to 'the modular/Hilbert/quaternionic Hecke complexes'. A second copy of Definition 5.14 (p. 835), with the same content, has been merged into this item.

items.name: Definition 6.1: the Hasse invariant h and a lift A of h^r
items.statement: Let h ∈ H^0(X, ω_k^{p−1}) be the Hasse invariant of the special fibre of X = X_K; here ω = det E, E = π_*Ω^1_{A/X}, and X is a toroidal compactification over O as in §5.2. Fix, for the rest of §6, an integer r > 0 and a section A ∈ H^0(X, ω^{r(p−1)}) (over O) lifting h^r. Such r and A exist by the Koecher principle and the ampleness of ω on the minimal compactification of X. A and h are pulled back to X_0(Q) and X_1(Q).
items.locator: §6.1, Definition 6.1 and the following sentence, pp. 835–836

items.name: A power of the Hasse invariant lifts to characteristic zero
items.statement: For the (neat-level) Siegel 3-fold X over O there are an integer r > 0 and a section A ∈ H^0(X, ω^{r(p−1)}) whose reduction modulo ϖ is h^r ∈ H^0(X_k, ω_k^{r(p−1)}).

items.name: Lemma 6.2(1): multiplication by h is injective and prime-to-p Hecke-equivariant
items.note: The Siegel analogue of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/hasse-multiplication-phi. That item is planned at R15.3/R15.2 only for modular curves. Here it depends on the missing Siegel Hasse invariant and the missing Siegel Hecke operators. Injectivity needs h to be nonzero on every component of the special fibre (the ordinary locus is dense).

items.name: Lemma 6.2(2): multiplication by h commutes with T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2} when b ≥ 3
items.statement: Let μ = (a,b) ∈ X*(T)^+_M with a ≥ b ≥ 3. Then the injection h: H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)_k) ↪ H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a+p−1, b+p−1)_k) of Lemma 6.2(1) (and its cuspidal version) is also equivariant for the operators T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2}.
items.note: This depends on the missing p-operators and on the two external inputs from Pilloni and Tilouine (items ext-hasse-commutes-with-Up-operators and ext-tilouine-Tp-Up-congruences). The extraction records a gap in the proof (the S_p-term); a q-expansion argument repairs it. No layer plans U_{p,1} or U_{p,2} on Siegel forms mod p.

items.name: Multiplication by the Hasse invariant commutes with U_{p,1} and U_{p,2}
items.statement: Multiplication by the Hasse invariant h (from weight (a,b) to weight (a+p−1, b+p−1), on mod-p Siegel modular forms) commutes with the Hecke operators U_{p,1} and U_{p,2}.
items.note: External input: Pilloni 2012 §A.3 and Tilouine 2012 Lemme 8.7. No layer plans the operators U_{p,1}, U_{p,2} on mod-p Siegel forms or their commutation with h. OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O6 plans 'the operators at primes 𝔭|p' only for Hilbert overconvergent forms. O8 treats Siegel varieties only as coefficient-sheaf examples. External input: V. Pilloni, Sur la théorie de Hida pour le groupe GSp_2g, Bull. Soc. Math. France 140 (2012) [57], §A.3; J. Tilouine, Formes compagnons et complexe BGG dual pour GSp4, Ann. Inst. Fourier 62 (2012) [68], Lemme 8.7

items.name: Congruences T_{p,1} ≡ U_{p,1} and p^{3−b}T_{p,2} ≡ U_{p,2} mod p for b ≥ 3
items.statement: For μ = (a,b) with a ≥ b ≥ 3, on mod-p Siegel modular forms of weight μ: T_{p,1} ≡ U_{p,1} mod p and p^{3−b}T_{p,2} ≡ U_{p,2} mod p.
items.note: External input: Tilouine 2012 Lemme 8.5. It concerns the level-p operators U_{p,i} against the spherical T_{p,i} on Siegel forms mod p. No layer plans either operator family for GSp4. External input: J. Tilouine, Formes compagnons et complexe BGG dual pour GSp4, Ann. Inst. Fourier 62 (2012) [68], Lemme 8.5

items.name: Definition 6.3: the bound N(μ) for vanishing of higher cohomology
items.statement: Let μ = (a,b) ∈ X*(T)^+_M with a ≥ b ≥ 2. N(μ) denotes an integer such that for all t ≥ N(μ), all i > 0 and all Z ∈ {X, X_0(Q), X_1(Q)}, H^i(Z, ω(a+t, b+t)(−∞)_k) = 0. Such an integer exists by the proof of [57, Théorème 6.2].
items.locator: §6.1, Definition 6.3 and the preceding sentence, p. 836
items.note: A definition that rests on the missing vanishing theorem (ext-pilloni-vanishing-large-parallel-weight) for subcanonical extensions of vector-valued automorphic bundles on Siegel toroidal compactifications over k. The paper uses this property again in §7.1 (p. 848, the sentence before Lemma 7.4): for t ≥ N(μ), the vanishing hypothesis of Theorem 7.3 (H^i(X, W^sub_{μ+(t,t),k}) = 0 and H^i(X_0(Q), W^sub_{μ+(t,t),k}) = 0 for i > 0) holds in weight μ + (t,t). This is exactly the defining property of N(μ) on X and X_0(Q). Lemmas 7.4–7.6 (pp. 848–850) apply it to weight shifts by multiples of p − 1. Lemma 7.4 chooses t with (p−1)t ≥ N(μ).

items.name: Vanishing of higher coherent cohomology of cuspidal sheaves in large parallel twists
items.statement: For μ = (a,b) with a ≥ b ≥ 2 there is an integer N such that H^i(Z, ω(a+t, b+t)(−∞)_k) = 0 for all t ≥ N, all i > 0 and Z ∈ {X, X_0(Q), X_1(Q)} (toroidal compactifications over O of neat-level Siegel 3-folds).
items.note:
External input: the proof of Pilloni 2012 Théorème 6.2. It amounts to vanishing of R^iπ_* (π: toroidal → minimal) for the subcanonical extension, followed by Serre vanishing for the ample ω. Existing layers stop short of it:
- AutomorphicBundles:B3 defines the pushforward to the minimal compactification only in characteristic zero.
- TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure:TC.1 plans 'approximation/extension lemmas that produce finite-level classical sections after twisting by sufficiently high powers of an ample automorphic line bundle' for Scholze's Hodge-type towers on the minimal compactification with the boundary ideal. That is not higher-cohomology vanishing for vector-valued subcanonical extensions on the toroidal compactification over k.
- ShimuraCompactifications:C3 says higher direct images need 'a separate theorem', which it does not state here. External input: V. Pilloni, Sur la théorie de Hida pour le groupe GSp_2g, Bull. Soc. Math. France 140 (2012) [57], proof of Théorème 6.2

items.name: Surjectivity of reduction maps on H^0 in weights beyond N(μ)
items.statement: Let μ = (a,b), a ≥ b ≥ 2, t ≥ N(μ), and Z ∈ {X, X_0(Q), X_1(Q)}. Then H^0(Z, ω(a+t,b+t)(−∞)) → H^0(Z, ω(a+t,b+t)(−∞)_k) and H^0(Z, ω(a+t,b+t)(−∞)_K) → H^0(Z, ω(a+t,b+t)(−∞)_{K/O}) are surjective. Consequently H^0(Z, ω(a+t,b+t)(−∞)_{K/O}) ≅ H^0(Z, ω(a+t,b+t)(−∞)) ⊗_O K/O, with H^0(Z, ω(a+t,b+t)(−∞)) a finite free O-module.
items.locator: §6.1, remark after Definition 6.3, p. 836; the consequence is used in the proof of Theorem 6.13, p. 843
items.note: This is a formal consequence of vanishing: from H^1 = ϖH^1 and finiteness, Nakayama (mathlib:Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot) gives H^1 = 0, and surjectivity follows. The coherent cohomology of integral Siegel threefolds that it concerns is not planned. The modular-curve analogue (Katz 1.7.1) is the reviewed R15.2 node cited by PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/hecke-algebras-weight-n.

items.name: Lemma 6.4: multiplication by A^s mod ϖ^m is injective and Hecke-equivariant away from p
items.statement:
Let μ = (a,b) ∈ X*(T)^+_M with a ≥ b ≥ 2 and let m > 0. There exists an integer s > 0 such that, setting t = rs(p−1):
(1) t ≥ N(μ);
(2) multiplication by A^s defines an injection H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)_{O/ϖ^m}) ↪ H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a+t, b+t)_{O/ϖ^m}), and likewise on the cuspidal subspaces ω(·,·)(−∞)_{O/ϖ^m}.
The injection in (2) is equivariant for the Hecke operators T_{x,i} for each x ∉ S ∪ Q ∪ {p}, for the operators U_{x,i} for each x ∈ Q, and for the diamond operators ⟨u⟩, u ∈ Δ_Q. The paper omits the diamond operators, but Remark 6.5 needs them, and they hold because A is pulled back from X [sourceIssues E51].
Any integer s > N(μ)/(r(p−1)) with p^{m−1} | s works.
items.note: The Siegel version of the mod-ϖ^m weight shift. The modular-curve version is planned at AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.3 (see PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/hasse-multiplication-phi). This one needs the missing lift A, the bound N(μ) and Goldring's equivariance. The paper uses the same fact in §8.6: in the proof of Lemma 8.14 (pp. 865–866) and in the paragraph before Lemma 8.15 (p. 867). Multiplication by a power of the Hasse invariant, or by a lift whose q-expansion is ≡ 1 mod ϖ^m (for A^s this holds when p^{m−1} | s), is injective and commutes with the Hecke operators away from p. This multiplication is the identity on q-expansions, so injectivity also follows from the q-expansion principle (Theorem 8.1, p. 856). The GL2 weight-one analogue used in Lemma 8.14 is recorded in lemma-8-14-gl2-weight-one-analogue.

items.name: Hecke-equivariance of multiplication by A^s modulo ϖ^m when p^{m−1} | s
items.statement:
Let A ∈ H^0(X, ω^{r(p−1)}) be a lift to O of h^r, and suppose p^{m−1} | s.
- A^s mod ϖ^m depends only on h^r: if A ≡ A′ mod ϖ, then A^{p^{m−1}} ≡ A′^{p^{m−1}} mod ϖ^m.
- Multiplication by A^s, H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)_{O/ϖ^m}) → H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a+rs(p−1), b+rs(p−1))_{O/ϖ^m}), is injective.
- It commutes with the Hecke correspondences at every prime x ≠ p that Lemma 6.4 uses: the T_{x,i} for x ∉ S ∪ Q ∪ {p} and the U_{x,i} for x ∈ Q. It also commutes with the diamond operators ⟨u⟩.
The paper cites [32, Theorem 6.2.1] for this. Whether that theorem literally covers the U_{x,i} at the level was not checked.
items.note: External input: Goldring 2014, Theorem 6.2.1. No layer plans Hecke-equivariance of multiplication by a lifted Hasse power mod ϖ^m for Siegel (or general PEL) forms. The GL2 analogue is planned at AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.3 (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/hasse-multiplication-phi, whose note asks for the p^{m−1}-power refinement there). External input: W. Goldring, Galois representations associated to holomorphic limits of discrete series, Compos. Math. 150 (2014) [32], Theorem 6.2.1

items.name: The ideals I_{μ,m} ⊂ T_μ(Q) and Ĩ_{μ,m} ⊂ T̃_μ(Q)
items.statement: For μ = (a,b) with a ≥ b ≥ 2 and m > 0, I_{μ,m} (resp. Ĩ_{μ,m}) is the annihilator of H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_{O/ϖ^m}) in T_μ(Q) (resp. T̃_μ(Q)).
items.note: The general notion is in Mathlib: mathlib:Module.annihilator ('the ideal of all elements r : R such that r • M = 0'). The item is that notion applied to the missing Siegel Hecke algebra T_μ(Q) and the missing module H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_{O/ϖ^m}).

items.name: Remark 6.5: A^s induces a surjection T_{μ′}(Q) ↠ T_μ(Q)/I_{μ,m}
items.statement: Let μ = (a,b) with a ≥ b ≥ 2, m > 0, let s and t = rs(p−1) be as in Lemma 6.4, and let μ′ = μ + (t,t). Multiplication by A^s induces a surjective O-algebra map T_{μ′}(Q) ↠ T_μ(Q)/I_{μ,m}, sending each T_{x,i} (x ∉ S ∪ Q ∪ {p}), U_{x,i} (x ∈ Q) and ⟨u⟩ to the operator of the same name. In particular every maximal ideal m of T_μ(Q) pulls back to a maximal ideal of T_{μ′}(Q), also denoted m.
items.note: This depends on Lemma 6.4 (missing) and on the Siegel Hecke algebras (missing). The CG18 analogue for modular curves (case1-hecke-quotients) is also missing.

items.name: Remark 6.5: h induces T_{μ′}(Q) ↠ T_μ(Q)/I_{μ,1}, extending to T̃ when b ≥ 3
items.statement: Let μ = (a,b) with a ≥ b ≥ 2 and μ′ = μ + (p−1, p−1). Lemma 6.2 induces a surjection T_{μ′}(Q) ↠ T_μ(Q)/I_{μ,1}. If b ≥ 3, this extends to a surjection T̃_{μ′}(Q) ↠ T̃_μ(Q)/Ĩ_{μ,1}, also matching T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2}.
items.note: This depends on Lemma 6.2 (missing) and on the Siegel Hecke algebras T and T̃ (missing).

items.name: Proposition 6.6: the Hecke-valued character χ_μ
items.statement:
Let μ = (a,b) ∈ X*(T)^+_M with a ≥ b ≥ 2 (so that T^an_μ(Q) is defined), and let w = a+b−6. There is a continuous character χ_μ: G_Q → T^an_μ(Q)^× such that:
(1) χ_μ|G_{Q_p} is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weight w;
(2) for all x ∉ S ∪ Q ∪ {p}, χ_μ is unramified at x and χ_μ(Frob_x) = S_x.
In particular χ_μ = χ_{μ,0}ε^{−w} for some finite-order character χ_{μ,0}: G_Q → T̃_μ(Q)^×; in fact it takes values in T^an_μ(Q)^×.
items.note: A character valued in a Hecke algebra that interpolates the central operators S_x. Mathlib has the cyclotomic character (mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter, used for ε), and class field theory over Q is Tau Ceti's ClassFieldTheory roadmap. No layer plans the Hecke-valued central character of Siegel (or any GSp4) Hecke algebras. The rank-one CG18 analogue gl1-galois-rep-and-R-to-T is also missing.

items.name: Taylor (1991), Proposition 4: Hecke-valued character interpolating S_x
items.statement: The central operators S_x (x prime to the level and p) on Siegel modular forms of weight μ and level K_1(Q) are the Frobenius values of a continuous character χ_μ: G_Q → T^an_μ(Q)^× unramified outside S ∪ Q ∪ {p}, crystalline at p of Hodge–Tate weight w = a+b−6 (after the paper's ν^{−3}-twist of the Hecke action).
items.note: External input: the proof of Taylor 1991 (Duke 63), Proposition 4. No layer plans it. External input: R. Taylor, Galois representations associated to Siegel modular forms of low weight, Duke Math. J. 63 (1991) [65], proof of Proposition 4

items.name: Definition 6.7: the Hecke polynomial Q_x(X) and the eigenvalue map λ_f
items.statement: For a prime x, Q_x(X) := X^4 − T_{x,1}X^3 + (x·T_{x,2} + (x^3 + x)S_x)X^2 − x^3S_xT_{x,1}X + x^6S_x^2, a polynomial with coefficients in the Hecke algebra (printed with 'Q_x(T)' on the left, T standing for the Hecke operators; the paper later writes Q_x(X) for the same polynomial). If a modular form f is an eigenform for a collection of Hecke operators T, λ_f denotes the map with Tf = λ_f(T)f. If f is an eigenform for the T_{x,i} at x, then λ_f(Q_x(X)) denotes the specialised polynomial.
items.note: The GSp4 spinor Hecke polynomial. IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.3 plans only the GL_n polynomial and warns 'Do not assert this GL_n polynomial for a general reductive group without choosing a representation of its L-group'. SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.4 plans the Satake transform for unramified G in general, not the spin-representation polynomial. Definition 6.7 writes Q_x(T) for this polynomial in X, with T standing for the Hecke operators, and later text writes Q_x(X). This is a difference of notation, not a misprint.

items.name: Proposition 6.8(1)–(2): GSp4-valued Galois representation of a cuspidal eigenform of regular weight
items.note:
No layer attaches Galois representations to Siegel modular forms or cuspidal representations of GSp4:
- AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations (R19.1–R19.6) covers 'modular and Hilbert modular forms'.
- AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII covers GL_n over CM fields via unitary Shimura varieties.
- TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure's README says 'The totally-real symplectic realization additionally requires Arthur's endoscopic transfer/classification input', owned by ML.4, and builds no GSp4 representation.

items.name: Proposition 6.8(3): crystallinity at p, Hodge–Tate weights and crystalline Frobenius
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition 6.8 (μ = (a,b), a ≥ b ≥ 3, 𝐰 = a+b−3), r_f|G_{Q_p} is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights 𝐰, a−1, b−2, 0. If moreover f is an eigenform for the Hecke operators at p, then the characteristic polynomial of the crystalline Frobenius Φ on D_cris(r_f|G_{Q_p}) is λ_f(Q_p(X)).
items.note: Crystallinity, Hodge–Tate weights and crystalline Frobenius are planned for GL2 (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5) and for polarized GL_n over CM fields (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.6). The GSp4 statement (via the transfer to GL4) is not planned.

items.name: Proposition 6.8(4): ordinary eigenforms give upper-triangular r_f|G_{Q_p}
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition 6.8 (μ = (a,b), a ≥ b ≥ 3, 𝐰 = a+b−3), suppose f is ordinary, i.e. an eigenform for T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2} whose eigenvalues are p-adic units. Then λ_f(Q_p(X)) has distinct roots α_p, β_p, γ_p, δ_p with p-adic valuations 0, b−2, a−1, 𝐰 respectively. Furthermore r_f|G_{Q_p} is GSp4(K′)-conjugate to an upper-triangular representation (all entries above the diagonal arbitrary) with diagonal entries λ(α_p), ε^{−(b−2)}·λ(p^{−(b−2)}β_p), ε^{−(a−1)}·λ(p^{−(a−1)}γ_p), ε^{−𝐰}·λ(p^{−𝐰}δ_p).
items.note: The ordinary local structure is planned only for GL2 (OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.3, AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5). The GSp4 upper-triangular shape for ordinary Siegel eigenforms (Urban; Mok Thm 3.5) is not planned.

items.name: Proposition 6.8(5): local–global compatibility for absolutely irreducible r_f
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition 6.8, if r_f is absolutely irreducible then it satisfies local–global compatibility at all primes: for each prime x, WD(r_f|G_{Q_x})^{F-ss} corresponds to the local component π_x under the local Langlands correspondence for GSp4, with the paper's normalisation of the Hecke action.
items.note: Needs the local Langlands correspondence for GSp4 (Gan–Takeda). PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23/gsp4-llc records it as missing and routes it to ML.4 as a source. Local–global compatibility is planned only for GL2 (R19.4) and GL_n (AG2.5).
