items.name: Galois representations for cuspidal automorphic representations of GSp4 (Taylor, Laumon, Weissauer; Mok, Thm 3.5)
items.note: External input: Mok 2014, Theorem 3.5 (building on Taylor, Laumon, Weissauer, Urban, Genestier–Tilouine, Gan–Takeda and Sorensen). No layer plans it (see galois-rep-of-regular-weight-cuspidal-eigenform). External input: C. P. Mok, Galois representations attached to automorphic forms on GL2 over CM fields, Compos. Math. 150 (2014) [55], Theorem 3.5; building on Taylor, Laumon, Weissauer, with refinements by Urban, Genestier–Tilouine, Gan–Takeda, Sorensen

items.name: For simple generic π, R_p can be conjugated into GSp4 (as cited: 'main theorem of [6]')
items.statement: If π (as in Proposition 6.8) is simple generic in the terminology of [55], the representation R_p: G_Q → GL4(Q̄_p) is conjugate to a representation valued in GSp4(Q̄_p), preserving a symplectic form up to the similitude character.
items.note: The paper cites 'the main theorem of [6]', but the result is Bellaïche–Chenevier 2011, Thm 1.2 ([7]), not [6] [sourceIssues E56]. No layer plans that polarized Galois representations attached to automorphic forms carry the expected sign, nor its GSp4 consequence (see ext-bellaiche-chenevier-sign-theorem). External input: Cited as 'the main theorem of [6]': J. Bellaïche and G. Chenevier, Families of Galois representations and Selmer groups, Astérisque 324 (2009). The symplectic-sign result is the main theorem (Thm 1.2) of [7]: Bellaïche–Chenevier, The sign of Galois representations attached to automorphic forms for unitary groups, Compos. Math. 147 (2011)

items.name: Bellaïche–Chenevier: polarised Galois representations from unitary groups have the expected (symplectic) sign
items.statement: Let Π be a regular algebraic, conjugate self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation, descended to a unitary group. If its associated ℓ-adic Galois representation is absolutely irreducible, then the polarisation it carries has sign +1. In the GSp4 application, the 4-dimensional representation is therefore symplectic rather than orthogonal.
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7 plans polarizations and 'prove its symmetry sign' as formal API. AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.2 plans to 'recover the specified polarization'. No layer, README or reviewed decomposition names the theorem that for absolutely irreducible automorphic Galois representations of unitary groups the sign is +1 (Bellaïche–Chenevier 2011, Thm 1.2). The AG2 decomposition has no Bellaïche–Chenevier node. External input: J. Bellaïche and G. Chenevier, The sign of Galois representations attached to automorphic forms for unitary groups, Compos. Math. 147 (2011) [7], Theorem 1.2

items.name: Lemma 6.9(1): residual Galois representation attached to a maximal ideal of T^an_μ(Q)
items.statement: Let μ = (a,b) ∈ X*(T)^+_M with a ≥ b ≥ 2, and let m be a maximal ideal of T^an_μ(Q). There is a continuous semisimple representation r̄_m: G_Q → GL4(T^an_μ(Q)/m) such that for each x ∉ S ∪ Q ∪ {p}, r̄_m|G_{Q_x} is unramified and r̄_m(Frob_x) has characteristic polynomial Q_x(X) mod m.
items.note: For modular curves the analogue (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/residual-galois-rep-m-empty) is planned at R15.5/R19.1. For Siegel Hecke algebras it needs the missing GSp4 Galois representations (Prop. 6.8) and the missing Hecke algebras. Field-of-definition descent is planned (ext-cht-residual-field-of-definition). §1 uses r̄_m in Theorem 1.2 (p. 803), whose hypothesis asks for a maximal ideal m of T with r̄_m ≅ r̄. The symplectic refinement for absolutely irreducible r̄_m is Lemma 6.9(2) (p. 840), recorded in residual-galois-rep-symplectic-if-irreducible. 'Non-Eisenstein' (r̄_m absolutely irreducible) is Definition 6.11 (p. 840).

items.name: Lemma 6.9(2): absolutely irreducible r̄_m is symplectic
items.statement: In Lemma 6.9, if r̄_m is absolutely irreducible then r̄_m preserves a symplectic pairing. Hence, after conjugation, r̄_m: G_Q → GSp4(T^an_μ(Q)/m).
items.note: Uses Arthur's transfer (planned, ML.4), descent to a unitary group (ML.4) and the Bellaïche–Chenevier sign theorem (missing). No layer plans the conclusion for GSp4.

items.name: Descent of a residual representation to the field generated by its traces
items.statement: A continuous semisimple representation of G_Q over F̄ (F a finite field) whose characteristic polynomials have coefficients in F is conjugate to a representation defined over F.
items.note: Over a finite field F the obstruction vanishes, because finite division rings are commutative: mathlib:littleWedderburn ('A finite division ring is a field'). That step should be written into R01.5 with CHT Prop. 3.4.2 as source. The semisimplified reconstruction over F̄ is IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.1 ('reconstruction over algebraically closed fields up to semisimplification'). External input: L. Clozel, M. Harris, R. Taylor, Automorphy for some ℓ-adic lifts of automorphic mod ℓ Galois representations, Publ. Math. IHÉS 108 (2008) [20], argument of Proposition 3.4.2

items.name: Remark 6.10: Lemma 6.9 for T_μ(Q) and T̃_μ(Q)
items.statement: Lemma 6.9 (both parts) holds with T^an_μ(Q) replaced by T_μ(Q) or T̃_μ(Q): for a maximal ideal m of either algebra there is a continuous semisimple r̄_m: G_Q → GL4(T/m) with the same Frobenius characteristic polynomials. It is symplectic when absolutely irreducible.
items.note: The same as Lemma 6.9 for the missing algebras T_μ(Q) and T̃_μ(Q).

items.name: Definition 6.11: non-Eisenstein maximal ideals
items.statement: A maximal ideal m (of T^an_μ(Q), T_μ(Q) or T̃_μ(Q)) is non-Eisenstein if the representation r̄_m of Lemma 6.9 / Remark 6.10 is absolutely irreducible.
items.note: For GL2 the notion is planned at ModularCurvesPartII:R14.3 and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.6 (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/eisenstein-maximal-ideal). Here it is defined through r̄_m for the missing GSp4 Hecke algebras. The GL_n analogue non-eisenstein-max-ideal-GLn is also missing.

items.name: The auxiliary prime q (neat level)
items.statement: Let r̄: G_Q → GSp4(k) be as in §4, in particular satisfying Assumption 4.2: there is σ ∈ G_Q with ε̄(σ) = q̄ ≢ 1 mod p such that no ratio of two eigenvalues of r̄(σ) equals q̄. By the Chebotarev density theorem, applied to the finite extension cut out by r̄ and ε̄, there are infinitely many primes q with q ≢ 1 mod p such that no pair of eigenvalues of r̄(Frob_q) has ratio q mod p. Fix such a q with q ≠ p, r̄ unramified at q, and q ≥ 3. The paper says 'choose any such q' and omits q ≥ 3. That condition is needed so that the full congruence level at q makes K neat (§5.2).
items.note: A choice specific to this paper, made from Assumption 4.2 (§4) and Chebotarev. Chebotarev is planned (tauceti Chebotarev layers 10 and 14). Tau Ceti already has frobeniusPrimeSet and NumberField.exists_auxiliaryPrime, but no density theorem. No layer plans a prime of this kind for GSp4. GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5 and G7 plan Taylor–Wiles primes, a different condition.

items.name: The level K = ∏ K_x of §6.3
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3 supplies parahoric group schemes in general: 'For a facet construct the smooth affine O_E-group scheme …; Identify pro-p congruence subgroups'. That covers GSp4(Z_x) and the Iwahori, Klingen and paramodular subgroups as parahorics of GSp4. Π(x)^+ (the kernel of Π(x) → (Z/x)^×) and the assignment of K_x by the types U1, U2, U3, P and H are specific to this paper and not planned. No layer mentions paramodular or Klingen level for GSp4.

items.name: The ordinary maximal ideals m_∅ and m ⊇ m_∅ (regular weight)
items.statement: Let μ = (a,b) ∈ X*(T)^+_M with a ≥ b ≥ 3 (a regular weight). Let m_∅ be a maximal ideal of T^ord_μ (the ordinary Hecke algebra with Q = ∅) with residue field k. Via the common prime-to-(S ∪ Q ∪ {p}) Hecke operators, m_∅ pulls back to an ideal of T^an_μ(Q)^ord, which in turn pushes forward to an ideal of T_μ(Q)^ord; both are again denoted m_∅. The ideal m_∅ ⊂ T^an_μ(Q)^ord is maximal; m_∅ ⊂ T_μ(Q)^ord need not be. Let m ⊂ T_μ(Q)^ord be any maximal ideal containing m_∅. Under Assumption 6.12, r̄_m, r̄_{m_∅} and r̄ are all isomorphic.
items.note: Defined inside the missing ordinary Siegel Hecke algebras.

items.name: Assumption 6.12(1): r̄_{m_∅} ≅ r̄
items.statement: With r̄, μ and m_∅ as above: r̄_{m_∅} ≅ r̄. In particular, since r̄ is absolutely irreducible, m_∅ is non-Eisenstein.
items.note: A hypothesis of this paper on the missing GSp4 Hecke data.

items.name: The β-part H^0(…)^β, the idempotent e_β, and the algebras T(Q)^β (corrected)
items.statement:
Let α, β ∈ k^× be the elements attached to r̄|G_{Q_p} in §4: r̄|G_p has an unramified subspace λ(α) ⊕ λ(β), with α ≠ β. Let α̃, β̃ ∈ O be lifts. For M = O, O/ϖ^m or K/O:
- H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_M)^β is the image of the idempotent e_β onto the direct summand of H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_M) on which T_{p,1} − β̃ and Q_{p,2} − α̃β̃ are topologically nilpotent. For example e_β = (1 − lim_n (T_{p,1} − β̃)^{n!})·(1 − lim_n (Q_{p,2} − α̃β̃)^{n!}).
- T^an_μ(Q)^β (resp. T_μ(Q)^β, T̃_μ(Q)^β) is the image of T^an_μ(Q) (resp. T_μ(Q), T̃_μ(Q)) in End_O(H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_{K/O})^β).
The paper defines this image for each M under one notation. M = K/O is the one used in Theorem 6.13. For M = O/ϖ^m the image is the quotient by the annihilator of the ϖ^m-torsion.
The α-versions (e_α, H^0(…)^α, T(Q)^α) are defined with α and β swapped.
items.note: The idempotent is L0a-type algebra. e_β = (1 − lim(T_{p,1} − β̃)^{n!})(1 − lim(Q_{p,2} − α̃β̃)^{n!}) is built from PadicFamilies:L0a projectors ('U^(n!) eventually constant with value the projector e'), applied to U − β̃. The operators and Hecke algebras are missing. The extraction records that the printed e_β is reversed: it projects onto the summand where the operators are invertible.

items.name: Theorem 6.13(1)–(2): Galois representation valued in T_μ(Q)^β_m (regular weight)
items.statement:
Hypotheses:
- r̄ is as in §4: continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible, with ν(r̄) = ε̄^{−(a_4−1)} (a_4 ≥ 2 the integer called a in §4). It has the stated shape at p with α, β ∈ k^× and (α²−1)(β²−1)(α²β²−1)(α−β) ≠ 0, and satisfies Assumptions 4.1–4.3.
- q, S = S(r̄) ∪ {q}, Q and K are as in §6.3.
- μ = (a,b) with a ≥ b ≥ 3.
- m_∅ ⊂ T^ord_μ and m ⊂ T_μ(Q)^ord are as above, and Assumption 6.12 holds.
- T_μ(Q)^β_m ≠ 0, where T_μ(Q)^β is formed with M = K/O. The paper leaves this implicit. It forces (p−1) | (b−2), and it holds in the application in Theorem 6.17.
- w = a+b−6 and 𝐰 = w + 3 = a+b−3.
Then there is a continuous representation r = r^β_{μ,m}: G_Q → GSp4(T_μ(Q)^β_m) lifting r̄_m = r̄ such that:
(1) ν∘r = χ_μ ε^{−3} = χ_{μ,0}ε^{−𝐰}, where χ_{μ,0} is a finite-order character, unramified at p and trivial modulo m;
(2) for each prime x ∉ S ∪ Q ∪ {p}, r is unramified at x and r(Frob_x) has characteristic polynomial Q_x(X).
items.note: The main result of §6.3, a GSp4-valued lift over a Siegel Hecke algebra. Its GL2 counterparts (R19.6, R21.3) are planned. The GSp4 inputs are missing: Galois representations, Hecke algebras, weight shifting and gluing.

items.name: Theorem 6.13(3): units d_{p,i}, residual values β and α, ordinary shape at p
items.statement:
In the setting of Theorem 6.13 there are units d_{p,1}, d_{p,2}, d_{p,3}, d_{p,4} ∈ T_μ(Q)^β_m satisfying:
(a) d_{p,1} ≡ β and d_{p,2} ≡ α mod m;
(b) r|G_{Q_p} is GSp4-conjugate to an upper-triangular representation with diagonal λ(d_{p,1}), ε^{−(b−2)}λ(d_{p,2}), ε^{−(a−1)}λ(d_{p,3}), ε^{−𝐰}λ(d_{p,4}).
The paper further asserts Q_p(X) = (X − d_{p,1})(X − p^{b−2}d_{p,2})(X − p^{a−1}d_{p,3})(X − p^{𝐰}d_{p,4}) in T_μ(Q)^β_m[X]. This makes sense in T̃_μ(Q)^β_m[X], since the coefficients of Q_p(X) involve T_{p,1}, T_{p,2} and S_p, and the proof does not establish it in weight μ [sourceIssues E61, E60].
items.note: The paper has gaps here [sourceIssues E61, E60]. Q_p(X) has coefficients in T̃, not T, and the factorisation is transported from weight μ′ without transporting the p-operators. The proof also has the misprint d_{p,1} for d_{p,3} [sourceIssues E64]. No layer plans the GSp4 statement.

items.name: Theorem 6.13(4): after a square-root twist, r satisfies Definition 4.6(2)–(5)
items.note: Twisting deformations by characters is planned for GL2 (GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4, 'twisting by characters'). The GSp4 minimality conditions of Definition 4.6 and their verification via Sorensen and Genestier–Tilouine are missing.

items.name: Remark 6.14 (expectation, not used): the Hecke rings are torsion-free
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 6.13, the Hecke rings in question (T_μ(Q)^β_m) are expected to be torsion-free (O-flat).
items.note: An expectation that the paper does not use or prove. It concerns the missing GSp4 Hecke rings.

items.name: Reduction of Theorem 6.13 to high weight via A^s (proof of Theorem 6.13)
items.statement: Fix m > 0, choose s as in Lemma 6.4, and let t = rs(p−1) and μ′ = (a′,b′) = (a+t, b+t). The composite e′_β∘A^s (e′_β the β-idempotent in weight μ′) is an injection H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_{O/ϖ^m})^β_m ↪ H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a+t,b+t)(−∞)_{O/ϖ^m})^β_m, equivariant for T_{μ′}(Q) → T_μ(Q). It gives a surjection T_{μ′}(Q)^β_m ↠ T_μ(Q)^β_m/I_{μ,m}. Since T_μ(Q)^β_m = lim_m T_μ(Q)^β_m/I_{μ,m}, it suffices to construct, for each m, r_m: G_Q → GSp4(T_μ(Q)^β_m/I_{μ,m}) with the properties of the theorem, which is reduced to weight μ′.
items.note: The corrected construction e′_β∘A^s (the extraction records the gap and the fix) on the missing Siegel spaces. The limit T_μ(Q)^β_m = lim_m T/I_{μ,m} is elementary, as for PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/weight-one-torsion-hecke-quotients, which is missing.

items.name: T_{μ′}(Q)^β_m embeds in a product of rings of integers, one per eigenform (proof of Theorem 6.13)
items.statement: Let μ′ = (a′,b′) = μ + (t,t) with t ≥ N(μ). Then H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a′,b′)(−∞)_{K/O}) ≅ H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a′,b′)(−∞)) ⊗ K/O, so T_{μ′}(Q) acts faithfully on H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a′,b′)(−∞)) and on H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a′,b′)(−∞)_K). The paper concludes T_{μ′}(Q)^β_m ↪ ∏_i O_{K_i}, with K_i/K finite, one for each minimal prime ℘_i of T_{μ′}(Q)^β_m, and each ℘_i corresponding to an eigenform f_i for T_{μ′}(Q)^β_m.
items.note: The GL2 analogue (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/T-n-m-alpha-image) is planned at R15.2/R19.6. Here the Siegel Hecke algebra is missing. The extraction records the gap: reducedness of T_{μ′}(Q)^β_m, i.e. semisimplicity of U_{x,i} (x ∈ Q) and ⟨u⟩, is not proved.

items.name: Gluing Galois representations over a Hecke algebra inside ∏ O_{K_i} (CHT Prop. 3.4.4; Gee–Geraghty Lemma 7.1.1)
items.statement: Let T be a complete local Noetherian O-algebra with residue field k, finite over O, with T ↪ ∏_i O_{K′_i}. Let r_i: G_Q → GSp4(O_{K′_i}) be continuous lifts of an absolutely irreducible r̄: G_Q → GSp4(k) such that the characteristic polynomials of (a dense set of) Frobenius elements under ∏_i r_i have coefficients in T. Then ∏_i r_i is conjugate to a representation r: G_Q → GSp4(T) lifting r̄.
items.note: The GL_n part is planned. IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.1: 'reconstruction … over complete local rings when residual absolute irreducibility supplies an actual representation'. AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.6: 'prove representability by a continuous representation over the localised completed Hecke algebra under absolute residual irreducibility'. The symplectic refinement is not planned: Gee–Geraghty Lemma 7.1.1, replacing CHT Lemma 2.1.12, conjugates the glued GL4(T)-valued representation into GSp4(T). External input: L. Clozel, M. Harris, R. Taylor, Publ. Math. IHÉS 108 (2008) [20], argument of the proof of Prop. 3.4.4, using T. Gee and D. Geraghty, Companion forms for unitary and symplectic groups, Duke Math. J. 161 (2012) [29], Lemma 7.1.1 in place of [20, Lemma 2.1.12]

items.name: All lifts of r̄ are unramified at the auxiliary prime q
items.statement: Let q be as in §6.3: q ≠ p, r̄ unramified at q, q ≢ 1 mod p, and no two eigenvalues of r̄(Frob_q) have ratio q mod p. Then ad^0(r̄)(1) has no G_{Q_q}-subquotient isomorphic to k. So H^2(Q_q, ad^0(r̄)) ≃ H^0(Q_q, ad^0(r̄)(1))^* = 0, and H^1(Q_q, ad^0(r̄)) consists entirely of unramified classes. In particular every lift of r̄ to an object of C_O is unramified at q.
items.note: The cohomological inputs are planned (tauceti ClassFieldTheory layer 5: local Tate duality and the Euler characteristic). LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.2 plans unramified conditions away from p for GL-type deformations. Nothing plans GSp4-valued (ad^0 = sp4-adjoint) deformation theory. The p-power part of the similitude is unramified at q because q ≢ 1 mod p.

items.name: Sorensen, Corollary 1: parahoric-fixed vectors bound the monodromy
items.statement: Let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GSp4(A_Q) as in Proposition 6.8, whose Galois representation r_π satisfies local–global compatibility at a prime x ≠ p. If π_x has nonzero vectors fixed by the Iwahori subgroup I(x) (resp. the Klingen parahoric Π(x)), then r_π|I_x is unipotent and topologically generated by a conjugate of exp(N) with N ∈ {0, N1, N2, N3} (resp. N ∈ {0, N1, N2}). The contrapositive is the form used at primes of type P: if r_π|I_x is not unipotent, then π_x has no nonzero Π(x)-fixed vectors (indeed no I(x)-fixed vectors). The converse, that no Π(x)-fixed vectors forces non-unipotent inertia, does not hold (e.g. the Steinberg representation).
items.note: External input: Sorensen 2010, Corollary 1. It is GSp4 local–global compatibility at parahoric level. Only GL2 (R19.4) and GL_n (AG2.5) local–global compatibility are planned. External input: C. M. Sorensen, Galois representations attached to Hilbert–Siegel modular forms, Doc. Math. 15 (2010) [64], Corollary 1

items.name: Sorensen §4.5: paraspherical local components give rank-1 monodromy
items.statement: If π_x is paraspherical (it has a nonzero vector fixed by a non-special maximal compact subgroup, e.g. the paramodular group K(x)), then r_π|I_x is unipotent, generated by exp(N) with N of rank at most 1. Hence, if r̄|I_x has type U1, any such lift is minimal of type U1 (Definition 4.6(3)).
items.note: External input: Sorensen 2010, §4.5 (paraspherical representations, paramodular group). No layer mentions paramodular vectors or GSp4 paraspherical representations. External input: C. M. Sorensen, Galois representations attached to Hilbert–Siegel modular forms, Doc. Math. 15 (2010) [64], §4.5

items.name: Genestier–Tilouine, Prop. 3.2.3: Klingen-spherical components at Taylor–Wiles primes are unramified
items.statement: Let x ∈ Q satisfy Assumption 6.12(2) (x ≡ 1 mod p, r̄|G_x a sum of four pairwise distinct characters). Let π_x be the local component at x of a cuspidal π of level K_1(Q) whose residual representation is r̄. If π_x has nonzero Π(x)-invariants, so that it is a subquotient of an unramified principal series, then π_x is unramified.
items.note: External input: Genestier–Tilouine 2005, Prop. 3.2.3. It is local representation theory of GSp4(Q_x) (Klingen-parahoric invariants of subquotients of unramified principal series) together with the residual distinctness at a Taylor–Wiles prime. SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups plans induction and Jacquet functors in general (SR.2), but nothing for GSp4 parahoric invariants. External input: A. Genestier and J. Tilouine, Systèmes de Taylor–Wiles pour GSp(4), Astérisque 302 (2005) [31], Proposition 3.2.3

items.name: Definition 6.15: Katz modular of weight σ = (a,2)
items.note: Katz modularity in the nonregular Siegel weight (a,2) on torsion coherent H^0. Planned analogues exist only for GL2 weight-one Katz forms, and even those are missing in PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. The paper has a gap here [sourceIssues E65]: η is not required to be cuspidal, while T_σ acts on cusp forms. §1 states the hypothesis as 'r̄ is modular of level N(r̄) and weight (j,2)' (Theorem 1.1(5), p. 802; Theorem 1.2, p. 803) without defining it. The reading that matches Theorem 1.2 differs from Definition 6.15 in level and in module: some maximal ideal m of the Hecke algebra T acting on eH⁰(Y_1(N), ω(j,2) ⊗ K/O), the non-cuspidal space at level N(r̄), has r̄_m ≅ r̄ (see E1 and E3). Assumption 6.16(1) (p. 845) says only that r̄ is Katz modular of weight σ with m_∅ and η, so its content is exactly this definition. Theorems 6.17 and 8.13 cite 'Assumption 6.16'.

items.name: The (α,β)-part, the idempotent e_{α,β}, and T_σ(Q)^{α,β} (corrected)
items.statement:
Let σ = (a,2), m_∅ and η be as in Assumption 6.16, and let m be any maximal ideal of T_σ(Q) containing m_∅. Let α̃, β̃ ∈ O lift α, β.
- e_{α,β} is the idempotent projecting onto the direct summand on which T_{p,1} − (α̃ + β̃) and Q_{p,2} − α̃β̃ are topologically nilpotent. For example e_{α,β} = (1 − lim_n (T_{p,1} − α̃ − β̃)^{n!})·(1 − lim_n (Q_{p,2} − α̃β̃)^{n!}).
- H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O})^{α,β} := e_{α,β}H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O}).
- T_σ(Q)^{α,β} is the image of T_σ(Q) in End_O(H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O})^{α,β}).
The paper asserts that, by Katz modularity, this space is nonzero after localisation at m [sourceIssues E65].
items.note: The idempotent algebra is PadicFamilies:L0a (projectors 1 − lim(U − c)^{n!}). The operators and T_σ(Q) are missing. As printed, e_{α,β} projects onto the wrong summand [sourceIssues E59]. The resulting T_σ(Q)^{α,β}_m is the ring 'T' of the main theorem. §1 calls e = e_{α,β} 'a certain ordinary projection' (p. 803). As printed, lim((T_{p,1} − α̃ − β̃)(Q_{p,2} − α̃β̃))^{n!} keeps the part where both factors are units, which is disjoint from the intended summand (E59). e_{α,β} also differs from the ordinary idempotent e = lim(T_{p,1}Q_{p,2})^{n!} of §5.5 (p. 835). The Hecke algebra T of §1 (pp. 802–803) is generated by the Hecke operators at primes not dividing Np acting on eH⁰(Y_1(N), ω(j,2) ⊗ K/O). It is the introduction's version of T_σ^{α,β} with Q = ∅, but it uses the non-cuspidal module at level N(r̄) (E1). The paper also uses the definition with O/ϖ^m coefficients and, in Theorem 8.13 (§8.6, p. 865), without (−∞).

items.name: Theorem 6.17: minimal deformation valued in T_σ(Q)^{α,β}_m (nonregular weight (a,2))
items.note: The main output of §6: the Galois side of R = T in the nonregular weight (a,2). It needs Theorem 6.13, Theorem 8.13 (doubling) and the GSp4 minimal deformation conditions, all missing. §1 (p. 803) cites Theorem 6.17 as the source of the map from R^min to T_m. For Q = ∅ the theorem gives exactly this map, the one that Theorem 9.1 shows is an isomorphism.

items.name: Doubling: the α- and β-ordinary lines span the unramified plane of Definition 4.6(6)
items.statement:
(Proof of Theorem 6.17.) Let r′_m: G_Q → GSp4(T_σ(Q)^{α,β}_m/I_{σ,m}) be obtained from the surjection T_{σ′}(Q)^β_m ↠ T_σ(Q)^{α,β}_m/I_{σ,m} and Theorem 6.13.
- The representation obtained through the α-surjection is conjugate to r′_m: both lift the absolutely irreducible r̄ with the same Frobenius characteristic polynomials.
- By Theorem 6.13(3), r′_m|G_p has a G_p-stable direct summand of rank 1, spanned by a basis vector, on which G_p acts unramifiedly with Frobenius eigenvalue lifting β. The α-version gives one with Frobenius eigenvalue lifting α.
- Since α ≠ β, Nakayama's lemma shows these two lines span an unramified free rank-2 submodule of r′_m|G_p. It has the form required by Definition 4.6(6).
items.note: The only library input is Nakayama's lemma: mathlib:Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot (Mathlib/RingTheory/Nakayama.lean). The construction concerns the missing GSp4 Hecke-valued representations. Its target, Definition 4.6(6), is a GSp4 ordinary condition from §4.

items.name: End of the proof of Theorem 6.17: the minimal deformation r_m modulo I_{σ,m}
items.statement:
Setting of Theorem 6.17: r̄; σ = (a,2) with p − 1 > a; 𝔪 any maximal ideal of T_σ(Q) containing m_∅; Assumption 6.16; and (α²−1)(β²−1)(α−β)(α²β²−1) ≠ 0.
Fix m > 0. Let I_{σ,m} be the annihilator of H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{O/ϖ^m})^{α,β} in T_σ(Q)^{α,β} (as in Remark 6.5). Then there is r_m : G_Q → GSp4(T_σ(Q)^{α,β}_𝔪/I_{σ,m}) that is a minimal deformation of r̄ outside Q (Definition 4.6).
Construction:
(i) Let A ∈ H^0(X, ω^{r(p−1)}) be the fixed lift of h^r (Definition 6.1). By Theorem 8.13 there is a power A^s of A, here with s = p^{m−1}, together with injections
 e_β∘A^s : H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{O/ϖ^m})^{α,β}_𝔪 ↪ H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a+t,2+t)(−∞)_{O/ϖ^m})^β_𝔪,
 e_α∘A^s : H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{O/ϖ^m})^{α,β}_𝔪 ↪ H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a+t,2+t)(−∞)_{O/ϖ^m})^α_𝔪,
where t = rs(p−1) = rp^{m−1}(p−1). Here e_β = lim((T_{p,1} − β̃)(Q_{p,2} − α̃β̃))^{n!} and e_α are the idempotents of §6.3.
(ii) These give surjections T_{σ'}(Q)^β_𝔪 ↠ T_σ(Q)^{α,β}_𝔪/I_{σ,m} and T_{σ'}(Q)^α_𝔪 ↠ T_σ(Q)^{α,β}_𝔪/I_{σ,m}, where σ' = σ + (t,t).
(iii) Theorem 6.13 in weight σ', together with the first surjection, gives r'_m. It satisfies Definition 4.6 except conditions (1) and (6).
(iv) Because both surjections exist, r'_m|G_{Q_p} contains two distinct rank-1 unramified submodules spanned by basis vectors. Their Frobenius eigenvalues lift α and β. By Nakayama's lemma, r'_m contains an unramified rank-2 submodule as required by Definition 4.6(6).
(v) ν(r'_m) = ε^{−(a−1)}χ_Q, where χ_Q has finite p-power order and is unramified outside Q. Since p is odd, χ_Q has a square root. The twist r_m := r'_m ⊗ (χ_Q^{1/2})^{−1} satisfies all of Definition 4.6.
items.locator: §6.4, proof of Theorem 6.17, pp. 845–846 (the part on p. 846)
items.note: No layer plans GSp4-valued deformations or Galois representations valued in torsion Hecke quotients of Siegel forms. GlobalGaloisDeformations covers GL2 (R04.x) and polarized or unpolarized GL_n (G7, G8), and a search of every stage description for GSp, Siegel modular and symplectic Galois representations finds nothing. The inputs (Theorem 8.13 doubling by powers of the lifted Hasse invariant; Theorem 6.13) are the paper's own. Two slips on the p. 846 image: the target weight is printed ω(a + t, b + t) although σ = (a,2) (read b = 2), and the text says 'r_m | G_p' where r'_m is meant; the item already uses the intended readings.

items.name: Assumption 7.1 (Taylor–Wiles primes) and the lifts α'_x, β'_x, γ'_x, δ'_x
items.statement:
Fix μ = (a,b) ∈ X*(T)^+_M with a ≥ b ≥ 2. Let m_∅ be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of T_μ, i.e. r̄_{m_∅} is absolutely irreducible (Definition 6.11). The ideals it induces in T^an_μ(Q) and T_μ(Q) (§6.3) are also called m_∅.
Assumption 7.1: for each x ∈ Q, x ≡ 1 mod p, and r̄_{m_∅}|G_{Q_x} is a direct sum of four pairwise distinct characters with Frobenius eigenvalues α_x, β_x, γ_x, δ_x ∈ k^×. They are labelled so that the plane λ(α_x) ⊕ λ(β_x) is isotropic, and hence α_xδ_x = β_xγ_x.
For x ∈ Q, fix lifts α'_x, β'_x, γ'_x, δ'_x ∈ O^× of α_x, β_x, γ_x, δ_x.
items.note: Taylor–Wiles primes are planned only for GL2 (R04.5) and for polarized GL_n (G7: 'auxiliary-prime lemma with prescribed distinct Frobenius eigenvalues and chosen eigenspaces, q_v≡1 mod p^N'). No layer treats GSp4-valued r̄ or the symplectic labelling (λ(α_x) ⊕ λ(β_x) isotropic, so α_xδ_x = β_xγ_x). This is consistent with PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18, which marked its own local Taylor–Wiles conditions (conj-A-3-TW-primes) missing.

items.name: The operators R_x, the idempotents pr_x and pr_Q, and the map pr_Q ∘ i
items.statement:
For x ∈ Q, i ∈ {1,2} and j ∈ {0,1}, U_{x,i} := [K_j(Q) β_{x,i} K_j(Q)] acts on H^n(X_j(Q), ·) (§5.5 writes K_i(Q)), where β_{x,1} = diag(1,1,x,x) and β_{x,2} = diag(1,x,x,x²). In §7.1, j = 0.
- R_x := (xU_{x,2} − α'_xγ'_x)(xU_{x,2} − β'_xδ'_x)(xU_{x,2} − γ'_xδ'_x) ∈ T_μ(Q).
- pr_x := lim_{n→∞} R_x^{n!} (printed (R'_x)^{n!}). It is the idempotent cutting out the part of the module on which R_x is invertible, i.e. where xU_{x,2} is not congruent to α_xγ_x, β_xδ_x or γ_xδ_x mod ϖ.
- The pr_x commute with one another, and pr_Q := ∏_{x∈Q} pr_x.
- i : H^0(X, ·) → H^0(X_0(Q), ·) is pullback along X_0(Q) → X. The map studied in §7.1 is pr_Q ∘ i.
items.note: The Klingen-level operators U_{x,1}, U_{x,2} on integral Siegel coherent cohomology (defined in §5.5) are planned nowhere, so neither R_x nor pr_Q is. The generic step (the limit of a^{n!} in a finite O-algebra is an idempotent cutting out a localisation) falls under IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.2 ('Prove localization decompositions over complete coefficient rings'). PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 routed its analogous localizing operator there. The printed limit is lim (R'_x)^{n!}; R'_x is not defined and R_x is meant (checked on the p. 847 image).

items.name: The ideal m ⊂ T_μ(Q) at Taylor–Wiles level
items.statement: m denotes the ideal of T_μ(Q) containing m_∅ together with the elements xU_{x,2} − α'_xβ'_x and U_{x,1} − α'_x − β'_x for each x ∈ Q.
items.note: This is a definition in the Hecke algebra T_μ(Q) of Siegel coherent cohomology at level K_0(Q), which nothing plans. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18's GL2 analogues (maximal-ideal-m-of-Tuniv and others) are also missing.

items.name: Theorem 7.2 (isomorphism with Taylor–Wiles level K_0(Q))
items.statement:
Hypotheses: μ = (a,b) ∈ X*(T)^+_M with a ≥ b ≥ 2; m_∅ a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of T_μ; Assumption 7.1 holds (with the labelling chosen so that α_xβ_x ≠ γ_xδ_x for x ∈ Q, which the proof needs [sourceIssues E67]). Let m be the ideal of T_μ(Q) containing m_∅ and xU_{x,2} − α'_xβ'_x and U_{x,1} − α'_x − β'_x for x ∈ Q.
Conclusion: m is maximal, and
pr_Q ∘ i : H^0(X, ω(a,b)(−∞)_{K/O})_{m_∅} → H^0(X_0(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_{K/O})_m
is an isomorphism. It is equivariant for the operators T_{x,i} for each x ∉ S ∪ Q ∪ {p}, and for T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2} = (pT_{p,2} + (p + p³)S_p)p^{2−b}.
items.note: The theorem is the Siegel coherent 'no new forms at Taylor–Wiles level' isomorphism. Its GL2 and Bianchi analogues in PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 (lemma-3-5, lemma-5-8) are missing and routed to GL2ModularityLiftingDefectOne. No stage mentions Klingen level or Siegel coherent cohomology.

items.name: Theorem 7.3 (the isomorphism in high weight, with explicit inverse)
items.statement:
Hypotheses: μ = (a,b) with a ≥ b ≥ 2; m_∅, Assumption 7.1 (labelled so that α_xβ_x ≠ γ_xδ_x), m and pr_Q as in Theorem 7.2; H^i(X, W^sub_{μ,k}) = 0 and H^i(X_0(Q), W^sub_{μ,k}) = 0 for all i > 0.
Conclusion: pr_Q ∘ i : H^0(X, W^sub_{μ,K/O})_{m_∅} → H^0(X_0(Q), W^sub_{μ,K/O})_m is an isomorphism.
Let d_Q := ∏_{x∈Q}[GSp4(Z_x) : Π(x)] (prime to p) and let tr be the trace of X_0(Q) → X. The restriction of d_Q^{-1}tr to the m-summand is also an isomorphism. However, contrary to the printed claim, it is not the inverse of pr_Q∘i in general. Their composite c_Q := d_Q^{-1}tr∘pr_Q∘i is an invertible Hecke operator on H^0(X, W^sub_{μ,K/O})_{m_∅}, a p-adic limit of spherical Hecke operators at the primes of Q, congruent to 4^{−|Q|} mod m_∅. An explicit inverse is c_Q^{-1}∘(d_Q^{-1}tr restricted to the m-summand).
items.note: The statement is Siegel-specific. The characteristic-zero input is the external Genestier–Tilouine result, and the trace along X_0(Q) → X is planned only in characteristic zero (B5: 'Construct pullback, coefficient identification, and trace along Hecke correspondences'). d_Q = ∏[GSp4(Z_x):Π(x)] = ∏(x+1)(x²+1), which is ≡ 4^{|Q|} mod p, so it is prime to p for odd p.

items.name: Genestier–Tilouine: no newforms at Klingen level at Taylor–Wiles primes (characteristic 0)
items.statement: As used: in the setting of Theorem 7.3, pr_Q ∘ i : H^0(X, W^sub_{μ,K})_{m_∅} → H^0(X_0(Q), W^sub_{μ,K})_m (coefficients in the field K) is an isomorphism. Equivalently, the m-part at level K_0(Q) contains no newforms at x ∈ Q, and pr_Q maps the x-old space isomorphically onto it. d_Q^{-1}tr restricted to the m-summand is also an isomorphism. Its composite with pr_Q∘i is multiplication by the Satake value c_Q = ∏_{x∈Q} Q_W(x^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{w'∈wW_Π} ∏_{a>0} c_a(w'χ_x) on each eigenform. This value is ≠ 1 in general, so the inverse is c_Q^{-1}d_Q^{-1}tr, not d_Q^{-1}tr as the paper claims.
items.locator: §7.1, proof of Theorem 7.3, p. 848 ('follows exactly as in the proof of [31, Proposition 11.1.2]')
items.note: No layer mentions Genestier–Tilouine, Klingen-parahoric invariants for GSp4(Q_x) or the Taylor–Wiles analysis for GSp4. This is an external input and should also be listed as a prerequisite paper (Astérisque 302 (2005), 177–290). External input: A. Genestier and J. Tilouine, Systèmes de Taylor–Wiles pour GSp(4), in Formes automorphes II: le cas du groupe GSp(4), Astérisque 302 (2005), 177–290, Proposition 11.1.2 [31]

items.name: Degree-0 cohomology with O/ϖ^n coefficients is ϖ^n-torsion in K/O cohomology
items.statement: Let Z be X, X_0(Q), X_1(Q) or X_Δ(Q) (flat over O), let F be a locally free sheaf on Z, and let n ≥ 1. The exact sequence 0 → O/ϖ^n → K/O →(ϖ^n) K/O → 0 and left exactness of H^0 give H^0(Z, F ⊗ O/ϖ^n) = H^0(Z, F ⊗ K/O)[ϖ^n]. This is compatible with Hecke operators and localisation. In particular, H^0(Z, F_k) is the ϖ-torsion of H^0(Z, F_{K/O}).
items.locator: §7.1, p. 848 (parenthetical remark before Lemma 7.4); used in the proofs of Lemma 7.4 (p. 848) and Theorem 7.2 (p. 851)
items.note: This is a two-line consequence of left exactness of global sections, applied to 0 → F⊗O/ϖ^n → F⊗K/O → F⊗K/O → 0, which is exact because F is O-flat. Tau Ceti already proves left exactness at the pinned commit: exact_sections (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Cohomology/LongExactSequence.lean, 'Global sections are left exact') and cohomologyZeroEquiv (H⁰(X, M) ≃+ Γ(M, ⊤)). Still missing from the libraries: the O_X-module F ⊗_O M for an O-module M, and the flatness argument. These are coherent-cohomology-with-coefficients statements owned by A0-extension. Hecke compatibility is naturality, but it needs the integral Siegel Hecke operators, which are missing elsewhere. The paper first states this fact in Remark 6.5 (§6.1, p. 837), for ω(a,b)(−∞) on X_1(Q) with a ≥ b ≥ 2 and m > 0: H⁰(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_{O/ϖ^m}) ≅ H⁰(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_{K/O})[ϖ^m]. The rest of Remark 6.5 is recorded in annihilator-ideals-I-mu-m, weight-shift-surjection-by-hasse-power and weight-shift-surjection-by-hasse-h.

items.name: Lemma 7.4 (the mod-ϖ isomorphism via the Hasse invariant)
items.statement:
Setting of Theorem 7.2: μ = (a,b) with a ≥ b ≥ 2, m_∅ non-Eisenstein, Assumption 7.1, and m, pr_Q, d_Q, tr. Choose t with (p−1)t ≥ N(μ), and set μ' = (a + t(p−1), b + t(p−1)). Let h ∈ H^0(X, ω_k^{p−1}) be the Hasse invariant.
Two commutative squares have horizontal maps h^t : H^0(X, W^sub_{μ,k})_{m_∅} → H^0(X, W^sub_{μ',k})_{m_∅} and h^t : H^0(X_0(Q), W^sub_{μ,k})_m → H^0(X_0(Q), W^sub_{μ',k})_m. The vertical maps are:
(1) pr_Q∘i (the right one an isomorphism by Theorem 7.3);
(2) d_Q^{-1}tr (the right one also an isomorphism).
Both squares are co-Cartesian. In particular, both left-hand vertical maps are isomorphisms in weight μ.
They are not mutually inverse in general, contrary to the printed claim. d_Q^{-1}tr∘pr_Q∘i = c_Q, a Hecke operator commuting with h that is congruent to 4^{−|Q|} mod m_∅. The inverse of pr_Q∘i is c_Q^{-1}d_Q^{-1}tr, and the proof works with f = c_Q^{-1}d_Q^{-1}tr(F).
items.note: Siegel-specific; it needs the Siegel Hasse invariant h and Theorem 7.3. Gap in the proof (p. 849 image): it says X_0(Q) and X are 'smooth (and in particular irreducible) over k'. Smoothness gives irreducible connected components, not irreducibility. Injectivity of multiplication by h on H⁰ needs h to be nonzero on every connected component, i.e. density of the ordinary locus in each component. The conclusion stands.

items.name: The nonordinary loci S ⊂ X_k and S_0(Q) ⊂ X_0(Q)_k
items.statement: S (resp. S_0(Q)) is the nonordinary locus of X_k (resp. X_0(Q)_k). As a scheme it is the zero locus V(h) of the Hasse invariant (the p-rank ≤ 1 locus), as the exact rows in Lemmas 7.5–7.6 require. The operators T_{x,i} (x ∉ S ∪ Q ∪ {p}) act on H^0(S, W^sub_{μ,k}) and H^0(S_0(Q), W^sub_{μ,k}), and U_{x,i} (x ∈ Q) act on H^0(S_0(Q), W^sub_{μ,k}). These spaces are localised at m_∅, resp. m, in the sense of the abstract Hecke polynomial algebra (cf. p. 851). The letter S also denotes the set of primes, and in §7.2 the ring O[Δ].
items.note: The Siegel Hasse invariant h ∈ H⁰(X, ω_k^{p−1}) and its vanishing locus are planned nowhere. AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.3 constructs the Hasse invariant on modular curves. HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H2 constructs the Hilbert Hasse ideal. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.2 owns Ekedahl–Oort/G-zip strata and their Hasse sections, but IG.0 fixes the CSnc unitary datum ('Instantiate PELModuli M0–M3's actual integral-model objects for this split datum').

items.name: The secondary Hasse invariant h̃ on the nonordinary locus
items.note: h̃ is the Hasse section of the p-rank-≤1 Ekedahl–Oort closure of the Siegel 3-fold. IG.2 already names Boxer's thesis ('Boxer Theorem C') as a source for EO Hasse sections, but only for its fixed unitary datum. Boundary extension (Boxer Thm B.2, 6.2.3) and Hecke-equivariance away from p (Boxer Thm 4.5.4(3)) are planned nowhere. Bibliography misprint (p. 893) [sourceIssues E154]: [33] Goldring–Koskivirta is printed as 'Invent. Math. 217 (2019), no. 3, 137–151'; the paper occupies pp. 887–984 (MR 3989256, as printed). The item's external field already uses 887–984. External input: G. Boxer, Torsion in the coherent cohomology of Shimura varieties and Galois representations, Ph.D. thesis, Harvard University, 2015 [12]: Theorem B.2 and Theorem 6.2.3 (extension to the boundary, 'by the normality of the p-rank 1 locus'), Theorem 4.5.4(3) (Hecke equivariance); W. Goldring and J.-S. Koskivirta, Strata Hasse invariants, Hecke algebras and Galois representations, Invent. Math. 217 (2019), 887–984 [33]; also unpublished work of Geraghty with Goldring

items.name: Exact sequences from multiplication by h (used in Lemmas 7.5 and 7.6)
items.statement:
Let ν = (a',b') with a' ≥ b' ≥ 2 and ν⁺ = ν + (p−1, p−1). Multiplication by h gives an exact sequence of sheaves on X_k
0 → W^sub_{ν,k} →(h) W^sub_{ν⁺,k} → W^sub_{ν⁺,k}|_S → 0,
and the analogue on X_0(Q)_k with S_0(Q). This yields long exact sequences
0 → H^0(X, W^sub_{ν,k}) → H^0(X, W^sub_{ν⁺,k}) → H^0(S, W^sub_{ν⁺,k}) → H^1(X, W^sub_{ν,k}) → H^1(X, W^sub_{ν⁺,k}) → ⋯
and the same on X_0(Q). These are compatible with pr_Q∘i, with d_Q^{-1}tr, and with localisation at m_∅ and m. Consequences:
- if H^1(X, W^sub_{ν,k}) = 0, then 0 → H^0(W_ν) → H^0(W_{ν⁺}) → H^0(S, W_{ν⁺}) → 0 is exact;
- if H^1(X, W^sub_{ν⁺,k}) = 0, then H^0(W_{ν⁺}) → H^0(S, W_{ν⁺}) → H^1(W_ν) → 0 is exact;
- the same holds on X_0(Q).
items.note: The sheaf sequence 0 → W_ν →h W_{ν⁺} → W_{ν⁺}|_S → 0 needs the Siegel Hasse invariant as a nonzerodivisor on X_k, which is missing. Everything after that is the long exact sequence, which Tau Ceti has at the pinned commit: TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exact_cohomologyMap_cohomologyδ, exact_cohomologyδ_cohomologyMap, sections_surjective ('exact on the right as soon as H¹(X, M₁) vanishes') and cohomologyδBaseLinear (O-linearity). Compatibility with pr_Q∘i, d_Q^{-1}tr and localisation needs the missing integral Hecke operators.

items.name: Lemma 7.5 (the isomorphism on the nonordinary locus)
items.statement: Setting of Theorem 7.2 (μ = (a,b) with a ≥ b ≥ 2, m_∅ non-Eisenstein, Assumption 7.1, m, pr_Q). The map pr_Q ∘ i : H^0(S, W^sub_{μ,k})_{m_∅} → H^0(S_0(Q), W^sub_{μ,k})_m is an isomorphism. d_Q^{-1}tr (from S_0(Q) to S) restricted to the m-part is also an isomorphism. The inverse of pr_Q∘i is c_Q^{-1}∘d_Q^{-1}tr with c_Q = d_Q^{-1}tr∘pr_Q∘i, not d_Q^{-1}tr as printed.
items.note: Siegel-specific; it needs h, h̃ and Lemma 7.4. The arithmetic s(p²−1) = s(p+1)(p−1) = t(p−1) was checked on the p. 849 image.

items.name: Lemma 7.6 (the isomorphism on H^1 over k)
items.statement: Setting of Theorem 7.2, μ = (a,b) with a ≥ b ≥ 2. The map pr_Q ∘ i : H^1(X, W^sub_{μ,k})_{m_∅} → H^1(X_0(Q), W^sub_{μ,k})_m is an isomorphism. Its inverse is c_Q^{-1}∘d_Q^{-1}tr, where c_Q = d_Q^{-1}tr∘pr_Q∘i is congruent to 4^{−|Q|} mod m_∅. The printed inverse d_Q^{-1}tr is wrong in general. The proof as printed covers only weight μ' = μ + (t−1)(p−1)(1,1) with t ≥ N(μ); see the noted gap.
items.note: Siegel-specific. It uses the four-term exact rows from hasse-multiplication-exact-sequences and reverse induction on t.

items.name: Theorem 7.2 at finite level O_n = O/ϖ^n
items.statement: Setting of Theorem 7.2. For each n ≥ 1, with O_n := O/ϖ^n, the map pr_Q ∘ i : H^0(X, W^sub_{μ,O_n})_{m_∅} → H^0(X_0(Q), W^sub_{μ,O_n})_m is an isomorphism. By item h0-torsion-coefficients, this says that the map of Theorem 7.2 is an isomorphism on ϖ^n-torsion for every n, hence an isomorphism.
items.note: Siegel-specific. It combines induction on n and the five lemma (Mathlib has the five lemma for abelian categories) with Lemmas 7.4 and 7.6.

items.name: Setting of §7.2: the weight (a,2), the group Δ and the cover X_Δ(Q)
items.statement:
In §7.2:
- μ = (a,2) is a limit of discrete series weight (Definition 5.7, family (a,2;c) with a ∈ Z_{≥2}, so a ≥ 2), and p > a − 2.
- Δ is a quotient of Δ_Q := ∏_{x∈Q}(Z/x)^×.
- X_Δ(Q) → X_0(Q) is the corresponding subcover of X_1(Q) → X_0(Q), i.e. X_Δ(Q) = X_1(Q)/ker(Δ_Q → Δ). It is finite étale and Galois over X_0(Q) with group Δ.
- m is a fixed non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of T_μ(Q), i.e. r̄_m is absolutely irreducible (Definition 6.11, Remark 6.10).
items.note: The intermediate covers X_Δ(Q) = X_1(Q)/ker(Δ_Q → Δ) and limit-of-discrete-series weights are planned nowhere, for the same reasons as sec7-standing-setting.

items.name: Pontryagin duality (implicit convention)
items.statement: For an O-module M, M^∨ := Hom_O(M, K/O). In §7.2 and §9, H^i(…, ·_{K/O})^∨ and H^0(…)^{α,β,∨} denote Pontryagin duals. On vector bundles, L^∨ denotes the dual bundle.
items.note: This follows PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/pontryagin-dual. M^∨ = Hom_O(M, K/O) is the O-linear Pontryagin dual that CC.3 plans. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2 uses the same dual for Selmer groups. Mathlib's CharacterModule (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/CharacterModule.lean: 'def CharacterModule : Type uA := A →+ AddCircle (1 : ℚ)') and its topological PontryaginDual are ℤ-linear near misses; the CC.3 audit (AUDIT-14) rates the target 'partial'.

items.name: Coherent homology H_i(X_Δ(Q), L)
items.statement: For a vector bundle L on X_Δ(Q) and every i, H_i(X_Δ(Q), L) := H^i(X_Δ(Q), (ω^3 ⊗ L^∨(−∞))_{K/O})^∨ (Pontryagin dual).
items.note: Consistent with PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/coherent-homology and homology-H-i, both missing: no layer defines Pontryagin-dual coherent homology on integral models. Its ingredients are the O-linear dual (CC.3, planned) and Tau Ceti's TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology.

items.name: The bundle L = ω(1, 3−a), the identification ω^3 ⊗ L^∨(−∞) ≅ ω(a,2)(−∞), and the Hecke action on H_0
items.statement: Take L = ω(1, 3−a) = Sym^{a−2}E ⊗ det^{3−a}E. Since p > a − 2, (Sym^{a−2})^∨ ≅ Sym^{a−2} ⊗ det^{2−a} as GL2-representations over O (printed: 'as O-modules'). Hence ω^3 ⊗ L^∨(−∞) ≅ ω(a,2)(−∞), and H_0(X_Δ(Q), ω(1,3−a)) = H^0(X_Δ(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O})^∨. Therefore T_μ(Q) acts on H_0(X_Δ(Q), ω(1,3−a)), by transposes via H^0(X_Δ(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O}) ⊂ H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O}).
items.note: The GL2 identity (Sym^{a−2})^∨ ≅ Sym^{a−2} ⊗ det^{2−a} over O needs (a−2)! to be invertible, since Sym^n(V)^∨ is the divided power Γ^n(V^∨); hence the hypothesis p > a−2. The paper prints 'as O-modules' where 'as representations of GL2 over O' is meant (the item notes this). The transposed Hecke action on H_0 is Siegel-specific. Nothing plans either part.

items.name: Assumption 7.7 (vanishing of localised H^2)
items.statement: H^2(X_Δ(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_k)_m = 0. T_μ(Q) does not act on H^2. Localisation at m means localisation at the corresponding maximal ideal of the polynomial ring over O generated by the Hecke operators.
items.locator: §7.2, Assumption 7.7 and the following paragraph, p. 851
items.note: This is a hypothesis on localised Siegel coherent H² and is specific to the paper.

items.name: Remark 7.8 (Assumption 7.7 holds when p ≥ a ≥ 4)
items.statement: If p ≥ a ≥ 4, then H^2(X_Δ(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_k) = 0 even before localisation at m, so Assumption 7.7 holds. This is Theorem 5.1(2) with b = 2 (cf. Corollary 5.8(1)). Theorem 5.1 is stated for X, X_0(Q), X_1(Q), so the same vanishing holds for X_0(Q). For X_Δ(Q), an intermediate cover, the paper applies it without comment; the underlying Lan–Suh theorem holds at any neat level prime to p.
items.note: Checked: Theorem 5.1(2) with b = 2 requires a + 2 ≥ 6 and 2 ≤ a − 2 ≤ p − 2, i.e. 4 ≤ a ≤ p. It then gives vanishing for i > 1, hence H² = 0. No layer plans the Lan–Suh vanishing theorem for coherent cohomology of PEL toroidal compactifications. The paper makes the same observation after Theorem 9.1 (§9, p. 879: 'for p ≥ a ≥ 4, hypothesis (6) holds by Theorem 5.1'). There it gives H²(X_i(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_k) = 0 before localisation, for every Q and for i = 0, 1, so hypothesis (6) of Theorem 9.1 holds. Both uses are Theorem 5.1(2) / Corollary 5.8(1) with b = 2.

items.name: Lemma 7.9 (H_1 is p-torsion free)
items.statement: Suppose Assumption 7.7 holds, i.e. H^2(X_Δ(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_k)_m = 0. Then H_1(X_Δ(Q), ω(1,3−a))_m is p-torsion free. Equivalently, H^1(X_Δ(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O})_m is divisible.
items.note: Once localisation at m is available, this is formal from the long exact sequence of 0 → F_k → F_{K/O} →ϖ F_{K/O} → 0, which Tau Ceti has (exact_cohomologyMap_cohomologyδ). Hecke localisation of integral Siegel coherent cohomology is missing. The GL2 analogue PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/lemma-3-7-1 is also missing.

items.name: Lemma 7.10 (sub and full cohomology agree after localising at non-Eisenstein m)
items.statement: Let μ = (a,2) and m a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of T_μ(Q). For all i, the natural map H^i(X_0(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞))_m ⊗ K → H^i(X_0(Q), ω(a,2))_m ⊗ K is an isomorphism.
items.note: This is the characteristic-zero comparison of subcanonical and full coherent cohomology after localising at a non-Eisenstein m. It rests on the missing boundary vanishing, and nothing plans it.

items.name: Vanishing of localised boundary coherent cohomology
items.statement:
Let ∂X be the boundary of X_0(Q) and m a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of T_μ(Q), with μ = (a,2). Then H^i(∂X, ω(a,2))_m ⊗ K = 0 for all i. Reason given:
- Over C, H^*(∂X, ω(a,2)_C) is computed by the Harris–Zucker nerve spectral sequence, whose E_1-terms are built from the coherent cohomology of Shimura varieties for G_h and the cohomology of local systems for G_ℓ. Here G_h and G_ℓ are products of copies of GL2 and GL1.
- So to every Hecke eigenclass in any H^i(∂X, ω(a,2)_C) one can attach a compatible system of reducible GSp4-valued l-adic representations of G_Q.
- This is impossible for eigenclasses in the m-part, since r̄_m is absolutely irreducible.
items.note: This needs the Harris–Zucker boundary spectral sequence (missing) and Galois representations for the GL2 and GL1 Levi cohomology. ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.4 plans only the Betti boundary ('Describe conditions under which boundary localization vanishes ... by an actual eigenvalue argument'), not coherent boundary cohomology.

items.name: Harris–Zucker: the nerve spectral sequence for boundary coherent cohomology and its E_1-terms
items.note: No stage mentions Harris–Zucker, nerve spectral sequences or coherent cohomology of toroidal boundary strata. B3 stops at the canonical and subcanonical extensions themselves. External input: M. Harris and S. Zucker, Boundary cohomology of Shimura varieties III: Coherent cohomology on higher-rank boundary strata and applications to Hodge theory, Mém. Soc. Math. Fr. (N.S.) 85 (2001) [40], (3.2.4), (3.2.8), Corollary 3.2.9; M. Harris and S. Zucker, Boundary cohomology of Shimura varieties I, Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. (4) 27 (1994) [39], (3.6.1)

items.name: Theorem 7.11 (the Taylor–Wiles-level module is balanced)
items.note: This is the arithmetic balancedness input for defect-one patching. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.5 (reviewed node balanced-modules-and-module-patching, CG Prop. 2.3) plans the patching that consumes it, but not this verification. The GL2 and Bianchi analogues (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 prop-3-8-balanced and prop-5-10) are missing. As the item notes, the proof applies Lemma 7.9 to X_0(Q), which needs Assumption 7.7 for trivial Δ.

items.name: Defect over S = O[Δ] via coinvariants
items.statement: Let Δ be a finite p-group, S = O[Δ] (a local ring with residue field k), and M a finitely generated S-module. Let r be the O-rank of M_Δ = M ⊗_S O. Then d_S(M) = dim_k M ⊗_S k − dim_k Tor_1^S(M,k) = r − dim_k Tor_1^S(M,O)/ϖ. So M is balanced iff r ≥ dim_k Tor_1^S(M,O)/ϖ.
items.note: Consistent with PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/defect-via-coinvariants (missing, source route to R03.5). The R03.5 node defines only d_S(M) = dim_k M/m_S M − dim_k Tor₁^S(M, k). Formula checked: the Tor sequence for 0 → O →ϖ O → k → 0 gives dim Tor₁^S(M,k) = dim Tor₁^S(M,O)/ϖ + dim M_Δ[ϖ], and dim M⊗_S k = r + dim M_Δ[ϖ]. Mathlib has CategoryTheory.Tor, Rep.Tor (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupHomology/Basic.lean) and Representation.Coinvariants, but not this formula.

items.name: Pontryagin-dual Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for X_Δ(Q) → X_0(Q) and its consequences
items.statement:
Let L = ω(1,3−a), S = O[Δ] and M = H_0(X_Δ(Q), L)_m. Pontryagin duality applied to the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence of the Galois cover X_Δ(Q) → X_0(Q) (group Δ) gives a spectral sequence
Tor_i^S(H_j(X_Δ(Q), L)_m, O) ⇒ H_{i+j}(X_0(Q), L)_m,
compatible with the Hecke action. Consequences:
(1) M_Δ ≅ H_0(X_0(Q), L)_m;
(2) there is an exact sequence (H_1(X_Δ(Q), L)_m)_Δ → H_1(X_0(Q), L)_m → Tor_1^S(M, O) → 0.
items.note: The algebraic spectral sequence is planned: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7 ('Prove the spectral sequence Tor_i^A(H^j(C),B) ⇒ H^(j−i)(C⊗ᴸ_A B)'). Not planned: the coherent input, that RΓ(X_Δ(Q), π^*F) is a Hecke-equivariant perfect O[Δ]-complex with derived Δ-coinvariants computing X_0(Q). PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 routed that input (coherent-perfect-complex-C-n) to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes and its weight-one instance (hochschild-serre-coherent) to GL2ModularityLiftingDefectOne. Mathlib has group homology and Rep.Tor but no Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence.

items.name: Reduction of Theorem 7.11 to a characteristic-0 dimension inequality
items.statement:
In the setting of Theorem 7.11 (L = ω(1,3−a), M = H_0(X_Δ(Q), L)_m, S = O[Δ], r = rank_O M_Δ):
(a) If H_1(X_0(Q), L)_m is a free O-module of rank ≤ r, then d_S(M) ≥ 0.
(b) If H_1(X_0(Q), L)_m is p-torsion free (Lemma 7.9 for X_0(Q), i.e. H^2(X_0(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_k)_m = 0), then (a) applies as soon as dim_K H^1(X_0(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞))_m ⊗ K ≤ dim_K H^0(X_0(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞))_m ⊗ K.
(c) By Lemma 7.10, this is equivalent to dim_K H̄^1(X_0(Q), ω(a,2))_m ⊗ K ≤ dim_K H̄^0(X_0(Q), ω(a,2))_m ⊗ K, with H̄ the interior cohomology.
items.note: The reduction itself is elementary O-module algebra, but it is stated for Siegel coherent homology and relies on the missing items above (hochschild-serre-homology, lemma-7-9, lemma-7-10).

items.name: Automorphic description of H̄^i(X_0(Q), ω(a,2)_C)
items.statement:
Fix K ↪ C. By Remark 5.10, ω(a,b) ≅ W_μ ≅ V_σ with μ = (a,b; 3−a−b) = (a,2; 1−a) and σ = (−2, −a; 4−a), under the paper's normalisation of the Hecke action. By Theorem 5.2(2), H̄^i(X_0(Q), ω(a,2)_C) is contained in the image of the L²-cohomology
⊕_{π∈A_(2)(G)} ((π^∞)^{K_0(Q)} ⊗ H^i(Lie P^−, K^h; π_∞ ⊗ V_σ))^{⊕m_(2)(π)},
where m_(2)(π) is the multiplicity of π in A_(2)(G). (The paper prints '⊂'.) By Theorem 5.2(1), the cuspidal cohomology H^i_{cusp,σ} maps injectively onto
H̄^i(X_0(Q), ω(a,2)_C)_cusp ≅ ⊕_{π∈A_0(G)} ((π^∞)^{K_0(Q)} ⊗ H^i(Lie P^−, K^h; π_∞ ⊗ V_σ))^{⊕m_0(π)}.
items.note: This is Harris's description (the paper's Theorem 5.2) of interior coherent cohomology through (Lie P⁻, K^h)-cohomology of L² and cuspidal automorphic forms, specialised to GSp4. AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.5 plans weighted L² comparisons for Betti cohomology only ('ordinary cohomology must not be replaced by cusp or L² cohomology'), and nothing plans Harris's coherent theory.

items.name: Only Arthur's general type (a) contributes to the m-part
items.statement:
Let μ = (a,2) with a ≥ 2, m a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of T_μ(Q), and i ∈ {0,1}. Let π ∈ A_(2)(G) contribute to H̄^i(X_0(Q), ω(a,2))_m ⊗ C (for some K ↪ C), with central character χ_π. Let π̃ be its transfer to GL4(A) under Arthur's Classification Theorem. By Remark 5.12, π̃_∞ has infinitesimal character χ_τ with τ = (0, 0, −(a−1), −(a−1)) + (3/2)(1,1,1,1). Then π̃ is of class (a): a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL4(A) that is χ_π-self-dual. Classes (b)–(f) are excluded:
- (e), (f): π̃ is an isobaric sum of idèle class characters.
- (d): π̃ = λ|·|^{1/2} ⊞ λ|·|^{−1/2} ⊞ μ, with λ an idèle class character, μ cuspidal on GL2(A) and χ_μ = λ² = χ_π. The infinitesimal character forces a = 2 and μ of classical weight 2.
- (c): π̃ = μ|·|^{1/2} ⊞ μ|·|^{−1/2}, with μ cuspidal on GL2(A) of orthogonal type, i.e. induced from a quadratic extension of Q.
- (b): π̃ = μ_1 ⊞ μ_2, with μ_1 ≠ μ_2 cuspidal on GL2(A) and χ_{μ_1} = χ_{μ_2} = χ_π. By the infinitesimal character and the equal central characters, both μ_i come from classical eigenforms of weight a.
In every case (b)–(f) one attaches to π̃ a compatible family of reducible l-adic Galois representations, contradicting that m is non-Eisenstein.
items.note: This is GSp4-specific: it rules out the Arthur types (b)–(f) for non-Eisenstein m. It imports Arthur's classification (missing, see ext-arthur-gsp4-classification) and Galois representations for GL2 forms and Hecke characters. Checked against the p. 854 image.

items.name: Case (a): π_∞ is the limit of discrete series π(λ, C_i) and π is cuspidal
items.note: This chains Clozel's purity lemma, Theorem 5.6(3) (limits of discrete series for GSp4(R)) and Wallach, none of which is planned. Checked against the p. 855 image.

items.name: dim H^1 = dim H^0 for the weight-(a,2) sub-canonical cohomology at level K_0(Q)
items.statement:
Let μ = (a,2) with a ≥ 2 and m a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of T_μ(Q). Then dim_K H^1(X_0(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞))_m ⊗ K = dim_K H^0(X_0(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞))_m ⊗ K.
The result is conditional on Arthur's classification for GSp4 [3], which the paper notes was conditional at submission on the stabilization of the twisted trace formula (see [30]).
items.note: This is the paper's key characteristic-zero numerical coincidence for weight (a,2), and nothing plans it. It inherits the conditionality of Arthur's GSp4 classification. ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.4's acceptance says conditional classification inputs must stay visibly conditional.

items.name: Arthur's classification of the discrete spectrum of GSp4 (as used)
items.note: ML.4 owns classical-group classification inputs, and earlier extractions (PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18, PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20, PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20) marked Arthur's SO and Sp statements planned there. The GSp4 similitude classification (Arthur 2004, proved by Gee–Taïbi 2019) is not among its named sources: 'Selected sources: NEWTON-THORNE, ARTHUR-MOK, EXISTING', with Arthur/Mok/KMSW. Hence missing, by the conservative reading. A reviewer who reads 'Arthur ... classification inputs' as including Arthur's GSp(4) paper could mark it planned in ML.4. PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23/gsp4-llc (GSp4 local Langlands) is also missing. The transfer π̃ is compatible with π at the unramified places and in infinitesimal character at ∞. §1.4 (p. 806) notes that when the paper was first submitted, these results of Arthur for GSp4 were conditional on the stabilization of the twisted trace formula, and refers to [30] (Gee–Taïbi) for their current status. The paper also uses the transfer to GL4 in the proof of Lemma 6.9 (§6.2, p. 840): π̃ descends to an automorphic representation of a unitary group, and [7, Theorem 1.2] then shows that r_f is symplectic. A duplicate item for that transfer had been mapped as planned at ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.4. This item keeps the conservative reading (missing), and the use in Lemma 6.9 gets the same status. External input: J. Arthur, Automorphic representations of GSp(4), in Contributions to Automorphic Forms, Geometry, and Number Theory, Johns Hopkins Univ. Press, 2004, 65–81 [3], Classification Theorem parts (ii), (iii) and §5; proof completed in T. Gee and O. Taïbi, Arthur's multiplicity formula for GSp4 and restriction to Sp4, J. Éc. polytech. Math. 6 (2019), 469–535 [30]

items.name: Clozel's purity lemma (as used)
items.statement: If Π is a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_Q) that is algebraic in Clozel's sense, then Π_∞ is pure: its L-parameter restricted to C^× is ⊕_i z^{p_i} z̄^{q_i} with p_i + q_i independent of i. As applied: π̃ cuspidal on GL4(A), with π̃_∞ of infinitesimal character (3/2, 3/2, 5/2−a, 5/2−a), is essentially tempered.
items.note: No stage mentions Clozel's purity lemma, or temperedness at infinity of algebraic cuspidal GL_n representations. AF.4 owns algebraic weights and the C-algebraic versus L-algebraic distinction, which is the setting of the lemma. The infinitesimal character (3/2, 3/2, 5/2−a, 5/2−a) lies in 3/2 + Z, as Clozel's algebraicity for GL4 requires; regularity is not needed. External input: L. Clozel, Motifs et formes automorphes: applications du principe de fonctorialité, in Automorphic Forms, Shimura Varieties, and L-functions I (Ann Arbor, 1988), Perspect. Math. 10, Academic Press, 1990, 77–159, Lemme 4.9 [19]

items.name: Wallach: square-integrable automorphic forms with tempered archimedean component are cuspidal
items.statement: If π is a square-integrable automorphic representation of G(A) (discrete spectrum modulo the centre) whose archimedean component π_∞ is (essentially) tempered, then π is cuspidal.
items.locator: §7.2, proof of Theorem 7.11, p. 855 (applied to π and to π')
items.note: AS.4 constructs the discrete cuspidal and residual spectrum but does not state Wallach's criterion (tempered archimedean component implies cuspidal). Wallach's paper is cited only through Mok. External input: N. R. Wallach, On the constant term of a square integrable automorphic form (1984); not in the paper's bibliography. Cited via C. P. Mok, Galois representations attached to automorphic forms on GL2 over CM fields, Compos. Math. 150 (2014), 523–567, Theorem 2.3 [55]

items.name: Harris: (Lie P^−, K^h)-cohomology of the limits of discrete series π(λ, C_j)
items.statement: For λ = (a−1, 0; 4−a), σ = (−2, −a; 4−a) and j = 0, 1, H^j(Lie P^−, K^h; π(λ, C_j) ⊗ V_σ) is one-dimensional.
items.note: AF.1 plans (g,K)-cohomology ('Define relative Lie algebra cochains Hom_K(∧^q(g/k),V)'), but not (𝔭⁻, K^h)-cohomology, limits of discrete series or their Harish-Chandra parameters and chambers. External input: M. Harris, Automorphic forms and the cohomology of vector bundles on Shimura varieties, in Automorphic Forms, Shimura Varieties, and L-functions II (Ann Arbor, 1988), Perspect. Math. 11, Academic Press, 1990, 41–91, Theorem 3.4 [37]

items.name: The archimedean Arthur packet of a general-type parameter with limit of discrete series component
items.statement: For ψ = π̃ ⊠ 1 of general type with π_∞ = π(λ, C_i) essentially tempered, the local archimedean Arthur packet Π_{ψ_∞} is an L-packet [55, Theorem 2.1]. It consists of the two representations {π(λ, C_0), π(λ, C_1)} [55, §3.1].
items.note: This concerns archimedean Arthur packets for GSp4 with a limit-of-discrete-series component. ML.4 plans 'packets' only for its Arthur/Mok/KMSW classical-group sources, so it is missing for the same reason as ext-arthur-gsp4-classification. External input: C. P. Mok, Galois representations attached to automorphic forms on GL2 over CM fields, Compos. Math. 150 (2014), 523–567, Theorem 2.1 and §3.1 [55]

items.name: The q-expansion map for Siegel modular forms of weight (j,k)
items.statement:
Let R be an O-module (in practice R = O/ϖ^n or K/O), σ = (j,k) ∈ X*(T)^+_M, U := (Sym^{j−k}(O²) ⊗_O det(O²)^{⊗k}) ⊗_O R (a representation of GL2 over R), and W_σ = ω(j,k).
There is a q-expansion map from H^0(Y_1(Q), ω(j,k)_R) to formal sums Σ_{Q∈𝒳} a(Q)q^Q with a(Q) ∈ U. For L = 1 the target is R[ζ,ζ^{−1}][[q,q′]] ⊗_R U; fractional exponents with bounded powers of L in the denominators are allowed in general. The paper prints R[[q,q′,ζ]][ζ^{−1}] ⊗_R U, which does not contain the expansions [sourceIssues E84]. The map is taken at a cusp of each connected component of Y_1(Q) [sourceIssues E85].
items.note: B5 plans 'q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps and Fourier–Jacobi expansions at the relevant higher-dimensional boundary components', in characteristic zero. Siegel q-expansions at 0-dimensional cusps with coefficients in R = O/ϖ^n or K/O are not named. Integral q/Fourier–Jacobi principles are planned only for unitary groups (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4, EHLS). Tau Ceti's qExpansion declarations are for analytic GL2 forms only. Explicitly (§8.2, p. 857), F ↦ Σ_{n,m≥0} Σ_{r² ≤ 4mn} a_F(n,r,m) q^n ζ^r q′^m. The relevant atlas stage is AutomorphicBundles:B5.

items.name: Standing setup of §8: levels, Siegel 3-folds and automorphic bundles ω(a,b)
items.statement: Fix a prime p, a finite extension K/Q_p with ring of integers O, uniformizer ϖ and residue field O/ϖ. Let S and Q be finite sets of primes of Q, disjoint from each other and not containing p (Q = ∅ is allowed). K = ∏_x K_x ⊂ GSp4(A^∞) is a neat open compact subgroup with K_x = GSp4(Z_x) for x ∉ S (and K_x for x ∈ S one of the groups listed in §5.2). K_i(Q) = ∏_{x∉Q} K_x × ∏_{x∈Q} K_{x,i} for i = 0, 1, where K_{x,0} = Π(x) and K_{x,1} = Π(x)^+. Y = Y_K and Y_i(Q) = Y_{K_i(Q)} are the Siegel 3-folds over O (moduli of principally polarized abelian surfaces with level structure), and X = X_K, X_i(Q) = X_{K_i(Q)} are chosen smooth projective toroidal compactifications over O. With E = π_*Ω¹ of the semi-abelian scheme over X, ω := det E, and for integers a ≥ b, ω(a,b) := Sym^{a−b}E ⊗ det^b E and ω(a,b)_M := ω(a,b) ⊗_O M for an O-module M. The groups H^i(X, ω(a,b)_M) do not depend on the toroidal compactification. By the Koecher principle H^0(Y, ω(a,b)_M) ≅ H^0(X, ω(a,b)_M). Y_1(Q) has good reduction at p. X_1(Q) has good reduction outside L, the product of the primes in S ∪ Q.
items.locator: §8, opening paragraph, p. 856; §8.1–8.2, p. 856 (good reduction); recalled from §5.2, pp. 821–822
items.note: The objects are planned: the Siegel 3-folds over O with good reduction at p (M5, M2), the smooth projective integral toroidal compactifications with their semi-abelian scheme (C5), the bundles E, ω = det E and ω(a,b) = Sym^{a−b}E ⊗ det^b E (B4), independence of H^0 from the fan (B3), and independence of higher H^i through the higher-direct-image theorem C3 asks for. Neat levels are in D5. One part is not planned anywhere: the Koecher principle H^0(Y, ω(a,b)_M) ≅ H^0(X, ω(a,b)_M) for Siegel 3-folds with M = O/ϖ^n or K/O. The atlas plans Koecher only for Hilbert sections (C6: 'For g>1, prove the precise Koecher extension theorem needed for Hilbert sections'), and V2 mentions it only as a caveat. It should go into C5, next to the integral minimal compactification. The levels Π(x) and Π(x)^+ at x ∈ Q belong to the §5.2 items of another cluster. The §7 opening (p. 846, 'As in Section 5.2 …') states the same setting almost word for word. Three facts it recalls are recorded elsewhere: the universal subgroup H ⊂ A[Q] and the cover X_1(Q) = Isom(Z/Q, H) with group Δ_Q are in compatible-compactifications-K0Q and X-K1Q-Delta-Q-cover, and Π(x)/Π(x)^+ ≅ (Z/x)^× is in klingen-plus-subgroup.

items.name: The coefficient representation U of a weight σ = (j,k)
items.statement: For a weight σ = (j,k) ∈ X*(T)^+_M (integers j ≥ k) and an O-module R, U := (Sym^{j−k}(O²) ⊗_O det(O²)^{⊗k}) ⊗_O R, a representation of GL2 over R. In §8, R is always O/ϖ^n for some n, or K/O. The associated vector bundle is W_σ = ω(j,k). Restricted to SL2(Z), U = Sym^{j−k}(V) ⊗ R, where V = O² is the standard representation of SL2(Z) over O. ρ: SL2(Z) → GL(U) denotes this representation.
items.note: The representation is in the library. For R = O/ϖ^n, U is `tprod (symPowerRep R 2 (j−k)) (detPowerRep R 2 k)`. For R = K/O, which is not a ring, it is the O-representation tensored with the trivial action on K/O. Restriction to SL2(Z) goes through `SpecialLinearGroup.map (Int.castRingHom R)` and `toGL`, where the det-twist is trivial. The associated bundle W_σ = ω(j,k) is AutomorphicBundles:B4, which is planned.

items.name: Extension of ρ to the monoid M2(Z)
items.statement: The representation ρ: SL2(Z) → GL(U), U = Sym^{j−k}(V) ⊗ R, extends to a multiplicative map ρ: M2(Z) → End_R(U), M ↦ Sym^{j−k}(M) ⊗ R. This extension depends only on j − k and preserves integrality: it is defined over O.
items.note: The multiplicative map M ↦ Sym^{j−k}(M) on the monoid M2(Z) is `Representation.symmetricPower (j−k)` applied to the monoid representation M ↦ toLinAlgEquiv'((Int.castRingHom R).mapMatrix M) of M2(Z) on R². Multiplicativity is SymmetricPower.map_comp. The map depends only on j − k by construction. It is integral because it is defined over Z (or O) and base-changed.

items.name: Theorem 8.1: q-expansion principle for Siegel modular forms
items.statement: For σ = (j,k) and R = O/ϖ^n or K/O, a section F ∈ H^0(Y_1(Q), ω(j,k)_R) is determined by its q-expansions, in R[ζ,ζ^{−1}][[q,q′]] ⊗_R U, at one cusp on each geometric connected component of Y_1(Q) (after adjoining the needed roots of unity). That is, the q-expansion map to the product over these cusps is injective. It is injective at a single cusp only when Y_1(Q) is geometrically connected [sourceIssues E85]. By the Koecher principle the same holds on X_1(Q). (Paper: Theorem 8.1, citing [67, Proposition 3.2].)
items.note: The Siegel q-expansion principle over O/ϖ^n and K/O (Tilouine [67, Prop. 3.2]; Faltings–Chai V.1) is not planned. Its proof needs irreducibility of the fibres of the components and the formal completion at a cusp (C5). The addendum 'the same holds on X_1(Q)' also needs the Koecher principle for Siegel 3-folds, which is unplanned (see section-8-standing-setup). External input: Tilouine [67, Proposition 3.2]

items.name: Fourier coefficients a(F,Q) indexed by binary quadratic forms
items.statement: Let L be the product of the primes in S ∪ Q, and let R be a Z_p-module, hence a Z[1/L]-module [printed 'Z[1/L]-algebra'; sourceIssues E86]. Let 𝒳 be the set of 2×2 positive semidefinite symmetric matrices Q = (m, r/2; r/2, n) with m, n, r ∈ Z[1/L], equivalently the positive semidefinite matrices taking Z[1/L]-integral values on integral vectors. 𝒳 ⊂ M2(Q). Each F ∈ H^0(X_1(Q), W_{σ,R}) has a q-expansion F = Σ_{Q∈𝒳} a(F,Q) q^Q with a(F,Q) ∈ U = Sym^{j−k}(V) ⊗ R. Set a(F,Q) = 0 for Q ∈ M2(Q) \ 𝒳. The coefficients vanish unless the denominators of Q are bounded by a fixed power of L depending only on the level. In the notation a_F(n,r,m) := a(F,Q), F = Σ_{n,m≥0, r²−4mn≤0} a_F(n,r,m) q^n ζ^r q′^m. The associated binary quadratic form is mx² + rxy + ny², with discriminant r² − 4mn = −4 det Q.
items.note: This is part of the unplanned Siegel q-expansion (see siegel-q-expansion-map): indexing by 2×2 positive semidefinite half-integral matrices with Z[1/L] entries, bounded denominators, and the dictionary a_F(n,r,m) = a(F,Q) with discriminant r² − 4mn = −4 det Q. The printed text (p. 856) calls R 'thus a Z[1/L]-algebra'. Since p ∤ L, a Z_p-module is only a Z[1/L]-module, and K/O, one of the R of interest, is not a ring [sourceIssues E86]. The printed 'or equivalently' description of 𝒳, as all (m, ½r; ½r, n) with m, n, r ∈ Z[1/L], leaves out positive semidefiniteness (m, n ≥ 0, r² − 4mn ≤ 0). The first half of the same sentence says 'positive semidefinite', and the q-expansion on p. 857 sums only over such matrices [sourceIssues E87].

items.name: The action M.Q = (det M)^{−1} M Q M^T
items.statement: GL2(Q) acts on M2(Q) by M.Q := (det M)^{−1} M Q M^T (right-hand side a product of matrices). The action is linear in Q and is a left action: (AB).Q = A.(B.Q). It preserves determinants, det(M.Q) = det Q, and M^{−1}.Q = det(M) M^{−1} Q M^{−T}.
items.note: The action is elementary: linear in Q, a left action, and determinant-preserving. The twisted action itself is not in either library and no layer plans it.

items.name: Equivariance of Fourier coefficients under Γ̄
items.statement: For F ∈ H^0(X_1(Q), W_{σ,R}), every Q ∈ M2(Q) and every M ∈ Γ̄ ⊂ SL2(Z): a(F, M.Q) = ρ(M) a(F,Q). Here Γ̄ is the congruence subgroup of SL2(Z) defined in [67, p. 807]. Because the level is spherical at p, Γ̄ has level prime to p, and hence it surjects onto SL2(F_p).
items.locator: §8.2, p. 857; surjectivity onto SL2(F_p): §8.4, proof of Theorem 8.11, p. 862
items.note: The equivariance a(F, M.Q) = ρ(M)a(F,Q) for M ∈ Γ̄ belongs to the unplanned Siegel q-expansion. Γ̄ is Tilouine's congruence subgroup [67, p. 807], of level prime to p. That its reduction mod p is all of SL2(F_p) is strong approximation for SL2 (surjectivity of SL2(Z) → SL2(Z/N)); it is not recorded for this Γ̄ in either library. External input: Tilouine [67, p. 807] (definition of Γ̄)

items.name: Remark 8.2: standing assumption on weights and Nebentypus
items.statement: Throughout §8 the weight σ = (j,k) satisfies either j ≥ 4 or j = k = 2. The motivation: for representations with similitude character ν = ε^{j+k−3} (ε the cyclotomic character), oddness forces j ≡ k mod 2, so j > k ≥ 2 implies j ≥ 4. When the auxiliary primes q | Q (Taylor–Wiles primes) carry a nontrivial Nebentypus, twisting makes it trivial, at the cost of increasing the level at Q. All q-expansion formulas are therefore written with trivial Nebentypus. Weight (j,k) = (3,2), which is possible with nontrivial Nebentypus, is not covered.
items.note: This is a convention of §8: j ≥ 4 or j = k = 2, trivial Nebentypus after twisting at Taylor–Wiles primes, and weight (3,2) excluded. The parity argument uses oddness of ν = ε^{j+k−3}. No layer records the convention. It belongs in the brief of the layer that hosts §8.

items.name: Notation for the Hecke operators at p in §8
items.statement: In §8 the subscript p is dropped. T := T_{p,1} = [K β_{p,1} K] with β_{p,1} = diag(1,1,p,p); T2 := T_{p,2} = [K β_{p,2} K] with β_{p,2} = diag(1,p,p,p²); S := S_p = T_{p,0} = [K β_{p,0} K] with β_{p,0} = diag(p,p,p,p). The Hecke action is normalized as in §5.5 and Remark 5.10. U := U_{p,1} and U2 := U_{p,2} denote the formal operators on q-expansions given explicitly in Lemmas 8.3 and 8.4.
items.locator: §8.3, p. 858; matrices and normalization from §5.5, p. 833, and Remark 5.10, p. 833
items.note: The double cosets [Kβ_{p,i}K] of GSp4(Q_p) and their characteristic-zero action on Siegel forms are planned (SR.4, RG2.4, B5). Two things are not. First, the operators T, T2, S with the paper's normalization (§5.5, Remark 5.10) acting on H^0 with O/ϖ^m or K/O coefficients; that is Lemma 8.8. Second, the formal q-expansion operators U and U2.

items.name: The coset representatives 𝒮 for Γ̄ diag(p,1) Γ̄
items.statement: 𝒮 denotes any set of representatives in M2(Z) for the left cosets MΓ̄ contained in the double coset Γ̄ (p 0; 0 1) Γ̄, normalized to be integral of determinant p. Because Γ̄ has level prime to p, this coset decomposition is essentially that of SL2(Z)(p 0; 0 1)SL2(Z), which has p + 1 cosets.
items.locator: §8.3, Lemma 8.3 and the paragraph after it, p. 858
items.note: Only partly covered, so marked missing. Tau Ceti has the p+1 coset representatives of diag(1,p) for SL2(Z), Γ0(N) and Γ1(N) with p ∤ N. It does not have them for Tilouine's Γ̄ [67, p. 807], which is not pinned down and may be of principal-congruence type. The paper uses left cosets MΓ̄ of integral matrices of determinant p, which is the transpose of Tau Ceti's right-coset form. The reduction 'essentially that of SL2(Z)' for level prime to p is not proved in either library.

items.name: Lemma 8.3: T = U + p^{k−2}Z + p^{k+j−3}V on q-expansions
items.statement: In weight σ = (j,k) there is an identity of formal operators on q-expansions T = U + p^{k−2}Z + p^{k+j−3}V, where U, Z and V preserve formal integral q-expansions and a(UF,Q) = a(F,pQ), a(ZF,Q) = Σ_{M∈𝒮} ρ(M) a(F, M^{−1}.Q). Moreover, for M ∈ 𝒮, a(F, M^{−1}.Q) = 0 unless M^{−1}.Q is a p-integral binary quadratic form.
items.note: The action of T_{p,1} on Siegel Fourier coefficients, with integrality of U, Z and V, is planned nowhere. It is known in characteristic zero (Cléry–van der Geer, Prop. 10.2), and the paper renormalizes 𝒮 to integral matrices. External input: F. Cléry and G. van der Geer, Constructing vector-valued Siegel modular forms from scalar-valued Siegel modular forms, Pure Appl. Math. Q. 11 (2015), 21–47, Prop. 10.2 ([18]); the paper renormalizes 𝒮 to integral matrices of determinant p and absorbs the determinant into the coefficient

items.name: Lemma 8.4 (i): T2 = p^{k+j−6}U2 + p^{k−3}Z2 + p^{2k+j−6}V2 and the formula for Z2
items.statement: In weight σ = (j,k) there is an identity of formal operators on q-expansions T2 = p^{k+j−6}U2 + p^{k−3}Z2 + p^{2k+j−6}V2, where U2, Z2 and V2 preserve formal integral q-expansions and a(Z2F,Q) = Σ_{M∈𝒮} ρ(M) a(F, M^{−1}.pQ), with 𝒮 as in Lemma 8.3.
items.note: The decomposition of T_{p,2} on Siegel q-expansions (following Andrianov, Quadratic Forms and Hecke Operators, §§3.2–3.3) is planned nowhere and is not in either library. External input: Obtained 'by a laborious computation (following the arguments of [2, Sections 3.2 and 3.3])': A. N. Andrianov, Quadratic Forms and Hecke Operators, Grundlehren 286, Springer 1987

items.name: Lemma 8.4 (ii): U2 acts diagonally by −1 + p·(disc/p)
items.statement: The operator U2 of Lemma 8.4 is diagonal on q-expansions. For Q = (m, r/2; r/2, n): if Q ≢ 0 mod p, then a(U2F,Q) = (−1 + p·((r² − 4mn)/p)) a(F,Q), where (·/p) is the Legendre symbol and r² − 4mn = −4 det Q is the discriminant. If Q ≡ 0 mod p, then a(U2F,Q) = (−1 + p²) a(F,Q).
items.note: The diagonal formula for U2 is a Siegel-specific Hecke computation and is planned nowhere.

items.name: Explicit formulas for Z and Z2 in parallel weight (k,k)
items.statement: In weight (k,k), where ρ is trivial, write a(F,n,r,m) := a_F(n,r,m). Then a(ZF,n,r,m) = a(F, pn, r, m/p) + Σ_{0≤α<p} a(F, (n+αr+α²m)/p, r+2mα, pm), and a(Z2F,n,r,m) = a(F, p²n, pr, m) + Σ_{0≤α<p} a(F, n+αr+α²m, p(r+2mα), p²m).
items.note: These are the explicit scalar-weight forms of Z and Z2 as sums over α mod p. They are not in either library and planned nowhere.

items.name: Formal identity Z2 = UZ (= ZU)
items.statement: As operators on formal q-expansions, Z2 = UZ: a(Z2F,Q) = a(ZF,pQ) = Σ_{M∈𝒮} ρ(M) a(F, M^{−1}.pQ). Moreover U and Z2 commute formally (UZ2 = Z2U), since M^{−1}.pQ = adj(M) Q adj(M)^T is p-integral for every M ∈ 𝒮. In general Z2 ≠ ZU, because a(UF,R) = 0 for non-p-integral R while a(F,pR) need not vanish.
items.note: This is an elementary identity of formal operators, from M^{−1}.(pQ) = p(M^{−1}.Q). It depends on the unplanned operators U, Z and Z2.

items.name: Definition 8.5: the operator X2 with U2 = −1 + p·X2
items.statement: X2 is the formal operator on q-expansions with U2 = −1 + p·X2. Explicitly, if Q ≢ 0 mod p, then a(X2F,Q) = (D/p) a(F,Q), where D = r² − 4mn is the discriminant of the binary quadratic form associated to Q. The paper calls D 'the determinant of the quadratic form'; in Gauss's sense of b² − ac this gives the same Legendre symbol, but the matrix determinant mn − r²/4 does not. If Q ≡ 0 mod p, then a(X2F,Q) = p·a(F,Q). In all cases a(X2F,Q) ≡ (D/p) a(F,Q) mod p, and X2 preserves integral q-expansions.
items.note: X2 is a formal operator on Siegel q-expansions, planned nowhere. The item uses the corrected reading, with D the discriminant r² − 4mn.

items.name: Lemma 8.6: Z2X2 = 0 over O/ϖ
items.statement: Over O/ϖ, Z2 ∘ X2 = 0 as formal operators on q-expansions. The reason: a(X2G,R) ≡ 0 mod p whenever det(R) ≡ 0 mod p, and a(Z2F,Q) = Σ_{M∈𝒮} ρ(M) a(F, R_M) with R_M = M^{−1}.pQ, whose determinant is det(R_M) = p² det(Q) ≡ 0 mod p.
items.note: This formal identity mod p depends on the unplanned Z2 and X2.

items.name: Definition 8.7: p-primitive binary quadratic form
items.statement: A (p-integral) binary quadratic form Q is p-primitive if it is not of the form pR for a p-integral form R.
items.note: An elementary definition, found in neither library. Mathlib has QuadraticForm but no p-primitivity predicate for binary forms.

items.name: Construction of Hecke operators at p on H^0 via the p-rank ≥ 1 locus and Hartogs
items.statement: Over O/ϖ^m, the projections from the Siegel 3-folds with the appropriate parahoric level at p to X are proper but not finite, so the failure of finiteness is a failure of quasi-finiteness. It comes from abelian surfaces with 'too many' subgroup schemes of type α_p, for example those with Ker F ≅ α_p × α_p. This does not occur on the open X′ ⊂ X of abelian surfaces of p-rank ≥ 1 (ordinary or almost ordinary), where the correspondences are finite. The complement of X′ is the supersingular locus, of codimension 2. By Hartogs's lemma, H^0(X, ω(j,k)_{O/ϖ^m}) = H^0(X′, ω(j,k)_{O/ϖ^m}), so T and Q2 can be defined on H^0 through the finite correspondences over X′. The correspondence gives a power of p times the desired operator, and the q-expansion principle fixes the normalization. Integrality of the q-expansion formulas (Lemmas 8.3, 8.4) is implicit, and for Q2 it is checked in Lemma 8.12. Pilloni [56] gives a general construction.
items.note: The construction needs four things that are planned nowhere: (1) the p-rank stratification of the Siegel 3-fold mod p; (2) codimension 2 of the supersingular locus; (3) algebraic Hartogs, i.e. extension of sections of a vector bundle across codimension ≥ 2 on a normal Noetherian scheme; (4) the Siegel and Klingen parahoric-level Hecke correspondences at p over O/ϖ^m, finite over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus, normalized by the q-expansion principle. Pilloni (Crelle 2012) is an alternative source. External input: B. H. Gross, A tameness criterion for Galois representations associated to modular forms (mod p), Duke Math. J. 61 (1990), 445–517, Prop. 4.1 ([35]; the analogous argument for modular curves). V. Pilloni, Modularité, formes de Siegel et surfaces abéliennes, J. Reine Angew. Math. 666 (2012), 35–82 ([56]; constructs all these operators, also on higher coherent cohomology)

items.name: Lemma 8.8: T and Q2 act on H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j,k)_{K/O})
items.statement: For σ = (j,k) with j ≥ k ≥ 2 (the standing assumptions of §8), the operators T and Q2 act on H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j,k)_{K/O}). They commute with the other Hecke operators and act on q-expansions by the formulas of Lemmas 8.3 and 8.4: T = U + p^{k−2}Z + p^{k+j−3}V and Q2 = (p·T2 + (p+p³)S)p^{2−k}. It suffices to construct them with coefficients O/ϖ^m.
items.note: T and Q2 on H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j,k)_{K/O}) need the construction of the previous item and the Siegel q-expansion formulas, both missing. B5 plans Hecke correspondences in characteristic zero only. External input: Gross [35, Prop. 4.1] (analogous argument); Pilloni [56] (alternative general construction)

items.name: The contraction con: Sym^{j−k} ⊗ Sym² → Sym^{j−k−2}
items.statement: For j − k ≥ 2, con: Sym^{j−k} ⊗ Sym² → Sym^{j−k−2} is the natural SL2(Z)-equivariant projection (contraction). As a GL2-equivariant map its target is Sym^{j−k−2} ⊗ det² (for Sym² of the standard representation); equivalently, Sym^{j−k}V ⊗ Sym²V^∨ → Sym^{j−k−2}V untwisted, which is the form used on p. 876 with Q^∨. This matches the weight shift of θ1. It is defined integrally over Z_(p) under the hypothesis p − 2 > j − k of Prop. 8.9; p. 876 asserts integrality for k = 2 as soon as p > j − 2. p. 876 prints the target as Sym^{j−4} ⊗ det.
