items.locator: §8.4, Proposition 8.9(2), p. 861; §8.9, Proposition 8.25 and its proof, pp. 876–877
items.note: Tau Ceti's Clebsch–Gordan is for the Lie algebra over a characteristic-zero field. It gives neither the SL2(Z)-equivariant contraction Sym^{j−k} ⊗ Sym² → Sym^{j−k−2} nor its integrality over Z_(p) for p − 2 > j − k.

items.name: Proposition 8.9(1): the theta operator Θ on parallel weight (mod p)
items.statement: Let p > 3 and k ≥ 2. There is a map Θ: H^0(X_1(Q), ω(k,k)_{O/ϖ}) → H^0(X_1(Q), ω(k+p+1, k+p+1)_{O/ϖ}) whose effect on q-expansions is Θ(Σ a_Q q^Q) = Σ det(Q) a_Q q^Q, up to a nonzero constant. The printed statement has coefficients O/ϖ^m [sourceIssues E96].
items.note: Yamauchi's mod p theta operator Θ on Siegel forms of parallel weight (arXiv:1410.7894v5, Prop. 3.9) is planned nowhere. Yamauchi should be listed as a prerequisite. External input: T. Yamauchi, The weight reduction of mod p Siegel modular forms for GSp4, arXiv:1410.7894v5 (Aug. 2016), Prop. 3.9 ([75])

items.name: Proposition 8.9(2): the theta operator θ1 lowering the symmetric degree by 2 (mod p)
items.statement: Let p > 3, j − 2 ≥ k ≥ 2 and p − 2 > j − k. There is a map θ1: H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j,k)_{O/ϖ}) → H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j+p−1, k+p+1)_{O/ϖ}) whose effect on q-expansions is θ1(Σ a_Q q^Q) = Σ con(a_Q ⊗ Q) q^Q, up to a p-adic unit. Here con: Sym^{j−k} ⊗ Sym² → Sym^{j−k−2} is the natural SL2(Z)-equivariant projection. The printed formula has an extra factor det(Q) [sourceIssues E95], and the printed coefficients are O/ϖ^m [sourceIssues E96].
items.note: Yamauchi's θ1 (arXiv:1410.7894v5, Prop. 3.12) is planned nowhere. It needs the contraction map con, which is also missing. External input: Yamauchi [75, Prop. 3.12] (arXiv:1410.7894v5): θ1 = H_{p−1}·θ̃1, M_{(k1,k2)} → M_{(k1+p−1, k2+p+1)}, defined for p > k1 − k2 + 2

items.name: Yamauchi: Θ(F) ≠ 0 if F is nonzero on the superspecial locus and p ∤ k(2k−1)
items.statement: Let p ≥ 5, N ≥ 3 prime to p, and let F ∈ M_{(k,k)}(Γ(N), F̄_p) be a mod p Siegel modular form of degree 2 and parallel weight k ≥ 2 that is not identically zero on the superspecial locus S_(0,0). If p ∤ k(2k − 1), then Θ(F) is not identically zero. More precisely, at a superspecial point X with F(X) = α ≠ 0, Θ(F)(X) ≡ k(2k−1)α/9 modulo the maximal ideal of the complete local ring. Also, if p ∤ k, then θ(F) ≠ 0.
items.locator: used in §8.4, proof of Theorem 8.10, p. 862 (cited as [75, Theorem 4.7])
items.note: This is an external input (Yamauchi, arXiv:1410.7894v5, Thm. 4.7) planned nowhere. It needs superspecial points of the Siegel 3-fold and a local computation of Θ in a frame of E. Add Yamauchi as a prerequisite. External input: Yamauchi [75], arXiv:1410.7894v5, Theorem 4.7 (Theorem 3.18 in v1–v3)

items.name: Koblitz: the supersingular locus is a Cartier divisor in the p-rank ≤ 1 locus, cut out by a section of ω^{(p²−1)/2}
items.statement: For p > 2, inside the non-ordinary (p-rank ≤ 1) locus Y of the Siegel 3-fold X over O/ϖ, the supersingular locus Z is a Cartier divisor cut out by a section of ω^{(p²−1)/2}. Hence, for a vector bundle W on X and m = (p²−1)/2, there is an exact sequence 0 → H^0(Y, W ⊗ ω^{−m}) → H^0(Y, W) → H^0(Z, W).
items.locator: used in §8.4, proofs of Theorem 8.10 (p. 862) and Theorem 8.11 (pp. 862–863)
items.note: Koblitz (Compos. Math. 1975, p. 193) and van der Geer (1999, Thm. 2.4) are planned nowhere. So are the p-rank strata of A_2 mod p and the section of ω^{(p²−1)/2} cutting out the supersingular locus. External input: N. Koblitz, p-adic variation of the zeta-function over families of varieties defined over finite fields, Compos. Math. 31 (1975), 119–218, p. 193 ([50]). Exact order of vanishing: G. van der Geer, Cycles on the moduli space of abelian varieties, Aspects Math. E33 (1999), 65–89, Theorem 2.4 ([70])

items.name: Supersingular components are P¹'s with p²+1 superspecial points; E|_{P¹} ≅ O(−1) ⊕ O(p)
items.statement: Each irreducible component of the supersingular locus Z of X ⊗ O/ϖ (principal polarization, level prime to p) is isomorphic to P¹ and contains exactly p² + 1 superspecial points. The Hodge bundle E restricts to O(−1) ⊕ O(p) on each such P¹, so ω = det E restricts to O(p − 1).
items.locator: used in §8.4, proof of Theorem 8.10 (p. 862) and proof of Theorem 8.11 (p. 863)
items.note: The components of the supersingular locus of A_2 mod p (level prime to p) are P¹'s with p²+1 superspecial points, and E restricted to each is O(−1) ⊕ O(p). This comes from Katsura–Oort / Moret-Bailly, is planned nowhere, and the paper gives no citation. External input: Standard; the paper gives no citation (Moret-Bailly families; T. Katsura and F. Oort, Families of supersingular abelian surfaces, Compositio Math. 62 (1987), 107–167)

items.name: Vanishing of H^0 in weights with negative entries (used without proof)
items.statement: The proofs of Theorems 8.10 and 8.11 use three vanishing statements over O/ϖ. (a) H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j,2)_{O/ϖ} ⊗ ω^{−m}) = H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j−m, 2−m)_{O/ϖ}) = 0 for m = (p²−1)/2 and 4 ≤ j < p − 1 ('The first term vanishes', p. 863). (b) A nonzero F ∈ H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j,2)_{O/ϖ}), 4 ≤ j < p − 1, is not divisible by the Hasse invariant, i.e. H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j−p+1, 3−p)_{O/ϖ}) = 0 (needed for 'We are assuming that the restriction of F to Y is nonzero', p. 862). (c) Sections of ω^{k−(p²−1)/2} with 2k < p² − 1 on the non-ordinary locus vanish (proof of Theorem 8.10, p. 862).
items.note: These are the vanishing statements the paper uses without proof (a gap the extraction flags): H^0 of ω(a,b) over O/ϖ vanishes when b is negative, including sections over the non-ordinary locus. They are planned nowhere.

items.name: Theorem 8.10: Θ is injective in parallel weight 2 ≤ k ≤ p+1, k ≠ p−1, p ∤ k(2k−1)
items.statement: Let p > 3 and let k be an integer with 2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1, k ≠ p − 1, and p ∤ k(2k − 1). In particular k = 2 and k = p + 1 are admissible. Then Θ: H^0(X_1(Q), ω(k,k)_{O/ϖ}) → H^0(X_1(Q), ω(k+p+1, k+p+1)_{O/ϖ}) is injective: if ΘF = 0 then F = 0.
items.note: This depends on Θ, Yamauchi's Thm. 4.7, Koblitz, the P¹-components, the Hasse invariant and negative-weight vanishing, all missing. The item uses the corrected hypothesis k ≠ p − 1.

items.name: Yamauchi: θ1(F) ≠ 0 if F is nonzero on the superspecial locus and k1 ≢ 3k2 mod p
items.statement: Let p ≥ 5 and let (k1,k2) be a weight with r := k1 − k2 > 1 and p > r. Let F ∈ M_{(k1,k2)}(Γ(N), F̄_p) be not identically zero on the superspecial locus. If k1 − 3k2 ≢ 0 mod p, then θ1(F) is not identically zero. Moreover, at a superspecial point X, in a local frame of E, the relevant component of θ1(F) is −((k1−3k2)/2)t11F0|_X − ((k1−3k2)/2)t12F1|_X − (k1−3)t22F2|_X modulo m_R². So when k1 = 3k2 the conclusion still holds provided F2|_X ≠ 0 and p ∤ k1 − 3.
items.locator: used in §8.4, proof of Theorem 8.11, p. 862 (cited as [75, Theorem 3.20])
items.note: This is an external input (Yamauchi, arXiv:1410.7894v5, Thm. 4.9 = Thm. 3.20 in v1–v3) planned nowhere. Add Yamauchi as a prerequisite. External input: Yamauchi [75], arXiv:1410.7894v5, Theorem 4.9 (Theorem 3.20 in v1–v3; the paper's bibliography cites v5)

items.name: Theorem 8.11: θ1 is injective on weight (j,2) for 4 ≤ j < p − 1
items.statement: Let p − 1 > j ≥ 4 (so p ≥ 7). Then the map θ1: H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j,2)_{O/ϖ}) → H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j+p−1, p+3)_{O/ϖ}) of Proposition 8.9(2), with k = 2, is injective.
items.note: This depends on θ1, Yamauchi's Thm. 4.9, Koblitz, Serre duality, Lan–Suh vanishing and the P¹-components, all missing.

items.name: Hecke polynomial at p and crystalline Frobenius; Q2 ≡ αβ (§8.5)
items.statement: Let F be a cuspidal eigenform of weight σ = (j,k), level prime to p, with T-eigenvalue λ, T2-eigenvalue μ and Galois representation r. It is expected, and known in regular weights (Theorem 6.13), that r is crystalline at p with Frobenius characteristic polynomial X⁴ − λX³ + (pμ + (p³+p)p^{k+j−6})X² − λp^{k+j−3}X + p^{2k+2j−6}. The X²-coefficient is the eigenvalue of p^{k−2}Q2 = p·T2 + (p+p³)S. Newton above Hodge gives it valuation ≥ k−2, so the eigenvalues of Q2 are integral. Write the roots as α, βp^{k−2}, β^{−1}p^{j−1}, α^{−1}p^{k+j−3}. Then the X²-coefficient is αβp^{k−2} + αβ^{−1}p^{j−1} + 2p^{k+j−3} + α^{−1}βp^{2k+j−5} + (αβ)^{−1}p^{k+2j−4}. If α and β are p-adic units (the ordinary case), this is αβp^{k−2} + O(p^{k−1}), so the Q2-eigenvalue is ≡ αβ mod p. Nonnegativity of v_p(α) and v_p(β) alone does not suffice.
items.note: No layer plans the GSp4 spin Hecke polynomial at p or the Galois representation of a Siegel eigenform with its crystalline Frobenius, and neither library has them. The item depends on Theorem 6.13 (another cluster). External input: Known cases: Theorem 6.13 of the paper (ordinary, regular weight)

items.name: Lemma 8.12 (i): Q2 ≡ Z2 mod p for (j,k) ≠ (2,2)
items.statement: Let σ = (j,k) with j ≥ k ≥ 2 and (j,k) ≠ (2,2). Then, as operators on formal q-expansions, Q2 = (p·T2 + (p+p³)S)p^{2−k} ≡ Z2 mod p. In particular, if F is an ordinary form of regular weight σ whose crystalline Frobenius eigenvalues are as in §8.5, the eigenvalue of Z2 on F is ≡ αβ mod p.
items.note: This congruence of formal operators rests on Lemma 8.4 and on S acting by a scalar, both missing.

items.name: Lemma 8.12 (ii): in weight (2,2), Q2 ≡ Z2 + X2 mod p
items.statement: If σ = (2,2), then as operators on formal q-expansions Q2 = (p·T2 + (p+p³)S) ≡ Z2 + X2 mod p.
items.note: This is the weight-(2,2) case of the same congruence, rests on the same missing inputs, and is planned nowhere.

items.name: Theorem 8.13: injectivity of H^0(ω(j,2))^{α,β}_m → (×A) → π_β (the main theorem on q-expansions)
items.statement: Let σ = (j,2) with p − 1 > j ≥ 2; by the standing assumption of Remark 8.2, j = 2 or j ≥ 4. Assume r̄: G_Q → GSp4(O/ϖ) satisfies Assumption 6.16: (1) r̄ is Katz modular of weight σ with associated maximal ideal m_∅ and eigenform η. That is, r̄_{m_∅} ≅ r̄, and there is η ∈ H^0(X, ω(j,2)_{K/O})[m_∅] with T_{p,1}η = (α+β)η and Q_{p,2}η = αβη, where α, β ∈ (O/ϖ)^× are attached to r̄|G_{Q_p}. (2) For each x ∈ Q, x ≡ 1 mod p and r̄|G_{Q_x} is a direct sum of four pairwise distinct characters with Frobenius eigenvalues α_x, β_x, γ_x, δ_x, labelled so that λ(α_x) ⊕ λ(β_x) is isotropic, hence α_xδ_x = β_xγ_x. Assume also αβ(α²−1)(β²−1)(α−β)(α²β²−1) ≠ 0. Let m be the corresponding maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra away from p (containing m_∅). Let A be a nontrivial power of the Hasse invariant, of weight k; with coefficients O/ϖ^m, a lift with q-expansion ≡ 1 mod ϖ^m. Then the composite H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j,2)_{O/ϖ^m})^{α,β}_m →(×A) H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j+k, 2+k)_{O/ϖ^m})_m →(π_β) H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j+k, 2+k)_{O/ϖ^m})^β_m is injective, where π_β is the projection onto the summand on which U − β and Q2 − αβ (equivalently Z2 − αβ) are nilpotent. By symmetry the same holds with β replaced by α.
items.locator: §8.6, Theorem 8.13, pp. 864–865 (proof pp. 865–877: Lemmas 8.15–8.17, Theorem 8.22, Proposition 8.25)
items.note: This is the GSp4 analogue of CG18's doubling injectivity (psi-injective and case1-projection-isomorphism, both missing there). It depends on Lemmas 8.15–8.17, Theorem 8.22, Proposition 8.25, Theorems 8.10–8.11 and the Siegel Hecke formulas, all missing. The paper states the hypotheses through Assumption 6.16. Theorem 8.13 is applied in the proof of Theorem 6.17 (pp. 845–846) to the cuspidal subspaces H⁰(X_1(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{O/ϖ^m})^{α,β}_m. There it is used with a power A^s of A of weight t = rp^{m−1}(p−1), so s = p^{m−1}, and with both projections e_β and e_α. That choice of s is the one for which multiplication by A^s is Hecke-equivariant away from p on O/ϖ^m-coefficients (Lemma 6.4); the printed 'nontrivial power' in Theorem 8.13 should be read as such a suitable power [sourceIssues E102].

items.name: Lemma 8.14: the GL(2) weight-one analogue of Theorem 8.13
items.statement: Let X_1(N) be the modular curve (N prime to p) and let ρ̄: G_Q → GL2(F̄_p) be a modular representation of level N and weight 1 over F_p (it arises from a mod p Katz weight-one eigenform), such that ρ̄(Frob_p) has eigenvalues α and β with α − β ≠ 0. Let m be the corresponding maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra away from p. If A is a suitable power of the Hasse invariant, of weight k, then the composite H^0(X_1(N), ω_{O/ϖ^m})_m →(×A) H^0(X_1(N), ω^{k+1}_{O/ϖ^m})_m →(π_β) H^0(X_1(N), ω^{k+1}_{O/ϖ^m})^β_m is injective, where π_β is the projection onto the direct summand on which U − β is nilpotent.
items.note: The paper says this is the weight-one injectivity of Calegari–Geraghty [16] = Invent. Math. 2018, proved here by formal q-expansions. The CG18 extraction marked it missing (psi-injective, case1-projection-isomorphism) and routed it to GL2ModularityLiftingDefectOne. Gross's weight-one T_p is missing.

items.name: Gross: T_p on weight-one forms mod ϖ^m is U + ⟨p⟩V; T = U in higher weight
items.statement: For level N prime to p, the Hecke operator T = T_p acts on weight-one Katz forms H^0(X_1(N), ω_{O/ϖ^m}), commuting with the other Hecke operators, and acts on q-expansions by T = U + ⟨p⟩V, where U(Σ a_n q^n) = Σ a_{np} q^n and V(Σ a_n q^n) = Σ a_n q^{np}. Formally UV = id. In weight k′ ≥ 2, T_p = U + p^{k′−1}⟨p⟩V, so T = U mod p.
items.locator: used in §8.6, proof of Lemma 8.14, p. 866
items.note: The status matches PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18, which marked gross-weight-one-Tp missing. Gross's T_p on weight-one Katz forms mod ϖ^m at general level N prime to p is planned nowhere. External input: Gross [35], §4, Prop. 4.1 (weight-one T_p)

items.name: Katz: θ has no kernel on mod p forms of low weight
items.statement: θ = q d/dq acts on q-expansions of mod p modular forms of level prime to p, raising the weight by p + 1, and has no kernel on forms of weight 1 ≤ k′ ≤ p − 2; in particular it is injective on weight-one forms for p ≥ 3. Formally θ ∘ V = 0.
items.locator: used in §8.6, proof of Lemma 8.14 (alternative argument), p. 866
items.note: Consistent with PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 (katz-theta-injective, planned in R15.3). A nonzero form of weight 1 ≤ k′ ≤ p − 2 has filtration k′, so the filtration rule gives injectivity. θ∘V = 0 is a formal consequence of the q-expansion formula q d/dq. Katz LNM 601 is the source R15.3 records. External input: N. M. Katz, A result on modular forms in characteristic p, in Modular Functions of One Variable V, LNM 601 (1977), 53–61 ([45])

items.name: Reduction of injectivity to the socle and to coefficients O/ϖ
items.statement: The maps in Theorem 8.13 and Lemma 8.14 are equivariant for the Hecke operators away from p. For a Hecke-equivariant map of finite-length modules localized at m, injectivity can be checked on the T-socle (the m-torsion). The socle of H^0(·, ·_{O/ϖ^m})_m lies in its ϖ-torsion, which is H^0(·, ·_{O/ϖ})_m. Hence it suffices to prove injectivity with coefficients in the finite field O/ϖ.
items.note: The algebraic reduction is in the library. In an Artinian (finite-length) module the socle contains every simple submodule, so it is essential (isEssential_iff_forall_atom_le). A map injective on the socle is then injective (IsEssential.injective_of_injective_comp). Over the local Hecke algebra the socle is the m-torsion, so it lies in the ϖ-torsion. The identification H^0(·, W_{O/ϖ^m})[ϖ] = H^0(·, W_{O/ϖ}) is left exactness of global sections on the O-flat automorphic bundle. It needs only the bundle itself (AutomorphicBundles:B4, ShimuraCompactifications:C5).

items.name: On N, Q2 is invertible only on the part where U is invertible
items.statement: Claimed in the paper, without adequate proof: on N = H^0(X_1(Q), ω(j+k, 2+k)_{O/ϖ})_m, with k > 0 a multiple of p−1, every generalized eigenspace of Q2 (= Z2 on q-expansions) with nonzero eigenvalue lies in the submodule on which U (= T mod p) acts invertibly. The paper's justification ('lifting to characteristic 0') shows only that such eigensystems are ordinary for the Siegel parabolic. Q2-invertibility does not by itself force T-invertibility.
items.note: The paper proves this 'by lifting to characteristic 0' (proof of Lemma 8.15), using characteristic-zero Siegel eigenforms in weight (j+k, 2+k) and their Hecke eigenvalues at p. It is planned nowhere. The intended 'lifting to characteristic 0' reads the U- and Q2-eigenvalues of a characteristic-0 eigenform of weight τ = (j′, k′) = (j+k, 2+k) off its crystalline Frobenius eigenvalues at p: U from the smallest-slope one α′, and Q2 from the product α′β′ of the two smallest (§8.5). This needs local–global compatibility at p in regular weight (Theorem 6.13, §8.5). It also needs N to be spanned by reductions of characteristic-0 eigenforms, which the paper does not show. Even with both inputs, a unit Q2-eigenvalue says only that the slopes satisfy s1 + s2 = k′ − 2, i.e. the Newton polygon meets the Hodge polygon at its second vertex. It does not force s1 = 0, so it does not make U invertible [sourceIssues E107]. There is no formal shortcut either. The formal identity on p. 859 is Z2 = UZ, and U commutes with Z2, but Z2 ≠ ZU in general and Z does not act on N. So the remark in formal-identity-Z2-equals-UZ-equals-ZU that it gives a direct proof of this claim is not justified. What Lemma 8.15 actually needs is weaker, and it does follow formally. Let W = Σ_{i≥0} U^iM, a finite U-stable subspace of N. Then T ≡ U + Z on M, Z2 = UZ and Z2U = UZ2 give Z2^nW ⊂ U^nW for all n. Using M = Z2M (j > 2), resp. Z2²M = Z2M (σ = (2,2)), it follows that M, resp. Z2M, lies in the part of W on which U is invertible [sourceIssues E107].

items.name: The spaces M ⊂ N in the proof of Theorem 8.13
items.statement: This is the setting of Theorem 8.13. r̄ is as in Assumption 6.16. σ = (j,2) with p − 1 > j ≥ 2; by Remark 8.2, j ≥ 4 or j = 2. α, β ∈ k are units with αβ(α²−1)(β²−1)(α−β)(α²β²−1) ≠ 0. 𝔪 is the maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra away from p attached to r̄. A is a nontrivial power of the Hasse invariant; its weight k is a positive multiple of p − 1. After reducing to coefficients in the residue field k = O/ϖ (via the T-socle, p. 865), put M := H⁰(X₁(Q), ω(j,2)_k)^{α,β}_𝔪. This is the (α,β)-part, on which T_{p,1} − (α+β) and Q_{p,2} − αβ are nilpotent; the printed definition omits the superscript α,β [sourceIssues E108]. Put N := H⁰(X₁(Q), ω(j+k, 2+k)_k)_𝔪 and τ := (j+k, 2+k). Multiplication by A is a map M → N that is the identity on q-expansions. By the q-expansion principle (Theorem 8.1) it is injective, and M is identified with its image, M ⊂ N.
items.note: No layer plans mod-p coherent H⁰ of the automorphic bundles ω(j,k) on the Siegel threefold, the Hasse invariant of a genus-two abelian scheme as a Siegel form of weight (p−1,p−1), or the Siegel q-expansion principle mod p (Theorem 8.1). The nearest planned layers are characteristic 0 or genus one only. AutomorphicBundles:B4 says 'For Siegel data, identify the Hodge vector bundle, its determinant, and Schur-functor weights'. AutomorphicBundles:B5 plans 'Fourier–Jacobi expansions at the relevant higher-dimensional boundary components' and 'the expansion principle'. AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.3 constructs the Hasse invariant for modular curves only. The pinned declaration index contains no Siegel modular form, GSp₄ or abelian-surface Hasse declarations. Checked on p. 867: the printed M omits the superscript α,β, as the item says. Since αβ ≠ 0, Q2 acts invertibly on M (p. 867). By Lemma 8.12, Q2 acts on M as the formal operator Z2 when j > 2 and as Z2 + X2 when σ = (2,2), and on N, of weight τ, as Z2 (see hecke-operators-at-p-on-M-mod-p).

items.name: Hecke operators at p on M as formal operators
items.statement:
In the setting of thm-8-13-proof-spaces-M-N:
(i) Q₂ = (p·T₂ + (p+p³)S)·p^{2−2} acts on M (Lemma 8.8). Q₂ − αβ is nilpotent on M, so αβ is its only generalized eigenvalue there. Since αβ ≠ 0, Q₂ acts invertibly on M.
(ii) On q-expansions of elements of M, Q₂ acts as the formal operator Z₂ if σ = (j,2) with j > 2, and as Z₂ + X₂ if σ = (2,2) (Lemma 8.12).
(iii) T = T_{p,1} acts on M as the formal operator U + Z. By Lemma 8.3, T = U + p^{k−2}Z + p^{k+j−3}V with k = 2, so T ≡ U + Z mod p. In particular TF = (U+Z)F ∈ M for F ∈ M.
items.locator: §8.6, p. 867 (before Lemma 8.15); proof of Lemma 8.17, p. 869
items.note: The formal Hecke operators at p on Siegel q-expansions, and their action mod p on H⁰ (Lemmas 8.3, 8.4, 8.8, 8.12), are not planned. AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.2 ('Define Hecke actions from R14 and compare their coefficient formulas') covers modular curves only. AutomorphicBundles:B5 treats Hecke correspondences in characteristic 0. Checked on pp. 859–860 and 864: Q₂ = (p·T₂ + (p+p³)S)p^{2−k}, and Lemma 8.12 gives Q₂ ≡ Z₂ mod p for (j,k) ≠ (2,2) and Q₂ ≡ Z₂ + X₂ for (2,2). On p. 869 the proof uses T = U + Z on M.

items.name: U and Z₂ act on N; Z₂ = UZ commutes with U
items.statement: On N (weight τ = (j+k, 2+k), with τ ≠ (2,2) and second index 2 + k ≥ 3), T = T_{p,1} acts as the formal operator U, and Q₂ acts as the formal operator Z₂ (Lemmas 8.3 and 8.12 mod p). Hence U and Z₂ map N into N. In particular, for F ∈ M ⊂ N: UF ∈ N and Z₂F ∈ N, so Z₂M ⊂ N also when σ = (2,2); and ZF = TF − UF ∈ N. As formal operators Z₂ = UZ (p. 859), and Z₂ commutes with U.
items.locator: §8.6, proof of Lemma 8.15, pp. 867–868; proof of Lemma 8.17, p. 869
items.note: Same gap as hecke-operators-at-p-on-M-mod-p. The formal identity Z₂ = UZ (p. 859) and the action of T and Q₂ on high-weight Siegel forms mod p are not planned in any layer, and the libraries have no Siegel q-expansions.

items.name: Lemma 8.15, case σ = (j,2), j > 2
items.statement: Let α and β be as in Theorem 8.13, and let σ = (j,2) with j > 2. Then M = Q₂M = Z₂M, and M lies in the submodule of N on which U is invertible.
items.note: This is a step in the paper's own Hasse-invariant argument on Siegel forms mod p (p. 867). Nothing in the atlas or the libraries covers it.

items.name: Lemma 8.15, case σ = (2,2): Z₂ is injective on M
items.statement: Let α and β be as in Theorem 8.13 (so αβ ≠ 0 and (αβ)² ≠ 1), and let σ = (2,2). Then Z₂ acts on N: it is the formal operator through which the weight-τ Hecke operator Q₂ acts (Lemma 8.12). In particular Z₂M ⊂ N. The map M → Z₂M, F ↦ Z₂F, is injective, hence bijective. Z₂ acts invertibly on Z₂M (Z₂²M = Z₂M, using Z₂X₂ = 0 from Lemma 8.6), and Z₂M ⊂ N lies in the submodule of N on which U is invertible.
items.note: This is paper-specific (pp. 867–868). It uses Lemma 8.6 (Z₂X₂ = 0 over k) and the hypothesis (αβ)² ≠ 1. Nothing covers it. The injectivity of Z2 on M from this lemma is used again in the proof of Lemma 8.17(2) (p. 871) and at the end of §8.8 (p. 874), the case σ = (2,2) of Theorem 8.22; on the §8.8 appeal see sourceIssues E122. The paper remarks (p. 868) that this lemma is the one place where it uses (αβ)² ≠ 1 rather than the weaker αβ ≠ 1, which suffices on the Galois side.

items.name: Lemma 8.16: U(U − α)(U − β) is nilpotent on N
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 8.13, the operator U(U − α)(U − β) acts nilpotently on N.
items.note: The proof (p. 868) lifts to characteristic 0 and uses the fact that the only possible unit crystalline Frobenius eigenvalues of a lift of r̄ are ≡ α or β. This needs crystalline GSp₄ Galois representations attached to Siegel eigenforms with Hecke–Frobenius compatibility at p. No layer plans this: searches for GSp₄, Sorensen, Weissauer and Laumon found no Siegel Galois-representation layer.

items.name: Decomposition N = N_α ⊕ N_β ⊕ N_0 and the projection π_β
items.statement: For λ ∈ {α, β, 0}, let N_λ ⊂ N be the generalized λ-eigenspace of U. Since α, β, 0 are pairwise distinct (αβ(α−β) ≠ 0), Lemma 8.16 gives N = N_α ⊕ N_β ⊕ N_0; elements are written (F_α, F_β, F_0). U is invertible on N_α ⊕ N_β, which is exactly the submodule of N on which U is invertible, and U is nilpotent on N_0. π_β : N → N_β is the projection. On N_α ⊕ N_β, π_β has the same kernel N_α as (U − α)^m for m ≫ 0; the paper 'writes π_β as (U − α)^m'. On M (j > 2) and on Z₂M (σ = (2,2)), Q₂ − αβ is nilpotent. So there π_β agrees with the projection of Theorem 8.13 onto the part where U − β and Q₂ − αβ are nilpotent.
items.note: The decomposition is library linear algebra. The item is missing because N, U and the comparison with Theorem 8.13's projection concern Siegel forms mod p, which nothing plans. π_β first appears in the statement of Theorem 8.13 (p. 865), with O/ϖ^m coefficients, as the projection onto the summand on which U − β and Q2 − αβ are nilpotent. Equivalently, U − β and Z2 − αβ are nilpotent there, since Q2 ≡ Z2 mod p in weight (j+k, 2+k) (Lemma 8.12). π_α is defined symmetrically, and in this weight T ≡ U mod p (Lemma 8.3, as 2 + k ≥ 3). For arbitrary γ ∈ k̄ one defines N_γ ⊂ N ⊗_k k̄ in the same way. Then N ⊗_k k̄ = ⊕_γ N_γ, and the part on which U is invertible is ⊕_{γ≠0} N_γ. The same notation N_γ is used for the GL2 space N = H⁰(X_1(N), ω^{k+1}_{O/ϖ^m})_m in the proof of Lemma 8.14 (p. 866).

items.name: Lemma 8.17(1): a simultaneous U-, T-, Z-eigenform in weight (j,2), j > 2
items.statement: This is the setting of Theorem 8.13 with σ = (j,2) and j > 2, where Z₂M = M. Suppose π_β : M → N_β is not injective. Then there is a nonzero F = F_α ∈ M ∩ N_α such that UF = αF, TF = (α+β)F and ZF = βF.
items.note: This is paper-specific (pp. 868–869). Nothing covers it.

items.name: Lemma 8.17(2): the constrained form in weight (2,2)
items.statement: This is the setting of Theorem 8.13 with σ = (2,2). Suppose the composite M → Z₂M → N_β, F ↦ π_β(Z₂F), is not injective; printed: 'the composite π_β : Z₂M → N_β is not injective'. Then there is a nonzero F ∈ M with F = F_α + F_0, F_α ∈ N_α, F_0 ∈ N_0, such that UF_α = αF_α, TF = (α+β)F and X₂F = αβF_0. The proof also gives Q₂F = αβF, Z₂F = αβF_α and F_β = 0.
items.note: This is paper-specific (pp. 868–871). Nothing covers it.

items.name: X₂ maps M into N, UX₂ = 0 and X₂³ = X₂ mod p
items.statement:
Let σ = (2,2) and F ∈ M.
(i) X₂F = Q₂F − Z₂F lies in N: Q₂F ∈ M ⊂ N, and Z₂F ∈ N.
(ii) UX₂ = 0 as operators on formal q-expansions over k. Indeed a(UX₂F,Q) = a(X₂F,pQ) = p·a(F,pQ) ≡ 0, by Definition 8.5 applied to pQ ≡ 0 mod p and Lemma 8.3. Hence X₂F ∈ ker U ⊂ N_0, and in Lemma 8.17(2) UF_0 = 0 because F_0 = (αβ)⁻¹X₂F.
(iii) X₂³ = X₂ over k, since a(X₂F,Q) ≡ (D/p)a(F,Q).
items.locator: Used without statement in the proofs of Lemma 8.15 (p. 868) and Lemma 8.17(2) (pp. 870–871), and in the reduction to Theorem 8.22(2) (p. 873)
items.note: These are identities of the formal operator X₂ (Definition 8.5, U₂ = 1 + pX₂, a(X₂F,Q) ≡ (D/p)a(F,Q) mod p) on Siegel q-expansions. They are not planned anywhere.

items.name: Reduction of Theorem 8.13 to the q-expansion statement Theorem 8.22
items.statement:
Suppose Theorem 8.22 holds. Then Theorem 8.13 holds.
Case j > 2 (so j ≥ 4 by Remark 8.2). If π_β∘A is not injective on M, Lemma 8.17(1) produces 0 ≠ F ∈ M with UF = αF and ZF = βF. Here αβ(β²−1) ≠ 0, which contradicts Theorem 8.22(1).
Case σ = (2,2). If π_β(F) = 0 for some 0 ≠ F ∈ M, then π_β(Z₂F) = Z₂π_β(F) = 0, because Z₂ acts on N commuting with U. So Lemma 8.17(2) applies and gives 0 ≠ F = F_α + F_0 ∈ M with UF_α = αF_α, X₂F = αβF_0 and TF = (α+β)F. Since T ≡ U + Z in weight (2,2) and UF_0 = 0, ZF = (α+β)F − αF_α = βF + αF_0. With αβ(β²−1)(α²β²−1) ≠ 0 this contradicts Theorem 8.22(2).
items.locator: §8.6, p. 871 ('At this point, to prove Theorem 8.13, it suffices…'); §8.7, p. 873 ('In light of Lemma 8.17, to prove Theorem 8.13, it suffices to prove the following')
items.note: This is paper-specific (p. 871, 873). Nothing covers it.

items.name: Formal Siegel modular forms (formal q-expansions)
items.statement: A formal Siegel modular form (formal q-expansion) of weight σ = (j,k) over k is a formal sum F = Σ_{Q∈X} a(F,Q)q^Q. Here X is the set of 2×2 positive semidefinite Q = [[m, r/2],[r/2, n]] with m, r, n ∈ Z[1/L], where L is the product of the primes in S and Q; the paper notes that, since its arguments are p-adic, one may pretend L = 1. For Q ∈ M₂(Q) ∖ X, a(F,Q) := 0. The coefficients a(F,Q) lie in U_σ = Sym^{j−k}(V) ⊗ k, V = k², and satisfy a(F, M.Q) = ρ(M)a(F,Q) for M ∈ Γ̄, where M.Q = (det M)⁻¹MQMᵀ and ρ extends to a multiplicative map M₂(Z) → End(U_σ). The formal operators U, Z, V, Z₂, X₂ (§8.3, Definition 8.5) and Θ, θ₁ (Proposition 8.9) act on such sums by their coefficient formulas. A 'Siegel modular q-expansion' of weight σ is the q-expansion of an actual element of H⁰(X₁(Q), ω(σ)_k). The paper does not define the term; this is the reading its uses require.
items.locator: Conventions of §8.2 (pp. 856–857). Used as 'formal q-expansions' (p. 867), 'Siegel modular q-expansion' (Theorem 8.22, p. 873) and 'formal Siegel modular form' (Lemma 8.24, p. 875; Proposition 8.25, p. 876)
items.note: No library or layer defines formal Siegel q-expansions over half-integral positive semidefinite binary forms with the equivariance a(F, M.Q) = ρ(M)a(F,Q). Mathlib has `SymmetricPower` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorPower/Symmetric.lean:52) for the coefficient module Sym^{j−k}(V), but nothing indexed by binary forms. AutomorphicBundles:B5 plans Fourier–Jacobi expansions in characteristic 0. AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.2 plans q-expansions in genus one. More generally the coefficients may lie in U_σ = Sym^{j−k}(V) ⊗ R for any O-module R. The formal q-expansion is integral if its coefficients lie in the O-lattice. A binary quadratic form Q = (m, r/2; r/2, n) is p-integral if m, r, n ∈ Z_(p). The identities of Lemmas 8.3, 8.4, 8.6 and 8.12 hold as identities of formal operators on this space, with coefficients extended by zero outside 𝒳. They are T = U + p^{k−2}Z + p^{k+j−3}V (Lemma 8.3, p. 858), Z2 = UZ (p. 859), Z2X2 = 0 over k (Lemma 8.6, p. 859), and Q2 ≡ Z2 mod p, or Q2 ≡ Z2 + X2 mod p in weight (2,2) (Lemma 8.12, p. 864).

items.name: Definition 8.19: the multiset F(Q) of neighbouring classes
items.statement: Let S ⊂ M₂(Z) be a set of representatives of determinant p for the coset decomposition of Γ̄·diag(p,1)·Γ̄ (Lemma 8.3). Write [P] for the Γ̄-equivalence class of a binary quadratic form P, and M.P := (det M)⁻¹MPMᵀ. For a p-integral binary quadratic form Q, F(Q) is the following multiset of classes of p-integral binary quadratic forms: for each M ∈ S, add [P] to F(Q) if and only if some P ∈ [P] has Q = M.P. Equivalently, M contributes the class [M⁻¹.Q] exactly when M⁻¹.Q is p-integral.
items.note: This is the paper's combinatorial description of the operator Z through p-neighbours of binary quadratic forms. It is not planned, and the libraries have no Γ̄-classes of binary quadratic forms.

items.name: F(Q) depends only on [Q]
items.statement: For g ∈ Γ̄, F(g.Q) = F(Q) as multisets of classes.
items.locator: §8.7, p. 872 ('An easy lemma shows that F(Q) depends only on [Q]')
items.note: This is an elementary lemma about Definition 8.19 (p. 872: 'An easy lemma shows…'). It is not planned.

items.name: F(Q) is indexed by the zeros of Q on P¹(F_p)
items.statement: S is in natural bijection with P¹(F_p): S is the coset space of diag(1,p) in Γ̄ ⊂ SL₂(Z), where Γ̄ has level prime to p. A binary quadratic form defines a section of O(2) on P¹(F_p). For M ∈ S, M⁻¹.Q is p-integral if and only if Q mod p vanishes at the point of P¹(F_p) corresponding to M. Consequently: F(Q) is empty if Q does not represent zero mod p; #F(Q), counted with multiplicity, equals the number of zeros of Q in P¹(F_p), which is 0, 1 or 2 when Q is p-primitive; and if Q is not p-primitive, then Q ≡ 0 mod p and #F(Q) = p + 1.
items.note: This is missing as a statement about Siegel Hecke coset representatives and binary forms.

items.name: The Z-coefficient formula in terms of F(Q)
items.statement: Let F be a formal Siegel modular form of weight (j,k) and Q a binary form. Then a(ZF,Q) = Σ_{[P]∈F(Q)} ρ(M_P)a(F,P), where for each [P] ∈ F(Q) one picks P ∈ [P] and M_P ∈ S with M_P.P = Q; the term does not depend on the choice.
items.note: This rewrites Lemma 8.3's formula for Z (from Andrianov-type Hecke formulas, [18, Prop. 10.2]) in terms of F(Q). Nothing plans Siegel Hecke operators on Fourier coefficients.

items.name: Lemma 8.20: the neighbour relation is symmetric
items.statement: If [P] ∈ F([Q]), then [Q] ∈ F([P]). More precisely, after replacing Q by g.Q for some g ∈ Γ̄ one may take Q = M.P with M = diag(1,p). Then P = M⁻¹.Q = (pM⁻¹).Q, and pM⁻¹ = diag(p,1) lies in S up to Γ̄.
items.note: This is paper-specific (p. 872). Nothing covers it.

items.name: Discriminant d(Q) and the symbol (D/p)
items.statement: For Q = [[m, r/2],[r/2, n]], corresponding to the form mx² + rxy + ny², the discriminant is d(Q) := r² − 4mn = −4·det(Q). For D = d(Q), (D/p) is the Legendre symbol. The action M.Q preserves det(Q), hence d(Q).
items.locator: §8.7, p. 872 ('Let d(Q) denote the discriminant of Q'); identity r² − 4mn = −4det(Q) on p. 877
items.note: The definition, the Legendre symbol and the invariance of det and d are all available directly.

items.name: Zeros of a binary quadratic form over F_p
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime and Q = mx² + rxy + ny² with (m,r,n) ≢ (0,0,0) mod p. The number of zeros of Q in P¹(F_p) is 1 + (d/p), where d = r² − 4mn: there are 0, 1 or 2 zeros according as (d/p) = −1, 0 or 1.
items.note: The count of zeros in P¹(F_p) as 1 + (d/p) is not a library declaration: projective points, the point at infinity when m ≡ 0, and the degenerate case are not packaged. No layer plans it either. ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.1's reviewed node covers only Euler's criterion, Gauss's lemma and reciprocity. External input: Standard elementary fact; the paper gives no citation.

items.name: Lemma 8.21: size of F([Q]) for p-primitive Q
items.statement: Let Q be p-primitive and D = d(Q). Then exactly one of the following holds: (1) (D/p) = −1 and F([Q]) is empty; (2) (D/p) = 0 and F([Q]) has exactly one element; (3) (D/p) = +1 and F([Q]) has exactly two elements, counted with multiplicity. In case (3) the two elements may be the same class; this happens, for example, if (D/p) = 1 and the class number of D is 1.
items.note: This follows from F-of-Q-zeros-on-P1Fp and ext-zeros-binary-quadratic-form-mod-p. It is paper-specific and not planned.

items.name: Theorem 8.22(1): no U- and Z-eigenforms in weight (j,2), j ≥ 4
items.statement: Let p − 1 > j ≥ 4, and let F = Σ a(F,Q)q^Q be a Siegel modular q-expansion of weight σ = (j,2) in characteristic p. Suppose UF = αF and ZF = βF for some α, β ∈ k with αβ(β² − 1) ≠ 0. Then F = 0.
items.note: This is the paper's key q-expansion theorem (p. 873). Its proof uses Proposition 8.25 and Theorem 8.11 (Yamauchi's injectivity of θ₁ [75, Thm 3.20]). None of this is planned. The proof ends in §8.9 (p. 877), and the same sentence completes the proof of Theorem 8.13. The last step, for F ∈ H⁰(X_1(Q), ω(j,2)_k), runs as follows. Proposition 8.25 gives θ₁F = 0 as a formal q-expansion; on the Q not covered by its printed proof see sourceIssues E125. By Proposition 8.9(2), θ₁F is the q-expansion of a section of ω(j+p−1, p+3)_k, so it vanishes as a section by the q-expansion principle (Theorem 8.1). Only then does the injectivity of θ₁ (Theorem 8.11) give F = 0. The paper leaves the appeal to Theorem 8.1 implicit.

items.name: Theorem 8.22(2): the weight (2,2) statement
items.statement: Let p − 1 > 2, and let F = Σ a(F,Q)q^Q be a Siegel modular q-expansion of weight (2,2) in characteristic p. Suppose F = F_α + F_0, where UF_α = αF_α, X₂F = αβF_0 and ZF = βF + αF_0, for some α, β ∈ k with αβ(β² − 1)(α²β² − 1) ≠ 0. Then F = 0.
items.note: This is paper-specific (p. 873). Its proof (§8.8) uses Theorem 8.10 (injectivity of Θ, after Yamauchi [75]), which is not planned.

items.name: Step 1 of Theorem 8.22: a nonzero coefficient with p ∤ d(Q)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 8.22(1) or (2), if F ≠ 0 then a(F,Q) ≠ 0 for some Q with det(Q) ≢ 0 mod p, equivalently p ∤ d(Q).
items.note: This is paper-specific (pp. 873–874). Nothing covers it.

items.name: Z-eigenforms vanish on forms with (d/p) = −1
items.statement: Let F be a formal Siegel modular form of weight (j,2) with ZF = βF and β ≠ 0. Then a(F,Q) = 0 for every Q with (d(Q)/p) = −1. Indeed F(Q) = ∅ by Lemma 8.21(1), so βa(F,Q) = a(ZF,Q) = 0.
items.note: This is paper-specific (p. 874, 876). The page image of p. 874 prints 'the identity ZF = βZ', which should read ZF = βF.

items.name: §8.8: support of F in weight (2,2)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 8.22(2), ZF = βF + β⁻¹X₂F, since αF_0 = β⁻¹X₂F. For Q with (d(Q)/p) = −1, 0 = a(ZF,Q) = βa(F,Q) − β⁻¹a(F,Q) = (β − β⁻¹)a(F,Q), so a(F,Q) = 0 because β² ≠ 1. Hence a(F,Q) ≠ 0 only if (d(Q)/p) ∈ {0, 1}. Consequently a(F − X₂F, Q) = (1 − (d(Q)/p))a(F,Q) vanishes unless p | d(Q), so Θ(F − X₂F) = 0 as formal q-expansions.
items.note: This is paper-specific (p. 874). Two misprints are confirmed on the page image. 'a(X₂F,Q) is equal to (D/p)a(F,R)' should read a(F,Q) [sourceIssues E119]. 'D = det(Q) satisfying (D/p) = 0, 1' should use D = d(Q), the discriminant, because (det Q/p) = (−1/p)(d/p) [sourceIssues E119, E120].

items.name: §8.8: conclusion of the weight (2,2) case
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 8.22(2): F = X₂F, hence Z₂F = Z₂X₂F = 0 by Lemma 8.6, and therefore F = 0.
items.note: This is paper-specific (p. 874). It uses Theorem 8.10 and Lemmas 8.6 and 8.15, none of which is planned.

items.name: Neighbour cycles of Γ̄-classes under Z (split case)
items.statement: Fix D with (D/p) = 1. The Γ̄-classes of binary quadratic forms of discriminant D form a finite set; the paper identifies it with a ray class group. By Lemmas 8.20 and 8.21(3), each class [Q] has exactly two neighbours (the elements of F([Q]), with multiplicity) and the relation is symmetric, so the classes split into finitely many cycles. For a neighbour P = M.Q, with M ∈ S corresponding to a zero ξ of Q, there is N = pM⁻¹ ∈ S with N.P = Q and MN = pI. The corresponding back-tracking term of a(Z²F,Q) is ρ(M)ρ(N)a(F,Q) = ρ(pI)a(F,Q) = p^{j−2}a(F,Q), which is 0 when j > 2. For a cycle of size s, going once around in one direction gives, after modifying M_s by an element of Γ̄, A = M_s⋯M₁ ∈ M₂(Z) with det A = p^s and A.Q = Q, i.e. AQAᵗ = p^sQ. Going the other way gives B with BQBᵗ = p^sQ.
items.note: Part of this is planned for SL₂(ℤ): finiteness of classes of positive-definite binary forms of a given discriminant. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-11 plans 'the number of SL₂(ℤ)-classes of positive-definite integral binary quadratic forms … Define it by reduced forms — a finite, decidable count: no class groups'. The following are not planned: the congruence-subgroup (Γ̄) version, the identification with a ray class group, the p-neighbour 2-regular structure and the cycle matrices A, B with AQAᵗ = p^sQ. The page image of p. 874 says Γ̄ 'has a finite orbit'; this should read 'finitely many orbits'.

items.name: Lemma 8.24: Z^s-eigen-equation around a cycle
items.statement: Let j ≥ 4. The printed statement says only 'weight (j,2)', but the derivation needs j > 2. Let F be a formal Siegel modular form of weight (j,2) that is an eigenform of Z with eigenvalue β, and let Q have discriminant D with (D/p) = 1. Then there are an integer s > 0 and A, B ∈ M₂(Z) with det A = det B = p^s, AQAᵗ = p^sQ and BQBᵗ = p^sQ, such that β^s a(F,Q) = ρ(A)a(F,Q) + ρ(B)a(F,Q) = Sym^{j−2}[A]a(F,Q) + Sym^{j−2}[B]a(F,Q).
items.note: This is paper-specific (pp. 875–876). Nothing covers it.

items.name: Key claim in Proposition 8.25: contraction against Q^∨ kills the image of Sym^{j−2}[A]
items.statement: Let j ≥ 4 and p > j − 2. Let Q be a p-integral binary quadratic form, s ≥ 1, and A ∈ M₂(Z) (or M₂(Z_p)) with det A = p^s and AQAᵗ = det(A)Q. Then con(Sym^{j−2}[A]x ⊗ Q^∨) = 0 in Sym^{j−4}(k²) ⊗ det for every x ∈ Sym^{j−2}(V), V = k². Proof, as in the paper: if tr A ≢ 0 mod p, A is diagonalizable over Z_p as diag(u, p^s/u). If tr A ≡ 0, A is nilpotent mod p. In either case either A ≡ 0 mod p, or after a Z_p-change of basis the image of A mod p is kf₁ and n ≡ 0 mod p. Then Q^∨ ≡ me₁² + re₁e₂, and f₁^{j−2} contracts nontrivially only with e₂².
items.locator: §8.9, proof of Proposition 8.25: claim stated p. 876, proved p. 877
items.note: This is paper-specific (p. 877). Nothing covers it.

items.name: Hensel's lemma (eigenvalues of A over Z_p)
items.statement: A monic polynomial over Z_p with a simple root mod p has a unique root in Z_p lifting it. Applied to the characteristic polynomial X² − tr(A)X + p^s of A with tr(A) ≢ 0 mod p, this gives eigenvalues u ∈ Z_p^× and p^s/u, so A is diagonalizable over Z_p.
items.note: Hensel's lemma is library, which agrees with the earlier extractions (PAPER-GHOSH-SARNAK-22/27, PAPER-CHARLES-16/116). The following application in Proposition 8.25 is a short elementary step, not a declaration: A has eigenvalues u ∈ Z_p^× and p^s/u, so A is diagonalizable over Z_p, because the residues u ≢ 0 ≡ p^s/u are distinct. External input: Hensel's lemma (standard).

items.name: Proposition 8.25: θ₁F = 0 for a Z-eigenform
items.statement: Let F be a formal Siegel modular form of weight (j,2) modulo p that is an eigenform of Z with eigenvalue β ≠ 0, and suppose p > j − 2 (in context j ≥ 4). Suppose F has a nonzero coefficient a(F,Q) with (d(Q)/p) = 1. Then θ₁F = 0.
items.note: This is paper-specific (pp. 876–877). It relies on θ₁ (Proposition 8.9(2)), which is not planned.

items.name: Notation for Theorem 9.1
items.statement: Choose an auxiliary prime q ≠ p as at the beginning of §6.3: r̄ is unramified at q, q ≢ 1 mod p, and no two eigenvalues of r̄(Frob_q) have ratio q mod p. Put S = S(r̄) ∪ {q}. Let K = Π_x K_x ⊂ GSp₄(A^∞) be the compact open subgroup defined there: K_x = GSp₄(Z_x) at x = p and at unramified x ≠ q; K_x is Iwahori, Klingen, paramodular, Π(x)⁺ or full level x according to the type of r̄|G_x for x ∈ S(r̄); K_q is the full congruence subgroup of level q. K is assumed neat (§5.2). Put X = X_K. For a finite set Q of primes disjoint from S ∪ {p}, put X_i(Q) = X_{K_i(Q)} for i = 0, 1 (§5.2; K_{x,0} = Π(x) and K_{x,1} = Π⁺(x) for x ∈ Q). T_σ = T_σ^an(∅) and T_σ^an(Q) are the Hecke algebras of Definition 5.13, generated by the T_{x,i} for x ∉ S ∪ Q ∪ {p}. m_∅ is the maximal ideal of T_σ attached to r̄, which exists because r̄ is Katz modular (Definition 6.15); its pullback to T_σ^an(Q) is also written m_∅. H⁰(X, ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O})^{α,β} is the e_{α,β}-part (§6.4), intended as the part on which T_{p,1} − (α+β) and Q_{p,2} − αβ are topologically nilpotent. T^{α,β}_{σ,m_∅} is the image of T_σ in End_O of this space, localized at m_∅. R^min is the universal ring for deformations of r̄ that are minimal in the sense of Definition 4.6 with Q = ∅.
items.note: Some geometric pieces are planned. PELModuli:M5 says 'Construct Siegel moduli for every dimension'. ShimuraCompactifications:C5 plans integral PEL compactifications. AutomorphicBundles:B4 plans Siegel Hodge bundles and Schur weights. The following are not planned: the GSp₄ level subgroups K_i(Q) (Π(x), Π⁺(x)), the coherent Hecke algebras T_σ and T_σ^an(Q) with m_∅ and e_{α,β}-parts, and the GSp₄-valued minimal deformation ring R^min. GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1–R04.6, G7 and G8 plan GL_n deformations and polarized GL_n over CM fields only.

items.name: Theorem 9.1 (main theorem): minimal R = T for GSp₄ in weight (a,2)
items.statement:
Let r̄ : G_Q → GSp₄(k) be continuous, odd and absolutely irreducible, with similitude ν(r̄) = ε^{−(a−1)} (ε the mod p cyclotomic character), where p − 1 > a ≥ 2. Assume:
(1) There are units α, β ∈ k with r̄|G_{Q_p} ~ [[λ(α), 0, *, *], [0, λ(β), *, *], [0, 0, ν(r̄)λ(β⁻¹), 0], [0, 0, 0, ν(r̄)λ(α⁻¹)]], where λ(x) is the unramified character with Frob_p ↦ x, and (α²−1)(β²−1)(α²β²−1)(α−β) ≠ 0.
(2) For each x in S(r̄), the set of primes x ≠ p at which r̄ is ramified, r̄|G_{Q_x} is one of the types of Assumption 4.3.
(3) (Big image) r̄|G_{Q(ζ_p)} has big image in the sense of Assumption 4.1.
(4) r̄ is Katz modular of weight σ := (a,2) ∈ X*(T)⁺_M in the sense of Definition 6.15.
(5) (Neatness) r̄ satisfies Assumption 4.2.
(6) With the notation of thm-9-1-setup: for every Q satisfying Assumption 6.12(2), H²(X_i(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_k)_{m_∅} = 0.
Then the map R^min → T^{α,β}_{σ,m_∅} classifying the minimal deformation of Theorem 6.17 (with Q = ∅) is an isomorphism.
items.note: This is the main theorem, checked on the image of p. 878. No layer plans modularity lifting for GSp₄. OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting (R21) and GL2ModularityLifting cover GL₂, and PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure covers GL_n over CM fields. The abstract patching input (Proposition 3.3 = CG18 Proposition 2.3) is planned in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.5. This matches CG18's treatment: its weight-one analogue thm-3-26 was marked missing. Theorem 1.2 (§1, pp. 802–803) is the introduction's statement of the main result. It is not proved separately, and its freeness conclusion is thm-9-1-freeness. As printed it differs from Theorem 9.1 in several ways. It assumes ν(r̄) = ε̄^{1−j} only on inertia at p, not on all of G_Q, and 'irreducible' rather than 'absolutely irreducible' [sourceIssues E4]. It does not say 'odd', which costs nothing to add. It does not assume neatness either, but Assumption 4.2 follows from Assumption 4.1(H1), which it does assume [sourceIssues E4]. In place of Katz modularity (Definition 6.15) it assumes a maximal ideal m of T with r̄_m ≅ r̄. It requires j ≥ 4, where hypothesis (6) of Theorem 9.1 holds by Theorem 5.1 (p. 879). It is stated on Y_1(N), with N = N(r̄) 'determined by r̄ as in Section 5', whereas the level in Theorem 9.1 is the group K of §6.3, which includes the auxiliary prime q [sourceIssues E2]. Its module is eH⁰(Y_1(N), ω(j,2) ⊗ K/O), which by the Koecher principle (p. 821) is the H⁰ of the canonical extension. Theorem 9.1 uses the cuspidal H⁰(X, ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O}), and the paper never identifies the two m-localizations [sourceIssues E1].

items.name: Theorem 9.1 (freeness of the dual of the (α,β)-part of H⁰)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses (1)–(6) of Theorem 9.1 (r̄ continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible, with ν(r̄) = ε^{−(a−1)} and p − 1 > a ≥ 2; the ordinary shape at p with (α²−1)(β²−1)(α²β²−1)(α−β) ≠ 0; ramification of Assumption 4.3; big image; Katz modular of weight (a,2); neat; H²(X_i(Q), ω(a,2)(−∞)_k)_{m_∅} = 0 for Q satisfying Assumption 6.12(2)), the Pontryagin dual H⁰(X, ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O})^{α,β,∨}_{m_∅} is a free T^{α,β}_{σ,m_∅}-module.
items.note: This is the second conclusion of Theorem 9.1 (p. 879). It is missing for the same reasons as thm-9-1-R-min-equals-T.

items.name: The Taylor–Wiles patching datum for Theorem 9.1
items.statement:
(1) R = R^min and H = H⁰(X, ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O})^{α,β,∨}_{m_∅}.
(2) q = dim_k H¹_{∅*}(Q, ad⁰r̄(1)) ≥ 1, and for each N ≥ 1, Q_N is a set of q primes as in Proposition 4.10: x ≡ 1 mod p^N; r̄ unramified at x with r̄(Frob_x) having four distinct eigenvalues; H¹_{Q_N*}(Q, ad r̄(1)) = 0.
(3) R∞ = O[[x₁,…,x_{q−1}]].
(4) R_{Q_N} is the universal ring for deformations minimal outside Q_N (Definition 4.6). Choose a surjection R∞ ↠ R_{Q_N}, which exists by Proposition 4.10, and let φ_N : R∞ ↠ R_{Q_N} ↠ R^min be the composite. Δ is the unique quotient of Δ_{Q_N} = Π_{x∈Q_N}(Z/x)^× isomorphic to (Z/p^N Z)^q, and X_Δ(Q_N) → X_0(Q_N) is the corresponding subcover of X_1(Q_N) → X_0(Q_N) (§7.2). m_N ⊂ T_σ(Q_N) is the maximal ideal of Theorem 7.2: m_∅ together with xU_{x,2} − α′_xβ′_x and U_{x,1} − α′_x − β′_x for x ∈ Q_N. H_N := H⁰(X_Δ(Q_N), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O})^{α,β,∨}_{m_N}. It is an R∞-module via R∞ ↠ R_{Q_N} ↠ T_σ(Q_N)^{α,β}_{m_N}, the map classifying r_{Q_N} of Theorem 6.17. It is an S_N = O[(Z/p^N Z)^q]-module via the diamond operators and a chosen identification Δ ≅ (Z/p^N Z)^q.
items.note: The abstract patching datum is planned. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.5 has the reviewed node 'Balanced modules and Taylor–Wiles patching of modules (Calegari–Geraghty Proposition 2.3)', with S_N = O[(Z/p^N)^q], R∞ = O[[x₁,…,x_{q−1}]] and conditions (a)–(c). This GSp₄ instance is not planned: Taylor–Wiles sets for GSp₄ (Proposition 4.10), H_N at level X_Δ(Q_N) and the map R_{Q_N} → T_σ(Q_N). CG18's analogue patching-datum-weight-one was marked missing.

items.name: Condition (a) of Proposition 3.3: diamond operators come from R∞
items.statement: For each N, the image of S_N in End_O(H_N) is contained in the image of R∞. The printed reason is that under r_{Q_N} (Theorem 6.17), for x ∈ Q_N and σ ∈ I_x, r_{Q_N}(σ) is conjugate to diag(1, 1, ⟨u⟩, ⟨u⟩), where Art_x(u) = σ ([64, Corollary 3]); the diamond operators therefore lie in the image of R_{Q_N}.
items.note: This needs local–global compatibility at Taylor–Wiles primes for GSp₄ ([64, Cor. 3]; see ext-sorensen-cor-3), which is not planned.

items.name: Sorensen, local–global compatibility at Klingen-parahoric level ([64, Corollary 3])
items.statement: As invoked; the paper does not state it. Let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GSp₄ of cohomological weight with Galois representation ρ_π, and x ≠ p a prime such that π_x has nonzero Π⁺(x)-invariants on which Π(x)/Π⁺(x) ≅ (Z/x)^× acts through a character χ. Then ρ_π|I_x is governed by χ via local class field theory. As used on p. 879, σ ∈ I_x acts, up to conjugation, as diag(1, 1, χ(u), χ(u)) with Art_x(u) = σ: trivially on one isotropic plane and through χ∘Art_x⁻¹ on a complementary one. For r_{Q_N} this must be twisted to match Definition 4.6(5) [printed diag(1, 1, ⟨u⟩, ⟨u⟩); sourceIssues E129]. On p. 844 it is used to show that χ lifts ν∘r̄|I_x at primes of type P, and that Definition 4.6(5) holds at x ∈ Q.
items.locator: §9, proof of Theorem 9.1, step (a), p. 879 (also used in §6.3, p. 844)
items.note: No layer plans GSp₄ (Hilbert–Siegel) Galois representations or their local–global compatibility at x ≠ p: searches for Sorensen, Weissauer, Laumon, GSp₄ and Klingen found none. AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.5 plans 'Good-prime and ramified local–global comparison' for polarized GL_n only. ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.4 only registers 'Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs … transfer … local-global compatibilities' as source owners for classical groups. On p. 844 (proof of Theorem 6.13) the input is applied when π_x has nonzero Π(x)^+-invariants but no nonzero Π(x)-invariants, so that Π(x)/Π(x)^+ ≅ (Z/x)^× acts on π_x^{Π(x)^+} through a nontrivial character. It is used at primes of type P, where K_x = Π(x)^+, to get Definition 4.6(4), and at x ∈ Q to get Definition 4.6(5). That verification has to be run for the representation twisted by the inverse square root of χ_{μ,0} [sourceIssues E62]. External input: C. M. Sorensen, Galois representations attached to Hilbert–Siegel modular forms, Doc. Math. 15 (2010), 623–670, Corollary 3.

items.name: Condition (b) of Proposition 3.3: Δ_N-coinvariants of H_N recover H
items.statement: (H_N)_{Δ_N} = ((H⁰(X_Δ(Q_N), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O})^{α,β}_{m_N})^{Δ_N})^∨ = H⁰(X_0(Q_N), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O})^{α,β,∨}_{m_N}. Combine this with the isomorphism of Theorem 7.2 (Q = Q_N). That isomorphism is equivariant for T_{x,i} (x ∉ S ∪ Q_N ∪ {p}) and for T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2}, so it respects (α,β)-parts. The result is an isomorphism ψ_N : (H_N)_{Δ_N} ≅ H. ψ_N is R∞-linear, with R∞ acting on H through φ_N: both R∞-actions factor through the Hecke operators T_{x,i}, x ∉ S ∪ Q_N ∪ {p}, which are the images of traces of Frobenius (Chebotarev), and ψ_N is equivariant for these. The paper leaves this implicit.
items.note: This uses Pontryagin duality (planned elsewhere; CG18 used CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.3 and SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2), descent of H⁰ along X_Δ(Q_N) → X_0(Q_N), and the paper's Theorem 7.2 (no new (α,β)-classes at Taylor–Wiles level). The last two are not planned.

items.name: Condition (c) of Proposition 3.3: H_N is finite and balanced over S_N
items.statement: For each N, H_N is a finite S_N-module and is balanced over S_N (Definition 3.2: d_{S_N}(H_N) ≥ 0). The printed justification is 'by Theorem 7.11'.
items.note: Balancedness (Definition 3.2) is planned in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.5. Its verification here is the paper's Theorem 7.11 (coherent cohomology in degrees 0–1, with the H² vanishing of hypothesis (6)), which is not planned. CG18's analogues prop-3-8-balanced and HN-balanced-weight-one were marked missing.

items.name: Deduction of Theorem 9.1 from Proposition 3.3
items.statement: By (a)–(c), Proposition 3.3 (= CG18 Proposition 2.3) applies to the datum thm-9-1-patching-datum, so H is a finite free R^min-module. R^min acts on H through T^{α,β}_{σ,m_∅}, which acts faithfully on H, and R^min → T^{α,β}_{σ,m_∅} is surjective (T is generated by Hecke operators away from Np, which are coefficients of characteristic polynomials of Frobenius). Hence R^min → T^{α,β}_{σ,m_∅} is an isomorphism and H is a free T^{α,β}_{σ,m_∅}-module.
items.locator: §9, end of proof of Theorem 9.1, p. 880
items.note: The abstract Proposition 3.3 is planned (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.5), and so is the faithful/support conclusion (R03.6: 'Derive when a patched module is faithful…'). Their application to GSp₄, including surjectivity of R^min onto T^{α,β} and faithfulness of T on H, is not planned. CG18's analogue thm-3-26 was marked missing. The patched modules are H_N = H⁰(X_Δ(Q_N), ω(a,2)(−∞)_{K/O})^{α,β,∨}_{m_N} (p. 879). Step (c), that H_N is finite and balanced over S_N, is thm-9-1-step-c-balanced.

items.name: Jacquet–Shalika: simple pole of L(π × π^∨, s) at s = 1
items.statement: As cited: for a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL(n)/Q, the Rankin–Selberg L-function L(π × π^∨, s) is meromorphic for Re(s) > 0 and has a simple pole at s = 1.
items.note: The pole of L(π×π^∨, s) at s = 1 is the contragredient case that AL.3 retains. The libraries have no automorphic L-functions. External input: H. Jacquet and J. A. Shalika, On Euler products and the classification of automorphic forms, II, Amer. J. Math. 103 (1981), 777–815, cited as [43, Proposition 3.6].

items.name: Theorem A.1: the adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer group of a modular abelian surface vanishes
items.statement: Let A/Q be a semistable modular abelian surface with End(A) = Z. Let p be a prime such that (1) p is sufficiently large with respect to some constant depending only on A; (2) A is ordinary at p, and if α, β are the unit root eigenvalues (of crystalline Frobenius) on D_cris(V), then (α² − 1)(β² − 1)(α − β)(α²β² − 1) ≢ 0 mod p. Then H^1_f(Q, asp^0(r) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p) = 0, where asp^0(r) is the 10-dimensional adjoint representation of PGSp(4) composed with r. Moreover, the set of primes p satisfying these conditions has density 1. [The statement leaves V and r undefined (sourceIssues E134): V = H^1_et(A_{Q̄}, Q_p) is the p-adic realisation of A and r: G_Q → GSp_4(Z_p) the associated integral representation, whose ordinary shape at p is that of Theorem 9.1(1) with similitude ε^{−1}. 'Modular' means that A corresponds to a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GSp(4)/Q, that is, to a cuspidal Siegel modular form of scalar weight 2 (§A.3.2).]
items.locator: §A.1, Theorem A.1, p. 881; proof sketched in §A.4, pp. 888–890
items.note: No layer plans vanishing of adjoint (asp^0) Bloch–Kato Selmer groups for abelian surfaces or GSp4. PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.6 keeps general Bloch–Kato conjectural: 'Neither higher-rank BSD nor general Bloch–Kato follows from the rank-zero/one routes'. The proof needs Theorem 9.1 (main route), Lemmas A.5–A.8, and the identification of the tangent space at the O-point with H^1_f (item R-equals-T-equals-O-implies-selmer-vanishing). All of these are missing. Theorem A.1 is also announced in the introduction (§1, p. 803), as 'some cases of the Bloch–Kato conjecture for adjoint motives of modular abelian surfaces'.

items.name: Theorem A.2: conditional vanishing of adjoint Selmer groups for regular algebraic cusp forms on GL(n) over CM fields
items.statement: Let π be a weight 0 regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n)/F, for a CM field F, with coefficients in E. Let λ be a prime of O_E dividing p, and let r = r_λ(π): G_F → GL_n(O) be a p-adic representation associated to π with determinant ε^{n(1−n)/2}. Assume: (1) r̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} has enormous image in the sense of [16] (printed '[16, Section 9.2]'; the notion is in [16, §9.4]); (2) for every prime v ≠ p at which π is ramified: (a) π_v is an unramified twist of the Steinberg representation; (b) r|_{I_v} and r̄|_{I_v} are unipotent and, for a topological generator σ_v ∈ I_v of tame inertia, r̄(σ_v) consists of a single Jordan block, i.e. dim ker(r̄(σ_v) − id_n) = 1; (3) p is sufficiently large with respect to some constant depending only on π. Assume all of [16, Conjecture B] except assumption (4). Then the Selmer group H^1_f(F, ad^0(r) ⊗ K/O) is trivial.
items.locator: §A.1, Theorem A.2, pp. 881–882; proof in §A.4, pp. 888–889
items.note: This is conditional on CG18 Conjecture B without part (4). Of its inputs, only HLTT's Galois representations (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.4), the local rings (LocalGaloisDeformationRings:L7) and CG18 Theorem 6.4 (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.6) are planned. CG18 Conjecture B and Theorem 5.16 are missing in PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18.result.json (conj-B-*, thm-5-16), where they are routed to AutomorphyLiftingBeyondTaylorWiles. The appendix's replacement for Conjecture B(4) (Lemma A.3, Theorem A.4) is also missing.

items.name: Bloch–Kato Selmer groups H^1_f (with V and with V/T coefficients)
items.statement: Let F be a number field, K/Q_p finite with ring of integers O, V a de Rham p-adic representation of G_F over K, T ⊂ V a G_F-stable O-lattice and W = V/T. For a finite place v: if v ∤ p, H^1_f(F_v, V) = H^1(G_{F_v}/I_v, V^{I_v}) = ker(H^1(F_v, V) → H^1(I_v, V)); if v | p, H^1_f(F_v, V) = ker(H^1(F_v, V) → H^1(F_v, V ⊗_{Q_p} B_cris)); and H^1_f(F_v, W) is the image of H^1_f(F_v, V) under H^1(F_v, V) → H^1(F_v, W). Then H^1_f(F, V) (resp. H^1_f(F, W)) is the subgroup of classes in H^1(F, V) (resp. H^1(F, W)) whose restriction to every finite v lies in H^1_f(F_v, ·). The paper uses H^1_f(G_Q, V), H^1_f(Q, ad^0(M) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p), H^1_f(Q, ad^0(r) ⊗ K/O), H^1_f(Q, asp^0(r) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p) and H^1_f(F, ad^0(r) ⊗ K/O).
items.locator: §A.1, pp. 880–881 (used without definition); Theorems A.1 and A.2
items.note: L2 builds Selmer groups from local conditions over number fields, including unramified conditions and the passage from V to T and A = V/T. L4 adds the finite Bloch–Kato condition once period rings exist, and PadicHodgeRegulators:L1 supplies 'the finite local condition'. PAPER-DISEGNI-LIU-24/41 and PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26 (bk-selmer) are routed the same way. The paper uses H^1_f without defining it; the definition is Bloch–Kato [10], §3. External input: Bloch–Kato [10], 'L-functions and Tamagawa numbers of motives', §3 (the paper cites [10] on p. 880 but does not define H^1_f)

items.name: Adjoint objects ad^0(M), ad^0(r), asp^0(r)
items.statement: (i) For a pure irreducible motive M over Q with coefficients in E (under the standard conjectures), ad^0(M) is the pure motive of weight 0 with coefficients in E such that ad^0(M) ⊕ E = M ⊗ M^∨ (printed 'M × M^∨'), so L(ad^0(M), s) = L(π × π^∨, s)/ζ(s) when M corresponds to π. (ii) For a p-adic representation r: G → GL_n(O), ad^0(r) is r composed with the adjoint action on trace-zero matrices (dimension n² − 1). (iii) For r: G_Q → GSp_4(O), asp^0(r) is the 10-dimensional adjoint representation of PGSp(4), i.e. r composed with the adjoint action on Lie(PGSp_4) = sp_4 (p > 2). This is the ad^0(r) of main text §4, p. 813.
items.note: Coverage is partial. ad^0(r) for GL_n is planned in ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7 ('Construct the adjoint and trace-zero adjoint representations'). ad^0(M) as a motive needs MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.1's tensor products and duals together with the standard conjectures. asp^0(r) is planned nowhere: that is the adjoint action of a GSp4-valued r on sp4 = Lie(PGSp4), the representation in Theorem A.1. G7 plans polarizations of GL_n-valued representations over CM fields, not GSp4-valued ones. Mathlib has only near misses: LieAlgebra.Symplectic.sp (the skew-adjoint matrices for J, Mathlib/Algebra/Lie/Classical.lean) and Matrix.symplecticGroup (no similitude character). The paper also asserts (p. 880) that L(ad⁰(M), 1) is finite and nonzero. This rests on the result of Jacquet and Shalika cited there ([43, Proposition 3.6]): L(π × π^∨, s) has a simple pole at s = 1, which cancels the pole of ζ(s) (ext-jacquet-shalika-rankin-selberg-pole).

items.name: Conjecture: pure motives over Q are automorphic
items.statement: (Conjecture of Hasse–Weil, Langlands, Clozel and others, assuming the standard conjectures.) A pure irreducible Grothendieck motive M over Q with coefficients in a totally real field E, with no regularity or self-duality assumption, is automorphic: it corresponds to an algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL(n)/Q with L(π, s) = L(M, s).
items.note: The conjecture is planned as a statement with conjectural status, not as a theorem. Its scope is stated in the ML README: 'general functoriality, all motives automorphic and unrestricted categorical correspondences are research specifications, not assumed results'. The motive side (pure motives, standard conjectures) is in MC.1 and MC.7. Motivic L-functions are in PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.1 ('Define completed motivic L-functions from local Weil–Deligne data in admitted cases'). External input: Conjectures of Hasse–Weil, Langlands, Clozel (no specific citation in the paper)

items.name: Conjecture (Deligne, Bloch–Kato): order of vanishing and Selmer rank
items.statement: For any pure de Rham p-adic representation V of G_Q: dim H^1_f(G_Q, V) − dim H^0(G_Q, V) = ord_{s=1} L(V^*, s). In particular, for V = V^* = ad^0(M) (for which H^0 = 0 and L(ad^0(M), 1) is finite and non-zero), H^1_f(G_Q, ad^0(M)) should vanish.
items.note: The conjecture is planned as a conjectural declaration, and H^1_f comes from SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4. This follows the precedent PAPER-VENKATESH-19/12 ('The Bloch–Kato and Beilinson expectations'), which was marked planned at PS.3 and PS.6. The printed form, dim H^1_f(V) − dim H^0(V) = ord_{s=1} L(V^*, s), agrees with the usual form at s = 0 for V^*(1). The same paragraph of §A.1 (p. 880) goes on to the companion expectations recorded as conj-H1f-vanishing-weight-nonnegative and conj-bloch-kato-adjoint-special-value. External input: Deligne; Bloch–Kato [10] (conjecture)

items.name: Conjecture: H^1_f vanishes for pure motives of weight ≥ 0
items.statement: H^1_f(Q, V) = 0 for every p-adic representation V arising from a pure motive M of weight w ≥ 0. The vanishing of H^1_f(G_Q, ad^0(M)) (weight 0) is a special case.
items.note: This belongs to the general Bloch–Kato conjectural package that PS.6 and PS.7 register. For w ≥ 1 it follows from the order-of-vanishing conjecture: s = 1 lies in the region of absolute convergence of L(V^*, s), and H^0 = 0. The case w = 0 also needs nonvanishing on Re s = 1. The item should be stated as a separate conjectural declaration. External input: Bloch–Kato [10] (conjectural; the paper calls it 'the more general fact')

items.name: Conjecture: rationality of L(ad^0(M), 1) and the order of the Selmer group
items.statement: (a) After normalisation by a suitable (motivic) period, L(ad^0(M), 1) lies in Q^×. (b) Identifying M with its p-adic étale realisation, the p-adic valuation of the normalised value equals the valuation of the order of the Selmer group H^1_f(Q, ad^0(M) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p). §A.2 treats these as two separate conjectures: rationality of the period-normalised L(1), and equality of its p-adic valuation with the order of a Selmer group.
items.note: (a) Rationality of the period-normalised value is PS.1 when s = 1 is critical for ad^0(M), as for GL2 modular forms, and PS.3 (Beilinson-type) otherwise. (b) The equality of the p-adic valuation with the Selmer order is the p-primary Bloch–Kato statement of PS.6. Both are conjectural declarations. External input: Bloch–Kato [10] (Tamagawa number conjecture for ad^0(M)); related results on automorphic periods [5], [34], [69], and Hida [42]

items.name: Automorphic weakly compatible system of Galois representations
items.statement: M = {r_λ} is a weakly compatible system of n-dimensional irreducible representations of G_Q (indexed by places λ of a coefficient field E). It is automorphic if it corresponds to a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL(n)/Q compatibly with the local Langlands correspondence. For such M and a p-adic member r: G_Q → GL_n(O) (O the ring of integers of a finite K/Q_p) one asks whether H^1_f(Q, ad^0(r) ⊗ K/O) is finite.
items.note: Weakly compatible systems are planned in rank n. Compatibility with an automorphic π through local Langlands is AG2.5's local–global comparison, which uses ET.6's local Langlands.

items.name: Existence of Galois representations for regular algebraic cusp forms over CM fields (HLTT)
items.statement: For a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL(n) over a CM field F with coefficients in E, and each prime λ of O_E, there is a continuous semisimple representation r_λ(π): G_F → GL_n(Ē_λ), forming a weakly compatible system, compatible with the local Langlands correspondence at all but finitely many unramified places (Frobenius characteristic polynomials given by Hecke eigenvalues).
items.locator: §A.1, p. 881 ('families … whose existence was only recently proved to exist in [38]'); used to define r = r_λ(π) in Theorem A.2
items.note: HLTT is planned explicitly: the construction in AG2.4, good-prime unramifiedness and Frobenius polynomials in AG2.5, and the compatible system in AG2.6. AG2.4 warns not to promote the good-prime conclusion to full local–global compatibility, which is consistent with the appendix's reliance on Conjecture B. External input: Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne [38], printed as 'in preparation'; published as 'On the rigid cohomology of certain Shimura varieties', Res. Math. Sci. 3 (2016), Paper No. 37 (arXiv:1411.6717)

items.name: CG18 Conjecture B (existence and local properties of Galois representations for torsion cohomology; vanishing)
items.statement: ([16, §9.3, Conjecture B].) For a maximal ideal m of the anemic Hecke algebra T^an_{Q,ψ} acting on the cohomology of the arithmetic quotients Y_1(Q) of Res_{F/Q} PGL(n), there is a semisimple r̄_m: G_F → GL_n(T^an/m) with the prescribed Frobenius characteristic polynomials. If r̄_m is absolutely irreducible (m non-Eisenstein), it lifts to r_m: G_F → GL_n(T^an_{Q,ψ,m}), and if r̄_m ≅ r̄ and Q is a set of Taylor–Wiles primes, then: (1) for v | p, r_m|G_v is Fontaine–Laffaille with weights [0, 1, …, n−1]; (2) for v ∈ Q, r_m|G_v is of type D_v; (3) for v ∈ R, the characteristic polynomial of r_m(σ), σ ∈ I_v, is ∏(X − ψ_{v,i}(Art_v^{-1} σ)); (4)(a) H^i_ψ(Y_1(Q), O/ϖ^m)_m = 0 unless i ∈ [q_0, q_0 + l_0], (b) H^i_ψ(∂Y_1(Q), O/ϖ^m)_m = 0 for all i; (5) the Taylor–Wiles-level comparison H^*_ψ(Y, O/ϖ^m)_m ≅ H^*_ψ(Y_0(Q), O/ϖ^m)_{m_Q}.
items.locator: §A.1, Theorem A.2 and p. 882 ('[16, Conjecture B] consists of five parts'); p. 886 (Theorem A.4 replaces Conjecture B(4)); p. 889
items.note: In PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18.result.json every part of Conjecture B is missing: conj-B-residual-galois-rep, conj-B-lift-rm, conj-B-1 through conj-B-5, and conj-B-type-SQ-and-R-to-T-surjection. That route sends them to the proposed AutomorphyLiftingBeyondTaylorWiles. Only the Taylor–Wiles prime sets are planned (R04.5, G8). External input: Calegari–Geraghty [16], §9.3, Conjecture B, p. 414 (Invent. Math. 211)

items.name: Status of the parts of Conjecture B (remark with cited results)
items.statement: (Remark.) [16, Conjecture B] has five parts. Theorem A.2 assumes all but part (4); Theorem A.4 replaces (4). Part (1), local–global compatibility at v | p, is still open. Parts (2) and (3) concern local–global compatibility at finite v ∤ p. There is work in characteristic 0 by Varma [71], and arguments of this kind should also apply to Scholze's Galois representations for torsion classes [60], at least for modularity lifting purposes, where compatibility up to N-semisimplification usually suffices. Part (5) is essentially addressed in [16] and, differently (and 'arguably' better), in [46]. So the main remaining issue is local–global compatibility at ℓ = p. Results in this direction were announced in [1], but [1, Theorem 4.5.1] requires F to contain an imaginary quadratic field in which p splits, and that fails for a set of primes p of positive density. Even under such an assumption on p, one could not show that condition (2)(b) of Theorem A.2 holds for infinitely many p for a general π. The nilpotent ideal of [60] and [1] would be a further complication. The Steinberg hypothesis (2)(a) could in principle be weakened to π_v ≅ Sp_{n_1}(χ_1) ⊞ … ⊞ Sp_{n_k}(χ_k) with n = Σ n_i. That would require a more precise local–global compatibility at v ∤ p, i.e. a refinement of [16, Conjecture B].
items.note: Some of the cited results are planned: Varma's local–global compatibility at ℓ ≠ p in AG2.5 ('For the nonselfdual branch implement Varma's interpolation of local Hecke actions and nilpotent-orbit bounds'), Scholze's torsion Galois representations with a nilpotent ideal in TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure TC.0–TC.4 ('Export a quantified nilpotent ideal', TC.2), and the ACC+ local–global compatibility at p via degree shifting in PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.1 ('transfer the local p-adic Hodge condition'). Conjecture B itself is not planned. Nor is the Khare–Thorne or CG18 §9.4 treatment of part (5): CG18 thm-9-16 is missing, and its note says KT17's analogous lemmas are named in no layer. Nor is the Sp_{n_i}-type refinement of the Steinberg hypothesis. External input: Varma [71] (local–global compatibility at ℓ ≠ p); Scholze [60] (Galois representations for torsion classes); Khare–Thorne [46]; Allen–Calegari–Caraiani–Gee–Helm–Le Hung–Newton–Scholze–Taylor–Thorne [1, Theorem 4.5.1]

items.name: Theorem A.2's conclusion descends from an extension F'/F (remark)
items.statement: (Remark.) Let F′/F be a finite extension with Galois closure F″. If (ad^0 r̄)^{G_{F″}} = 0, then restriction H^1_f(F, ad^0(r) ⊗ K/O) → H^1_f(F′, ad^0(r) ⊗ K/O) is injective. This holds for example when r̄|G_{F″} is absolutely irreducible and p ∤ n, or when [F″:F] is prime to p. So the conclusion of Theorem A.2 for F follows from the same conclusion for r|G_{F′}. The paper states this for 'any extension F′/F' without the condition.
items.note: This needs restriction H^1_f(F, M) → H^1_f(F', M) to be injective. By inflation–restriction its kernel is H^1(Gal(F'/F), H^0(G_{F'}, M)), which vanishes when H^0(G_{F'}, ad^0 r ⊗ K/O) = 0, for instance when r̄|G_{F'} is absolutely irreducible and p ∤ n. The remark does not state this condition. The ingredients are in the libraries: mathlib:groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact (abstract groups, Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupCohomology/Functoriality.lean), tauceti:TauCeti.ContCohomology.explicitInfRes_exact and tauceti:TauCeti.ContCohomology.explicitInfl1_injective (continuous H^1, TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Inflation.lean). The Selmer-level statement is not planned.

items.name: Potential modularity of symmetric powers of non-CM elliptic curves over CM fields (ACC+)
items.statement: For a non-CM elliptic curve E over a CM field F, every symmetric power of E is potentially modular over some CM extension F'/F.
items.note: Potential automorphy over CM fields is assembled from PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, which is built from ACC+. The symmetric-power branches are in ML.3. This is consistent with PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/sato-tate-conjecture, which is planned at ML.3. External input: Allen–Calegari–Caraiani–Gee–Helm–Le Hung–Newton–Scholze–Taylor–Thorne [1] (arXiv:1812.09999)

items.name: Artin conjecture for odd two-dimensional representations over Q
items.statement: Every irreducible odd representation ρ: G_Q → GL_2(C) is modular of weight 1: there is a weight 1 cuspidal eigenform f with L(ρ, s) = L(f, s).
items.note: Weight-one modularity of odd Artin representations in the proved cases is ML.1. The solvable cases (Langlands–Tunnell) are R17.5. Serre's conjecture, from which the general odd case follows, is in ClassicalSerreModularity (R27.6, R33.1). External input: Buzzard [14], Buzzard–Taylor [15], Khare–Wintenberger [47], [48], Kisin [49]

items.name: Finiteness of the adjoint Selmer group of an Artin representation from the class group (remark)
items.statement: Let ρ: G_Q → GL_2(C) be irreducible and odd, and suppose ρ has a model over O (for a prime p). Then the finiteness of H^1_f(Q, ad^0(ρ) ⊗ K/O) follows from the finiteness of the p-part of the class group of the splitting field Q(ker ρ). The paper says 'the former is a quotient of the latter'.
items.note: The argument restricts to L = Q(ker ρ): the kernel H^1(Gal(L/Q), ·) is finite, and the image lies in Hom(G_L, ad^0 ρ ⊗ K/O)^{Gal(L/Q)} with local conditions forcing classes unramified over L, which the p-class group of L controls. No layer plans this comparison. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4 recovers class-group modules from Selmer groups of Tate twists, which is the nearest owner.

items.name: Weight one: adjoint Selmer group detected by congruences with Katz forms (remark following CG18)
items.statement: (Remark, following [16, Theorem 1.4].) Let ρ: G_Q → GL_2(C) be irreducible and odd, with weight 1 newform f, and suppose ρ has a model over O. Let p > 2 be a prime at which ρ is unramified and whose reduction ρ̄ is irreducible; this holds for all but finitely many p. Then R^min ≅ T_m, where T_m is the Hecke algebra acting on weight-1 Katz forms of the minimal level (coherent cohomology, O/ϖ^n coefficients). Hence H^1_f(Q, ad^0(ρ) ⊗ K/O) ≠ 0 if and only if T_m ≠ O, i.e. iff f has congruences (modulo powers of ϖ) with other weight 1 Katz forms, possibly ones that do not lift to characteristic 0. The paper states this 'at all primes p > 2 such that ρ is unramified'.
items.note: This is a consequence of CG18's minimal weight-one R = T (Theorems 1.4, 3.26 and 3.30). PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 marks those missing and routes them to the proposed GL2ModularityLiftingDefectOne. Katz weight-one forms without characteristic-zero lifts appear in AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.5. External input: Calegari–Geraghty [16] (weight one minimal R = T theorems, Theorems 1.4, 3.26 and 3.30 there)

items.name: For p large, the completed Hecke algebra at m is O
items.statement: If p is sufficiently large (with respect to the fixed automorphic representation π), then the completion of the appropriate Hecke algebra T at the maximal ideal m of residue characteristic p attached to π is formally smooth of dimension 1, i.e. T_m ≅ O. So the method proves modularity only of the characteristic-0 representation assumed modular, but it shows that this representation has no infinitesimal deformations.
items.locator: §A.3 (introduction), p. 884; used in §A.4, p. 888 ('one also will have an isomorphism T ≅ O')
items.note: No layer states that T_m ≅ O for p large. The proof needs: finitely many eigensystems; T torsion-free for large p; no congruences between distinct eigensystems outside the finitely many primes dividing a discriminant; and π's eigensystem defined over O_{E,v}. IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.2 plans image Hecke algebras and 'localization decompositions over complete coefficient rings', but not this large-p étaleness.

items.name: The invariants l_0 and q_0 for PGL(n) over an imaginary CM field of degree 2d
items.statement: For F an imaginary CM field of degree 2d: l_0 := d(rank SL_n(C) − rank SU_n(C)) = d(n − 1); 2q_0 + l_0 := d(dim SL_n(C) − dim SU_n(C)) = d(n² − 1); hence q_0 = d(n² − n)/2. Here rank means the absolute rank of the real Lie group (rank SL_n(C) = 2(n−1)) and dim the real dimension.
items.note: This is the same notion as PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/def-l0 and def-q0, both missing and routed there to AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups (AF.1, AF.4). No layer defines l0 = rank G(R) − rank K∞ or q0. I checked the values: l0 = d(n−1) and q0 = d(n²−n)/2 for 2d = [F:Q], with absolute ranks rank SL_n(C) = 2(n−1) and rank SU_n = n−1.

items.name: The arithmetic orbifold Y = Y(K) attached to π
items.statement: Fix a tempered cuspidal automorphic representation π of PGL(n)/F of weight 0 with coefficients in E (F imaginary CM). Y = Y(K) is the arithmetic orbifold of [16, §9] for Res_{F/Q} PGL(n), with level K = ∏ K_v maximal (PGL_n(O_{F_v})) at every prime where π is unramified and equal to the Iwahori subgroup Iw_v at every prime where π is ramified. For a finite set Q of primes (disjoint from the level and p), Y_0(Q) and Y_1(Q) denote the corresponding Γ_0(Q)- and Γ_1(Q)-type quotients of [16, §9.1]. Y_1(Q) → Y_0(Q) is Galois with group Δ_Q = ∏_{x∈Q} (O_F/x)^×.
items.note: Parts are planned. Y(K) for a compact open K is ALS.0 ('Prove the finite decomposition of X_K into arithmetic Γ-components ... proper discontinuity and, at neat level, freeness'). Iwahori subgroups are the parahorics of ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3 ('For a facet construct the smooth affine O_E-group scheme'). The Taylor–Wiles-level quotients Y_0(Q), Y_1(Q) with covering group Δ_Q = ∏(O_F/x)^× are planned nowhere. This is consistent with PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/levels-KQ-LQ-Y0Q-Y1Q and local-level-subgroups, both missing and routed to ALS.0/ALS.3. External input: Calegari–Geraghty [16], §9 and §9.1

items.name: The anemic Hecke algebra T (Betti case)
items.statement: T is the Z-subalgebra of End(⊕_{k,m} H^k(Y(K), Z/mZ)) generated by the Hecke endomorphisms T_{α,i} for i ≤ n and α (idèles) that are units at the primes dividing the level. T_Q denotes the Hecke algebra consisting of the Hecke operators prime to p and to the level together with U_x − α_x for x ∈ Q (Theorem A.4(2)).
items.note: The anemic T can be assembled from planned pieces: operators T_{v,i} (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.3), correspondences on complexes (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.3) and finite image algebras (IHG.2). The Taylor–Wiles-level T_Q with U_x − α_x at x ∈ Q is not planned, matching PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/def-9-1-hecke-algebra-TQ and hecke-algebra-T-an-galois-rep (both missing). External input: Calegari–Geraghty [16], Definition 9.1 (cited 'cf.')

items.name: Residual representation r̄_v and maximal ideal m (Betti case)
items.statement: For a prime v of O_E, r̄_v: G_F → GL_n(k) (k the residue field of O_{E,v}) is the semisimple reduction of the Galois representation attached to π, and m ⊂ T is the corresponding maximal ideal: the kernel of the map T → k sending T_{α,i} to the reduction of π's Hecke eigenvalue.
items.note: The residual representation r̄_v of π is planned in AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.7 ('Prove the reduction of each good-prime polynomial and independence of the associated maximal Hecke ideal'). The maximal ideal m of the Betti Hecke algebra T of Y(K) is not planned. It needs T (see def-anemic-hecke-algebra-T-betti) and the occurrence of π in H^*(Y(K)) (Franke; Borel–Wallach), both missing. CG18's non-eisenstein-max-ideal-GLn is also missing.

items.name: Lemma A.3: vanishing of localised Betti cohomology outside [q_0, q_0 + l_0] for large v
items.statement: In the setting of §A.3.1 (π a tempered cuspidal automorphic representation of PGL(n)/F of weight 0, F imaginary CM of degree 2d, Y = Y(K), T, r̄_v and m as defined), for all primes v of O_E of sufficiently large residue characteristic, with O = O_{E,v} and uniformiser ϖ, H^i(Y, O/ϖ^k)_m = 0 for every k ≥ 1 unless i ∈ [q_0, …, q_0 + l_0].
