items.note: This is the unconditional large-p replacement for CG18 Conjecture B(4)(a). Among its inputs only finite generation (ALS.1/ALS.2/ALS.6) is planned. Franke–Schwermer, Borel–Wallach/Clozel and Jacquet–Shalika strong multiplicity one are missing (separate items).

items.name: Finite generation and torsion-freeness of the cohomology of Y for large p
items.statement: Let K' ⊂ K be a neat normal subgroup of finite index, so that Y' = Y(K') is a manifold and Y' → Y is a Galois cover; let M be the product of the primes dividing [K : K']. Then H^*(Y', Z) is finitely generated, hence H^*(Y, Z[1/M]) is finitely generated. Consequently, for O of sufficiently large residue characteristic (prime to M), H^i(Y, O) = H^i(Y, Z[1/M]) ⊗ O is torsion-free of finite rank for all i, and only finitely many systems of Hecke eigenvalues occur in H^*(Y, R) (equivalently H^*(Y, C)).
items.note: Finite projective cochain models at neat level, together with compactness and homotopy equivalence of the Borel–Serre compactification, give finite generation. Descent to Y with |K/K'| inverted is the finite-cover Hochschild–Serre application of ALS.6. Torsion-freeness for large residue characteristic and the finiteness of eigensystems follow at once. External input: Standard (Borel–Serre compactification: Y' is homotopy equivalent to a compact manifold with boundary); no citation in the paper

items.name: Franke–Schwermer: cohomology eigenclasses come from isobaric automorphic representations
items.statement: Every Hecke eigenclass in H^*(Y, C) is realised by an isobaric automorphic representation Π of GL(n)/F (PGL(n)): its Hecke eigenvalues at almost all places are those of Π.
items.note: AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.5 plans Franke's comparison: 'compare relative Lie algebra cohomology of automorphic forms with that of all smooth functions of the required growth'. AS.4 plans the L² decomposition along cuspidal data. Two things are planned nowhere: the Franke–Schwermer decomposition of the space of automorphic forms along cuspidal support ([28, Theorem 2.3]), and the realisation of Hecke eigenclasses by isobaric Π. External input: Franke–Schwermer [28, Theorem 2.3]

items.name: Cohomology outside [q_0, q_0 + l_0] comes from non-tempered representations
items.statement: If an isobaric automorphic representation Π of PGL(n)/F contributes to H^i(Y, C) with i ∉ [q_0, q_0 + l_0], then Π (at ∞) is not tempered. Equivalently, representations tempered at ∞ contribute to cohomology only in degrees [q_0, q_0 + l_0].
items.note: This is the same theorem as PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/ext-borel-wallach and l0-q0-cohomological-range. Both are missing: AF.1 defines relative Lie algebra cochains and AF.4 cohomological representations, but no layer computes the (g,K)-cohomology range of tempered representations. Clozel's Lemme 3.14 (purity) is not planned either. External input: Borel–Wallach [11, Chapter II, Proposition 3.1]; Clozel [19, Lemme 3.14]

items.name: Jacquet–Shalika strong multiplicity one for isobaric representations
items.statement: If two isobaric automorphic representations of GL(n) over a number field have isomorphic local components at almost all places (equivalently, the same Hecke eigenvalues at almost all unramified places), then they are isomorphic. In Lemma A.3 this gives Π ≅ π, and in Lemma A.5 it gives agreement of the transfers to GL(4).
items.locator: §A.3.1, proof of Lemma A.3, p. 885; §A.3.2, proof of Lemma A.5, p. 887 ('by multiplicity 1')
items.note: Strong multiplicity one is planned only for GL2: GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.4 ('Prove strong multiplicity one with a precise set of places'), plus Tau Ceti ModularForms layer 5 for newforms. AF.2 states 'General automorphic multiplicities remain finite integers, not forced to equal one.' No layer plans GL_n strong multiplicity one for isobaric representations. Lemma A.5 also uses it for the GL4 transfers. External input: Jacquet–Shalika [43]

items.name: Taylor–Wiles data with distinct Frobenius eigenvalues; the maximal ideal m_α
items.statement: Q is a finite set of primes x of F such that N(x) ≡ 1 mod p and r̄(Frob_x) has n distinct eigenvalues. α = {α_x}_{x|Q} is a choice, for each x | Q, of an eigenvalue α_x of r̄(Frob_x). m_α is the maximal ideal of T_Q (the Hecke operators prime to p and the level, together with U_x − α_x for x ∈ Q) generated by m and the U_x − α_x (α_x lifted to O). In the coherent case (§A.3.2) the same notation is used for X_0(Q), X_1(Q) with r̄_p. m_Q denotes the maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra in which the operators at Q and at p are omitted.
items.locator: §A.3.1, Theorem A.4 and (1)–(2), pp. 885–886; §A.3.2, Lemmas A.5 and A.6, p. 887
items.note: The Galois side is planned: GlobalGaloisDeformations:G7 ('Prove the arbitrary-n auxiliary-prime lemma with prescribed distinct Frobenius eigenvalues and chosen eigenspaces, q_v≡1 mod p^N'), R04.5, and PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.4 ('selected eigenvalues'). The Hecke side is not: the ideal m_α ⊂ T_Q generated by m and the U_x − α_x (see def-anemic-hecke-algebra-T-betti), its coherent analogue, and m_Q.

items.name: Enormous image (CG18)
items.statement: r̄: G_F → GL_n(k) has enormous image if r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is big (in the sense of [20, Definition 2.5.1]) and, in addition, there exist suitable Taylor–Wiles primes x (N(x) ≡ 1 mod p) such that r̄(Frob_x) has distinct eigenvalues. In the appendix's use, enormous image of r̄_v|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} implies that there exist arbitrarily many sets Q of auxiliary Taylor–Wiles primes with r̄(Frob_x) having distinct eigenvalues.
items.note: This matches PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/enormous-image, which is planned at the same stages. CG's notion is informal. The atlas plans the precise ACC+ Definition 6.2.29, and the formal item should use that definition. The paper prints '[16, Section 9.2]'; the notion is in [16, §9.4]. External input: Calegari–Geraghty [16], §9.4 (introduction), p. 419 (an informal definition); precise versions: Khare–Thorne [46], and [1, Definition 6.2.29]

items.name: Theorem A.4: vanishing outside [q_0, q_0 + l_0] at Taylor–Wiles level
items.statement: In the setting of §A.3.1, assume r̄ is absolutely irreducible (used in the proof but omitted from the printed statement). Suppose that H^i(Y, O/ϖ^n)_m = 0 unless i ∈ [q_0, …, q_0 + l_0]. Let Q be a finite set of primes x such that r̄(Frob_x) has distinct eigenvalues and N(x) ≡ 1 mod p, let α = {α_x} be a choice of eigenvalues of r̄(Frob_x) for each x | Q, and localise with respect to the Hecke algebra T_Q consisting of the Hecke operators prime to p and to the level together with U_x − α_x for all x ∈ Q. Then H^i(Y_1(Q), O/ϖ^n)_{m_α} = 0 for all i ∉ [q_0, …, q_0 + l_0]. In particular, by Lemma A.3, the conclusion holds for all sufficiently large p.
items.note: This replaces CG18 Conjecture B(4) at Taylor–Wiles level, and nothing plans it. Its inputs, all missing, are boundary vanishing, Poincaré duality (planned, ALS.5), the Hochschild–Serre descent, and the level-raising comparison H^i(Y_0(Q),k)_{m_α} ≅ H^i(Y,k)_m. The Hochschild–Serre step from Y_1(Q) to Y_0(Q) uses Δ_Q = ∏(O_F/x)^×, which is not a p-group, so it needs the prime-to-p part to act trivially after localisation. See clusterNotes.

items.name: Localised boundary cohomology vanishes at an absolutely irreducible r̄
items.statement: If r̄ is absolutely irreducible, then the cohomology of the (Borel–Serre) boundary of Y_1(Q) (and of Y, Y_0(Q)) with O/ϖ^n coefficients vanishes after localisation at m. Reason: boundary cohomology is computed inductively from the cohomology of Levi subgroups, hence of GL_{n_i} with n_i < n, whose associated Galois representations are reducible.
items.note: ALS.4 plans the boundary triangle and the Levi Hochschild–Serre sequences, and asks for an eigenvalue argument: 'Describe conditions under which boundary localization vanishes ... by an actual eigenvalue argument; the phrase non-Eisenstein alone is not a proof of vanishing for arbitrary groups.' The GL_n statement needs more than that: Galois representations for torsion classes on the Levi quotients (TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure) and Caraiani–Le Hung's inductive computation ([17, §3, Prop. 3.3]). Neither is planned for this use. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/conj-B-4b-boundary-vanishing is missing. External input: Caraiani–Le Hung [17, §3, Proposition 3.3] (cited 'see, e.g.')

items.name: Poincaré duality reduces vanishing to degrees below q_0
items.statement: Let D = 2q_0 + l_0 = dim_R Y_1(Q). If the localised boundary cohomology vanishes, Poincaré duality identifies H^i(Y_1(Q), O/ϖ^n)_{m_α} with the dual of H^{D−i}(Y_1(Q), O/ϖ^n) localised at the dual maximal ideal. So vanishing for all i > q_0 + l_0 follows from vanishing for all i < q_0 (applied also to the dual ideal).
items.note: Finite-level Poincaré–Lefschetz duality with Hecke adjoints and the boundary triangle is planned. The dual maximal ideal m^* is planned there too (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/dual-maximal-ideal-m-star). The reduction to degrees below q0 is one line, but applying it needs the hypothesis for m^* as well (Lemma A.3 applied to π^∨). External input: Poincaré duality for (orbifold) arithmetic quotients; cf. CG18 item poincare-duality-bm

items.name: Lowest non-vanishing degree descends along a p-group cover (Hochschild–Serre)
items.statement: Let Y' → Y'' be a finite Galois covering with group Δ, let F be a sheaf of k-vector spaces (char k = p) with a Hecke action compatible with the covering, and let i be the least degree with H^i(Y', F)_m ≠ 0. If Δ is a p-group, or more generally if Δ acts on H^i(Y', F)_m through a p-group (e.g. the prime-to-p part of Δ acts trivially after localisation), then H^i(Y'', F)_m ≠ 0. By Hochschild–Serre, E_2^{a,b} = H^a(Δ, H^b(Y', F)_m) ⇒ H^{a+b}(Y'', F)_m, and E_2^{0,i} = H^i(Y', F)_m^Δ ≠ 0 survives to E_∞.
items.locator: §A.3.1, proof of Theorem A.4 (Y_1(Q) → Y_0(Q)), p. 886; §A.3.2, proof of Lemma A.6 (X_1(Q) → X_0(Q)), p. 888
items.note: The Betti Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence with its Hecke action is planned (ALS.6: 'the finite-cover Hochschild–Serre application'; PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/hochschild-serre-hecke is planned at ALS.6/P7/IHG.2). The Hecke-equivariant coherent version is missing (CG18 hochschild-serre-coherent). The lemma itself is planned nowhere: the lowest nonvanishing degree survives, and a p-group has nonzero invariants on a nonzero F_p-module. In both of the paper's uses (Y_1(Q) → Y_0(Q), X_1(Q) → X_0(Q)) the group is not a p-group. External input: Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence (standard); cf. CG18 item hochschild-serre-hecke

items.name: No new cohomology at Taylor–Wiles level with distinct eigenvalues: H^i(Y_0(Q), k)_{m_α} ≅ H^i(Y, k)_m
items.statement: For Q a set of primes x with N(x) ≡ 1 mod p and r̄(Frob_x) having distinct eigenvalues, and α a choice of eigenvalues, there is an isomorphism H^i(Y_0(Q), k)_{m_α} ≅ H^i(Y, k)_m for all i (induced by the natural maps together with the U_x-projection onto the α_x-part).
items.note: This is PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/conj-B5-via-thm-9-16 (missing, routed to AutomorphyLiftingBeyondTaylorWiles). Its local input thm-9-16 is also missing (routed source to SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0/SR.5). Khare–Thorne [46, Lemma 6.25] is named in no layer; the CG18 note says PA.4 only 'identif[ies] its specialization with the original complex'. External input: Calegari–Geraghty [16, §9.4] (Theorem 9.16 and the informal §9.4.2); Khare–Thorne [46, Lemma 6.25(4)]

items.name: Coherent set-up: Siegel 3-fold, compactifications and ω
items.statement: O is the ring of integers of a finite extension of Q_p. Y is a Siegel 3-fold of level prime to p over Spec O. X is a (smooth) toroidal compactification of Y and Z the minimal compactification. π: A → Y is the universal abelian surface, E = π_*Ω^1_{A/Y} (printed Ω^1_{A/X}), and ω = det E. By abuse of notation, ω also denotes the canonical extension of ω to X and the corresponding ample line bundle on Z. ω² = ω(2,2) is the sheaf of scalar weight 2 Siegel modular forms, ω²_{O/ϖ^n} = ω² ⊗ O/ϖ^n, and ω(−∞) is the subcanonical extension (twist by the boundary divisor). X_0(Q) and X_1(Q) are the toroidal compactifications at levels K_0(Q) and K_1(Q) (main text §5.2); X_1(Q) → X_0(Q) is finite étale Galois with group (Z/Q)^×.
items.locator: §A.3.2, p. 886; X_0(Q), X_1(Q), ω(−∞) used in Lemma A.6 and its proof, pp. 887–888
items.note: Most of the setup is planned. Planned pieces: Siegel moduli (PELModuli:M5, 'Construct Siegel moduli for every dimension'), the universal abelian scheme and Hodge line (M6), integral toroidal and minimal compactifications (ShimuraCompactifications:C5: 'integral toroidal algebraic spaces with their universal semi-abelian extensions ... Hodge-line positivity ... integral minimal compactification, then its projectivity'), and characteristic-zero canonical/subcanonical extensions with the Siegel Hodge bundle (AutomorphicBundles:B3/B4). Not planned: the integral subcanonical ω(−∞) over O/ϖ^n with Hecke action (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/coherent-setup is missing for this reason), and the compactified Taylor–Wiles covers X_1(Q) → X_0(Q) as finite étale Galois covers with group (Z/Q)^×, whose levels are defined in main-text §5.2. The paper prints Ω^1_{A/X}; Ω^1_{A/Y} is meant.

items.name: Coherent case: π for a modular abelian surface, r̄_p, m, m_Q
items.statement: Fix a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GSp(4)/Q corresponding to a modular abelian surface A with End_Q(A) = Z, hence to a cuspidal Siegel modular form of scalar weight 2. For each prime p, r̄_p: G_Q → GSp_4(F_p) is the corresponding semisimple residual representation and m is the corresponding maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra T (operators away from p and the level) acting on the coherent cohomology of X. For a set Q of auxiliary primes, m_Q is the maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra in which the operators at Q and at p are omitted.
items.note: r̄_p = A[p] is available from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6 (Tate modules of abelian varieties). Two pieces are planned nowhere: Galois representations attached to Siegel cusp forms (AG2 covers GL_n/unitary and R19 covers GL2), and the Hecke algebra on the integral coherent cohomology of Siegel threefolds with its maximal ideals m, m_Q (CG18's coherent Hecke operators are missing).

items.name: Lemma A.5: vanishing of H² and H³ of ω² at full level for large p
items.statement: In the setting of §A.3.2, for all sufficiently large p and any set Q of auxiliary primes, H^i(X, ω²_{O/ϖ^n})_{m_Q} = 0 for i = 2 and 3 (and all n ≥ 1), where m_Q is the maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra in which the operators at Q and p are omitted. Here ω² is the square of the canonical extension ω.
items.note: The proof sketch needs large-p finiteness as in Lemma A.3, the GSp4 → GL4 transfer with multiplicity one (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.4 keeps the symplectic branch conditional: 'The symplectic torsion branch has a named source-verification/construction task'), and the coherent degrees (0 and 1) of the holomorphic Siegel constituents. None of this is planned.

items.name: Lemma A.6: vanishing of H^{≥2} of ω² at Taylor–Wiles level
items.statement: In the setting of §A.3.2, suppose that H²(X, ω²_{O/ϖ^n})_{m_Q} = 0 for every set Q of auxiliary primes (as in Lemma A.5), and that r̄_p is absolutely irreducible. [The proof also needs H³(X, ω²_{O/ϖ^n})_{m_Q} = 0, which Lemma A.5 provides; recorded gap.] Let Q be any set of primes x such that r̄_p(Frob_x) has distinct eigenvalues and N(x) ≡ 1 mod p, and let α = {α_x} be any collection of eigenvalues of r̄_p(Frob_x) (printed 'ρ(Frob_x)') for x | Q. Then for all i ≥ 2: H^i(X_1(Q), ω²_{O/ϖ^n})_{m_α} = H^i(X_0(Q), ω²_{O/ϖ^n})_{m_α} = 0. In particular (with Lemma A.5), the conclusion holds for all sufficiently large p.
items.note: This is the coherent analogue of Theorem A.4. Its inputs are all missing: Serre duality with Hecke twist, coherent Hochschild–Serre for X_1(Q) → X_0(Q) (not a p-group cover), and BCGP Proposition 7.9.8. There is also a recorded gap: the hypothesis should include H³ vanishing.

items.name: Serre duality on the Siegel 3-fold, Hecke-equivariant up to a cyclotomic twist
items.statement: On X (and on X_0(Q), X_1(Q)), smooth and proper of relative dimension 3 over O with dualizing sheaf ω³(−∞), H^i(X, ω²_k) is dual to H^{3−i}(X, ω(−∞)_k), since (ω²)^∨ ⊗ ω³(−∞) = ω(−∞). The duality is Hecke-equivariant only up to a twist by a power of the cyclotomic character, so localisation at m on one side corresponds to localisation at the twisted ideal m^* on the other.
items.note: Grothendieck–Serre duality in relative dimension > 1 over O/ϖ^n is planned nowhere. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/verdier-serre-duality is missing and routed to AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension; only curve duality is planned (Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge layer B, SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.3). The Hecke-equivariance up to a cyclotomic twist on Siegel threefolds is not planned either. External input: Grothendieck–Serre duality; main text §5.3 (p. 830: ω(a,b)^∨ ⊗ det Ω^1 ≅ ω(3−b, 3−a)(−∞)) and §7.2 (p. 851: ω³(−∞) is dualizing)

items.name: BCGP: coherent cohomology at Taylor–Wiles level with distinct eigenvalues (GSp4)
items.statement: For Q a set of Taylor–Wiles primes x (x ≡ 1 mod p, r̄_p(Frob_x) with distinct eigenvalues) and α a choice of eigenvalues, the localised coherent cohomology groups H^i(X_0(Q), ·)_{m_α} are identified with H^i(X, ·)_{m_Q} for all i. In particular, if i is least with H^i(X_0(Q), ω(−∞)_k)_{m^*_α} ≠ 0, then H^i(X, ω(−∞)_k)_{m^*_Q} ≠ 0.
items.note: This is BCGP (arXiv:1812.09269), Proposition 7.9.8 with Lemmas 2.4.36–2.4.37. The papers.json guide routes PAPER-BCGP18 to a new roadmap, AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity (DESIGN-BCGP18, still pending in queue.json), so it has no layers yet. No atlas layer plans coherent Taylor–Wiles comparisons for GSp4. External input: Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni [13, Proposition 7.9.8, using Lemmas 2.4.36 and 2.4.37; Sections 2.4 and 7.9] (arXiv:1812.09269v1 numbering); Khare–Thorne [46, Lemma 6.25]

items.name: R in the Betti case: minimal deformation ring with Fontaine–Laffaille condition at p
items.statement: In the Betti (GL(n)/F, F CM) case, R is the minimal deformation ring of r̄ (determinant fixed as in Theorem A.2) for the following local conditions: (a) if v is a prime of bad reduction (so r̄(σ) is unipotent with a single Jordan block for a topological generator σ of tame inertia), the local deformation ring is R^1_v of [16, §8.5.1] (lifts on which every σ ∈ I_v has characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n); (b) if v | p and p is sufficiently large with respect to n and the primes ramified in F, the deformations are Fontaine–Laffaille of weight [0, 1, …, n−1]; unramified at all other primes.
items.note: Planned piece by piece, as in PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/deformation-problem-RQ, unipotent-framed-ring-R1v and fl-framed-deformation-ring-Rv, which are all planned: the fixed-determinant rank-n global problem (G8), assembly from prescribed local rings (R04.3), Fontaine–Laffaille and unipotent/minimally ramified local conditions (L7, R08.2). External input: Calegari–Geraghty [16, §8.5.1] (R^1_v); Clozel–Harris–Taylor [20] (Fontaine–Laffaille deformations)

items.name: Unipotent lifts of a regular unipotent residual monodromy are minimally ramified
items.statement: Let A be an object of C_O, let r be a lift to A of r̄|_{G_v} (v ∤ p) such that r̄(σ) is unipotent with a single Jordan block, σ a topological generator of tame inertia, and suppose r(σ) acting on A^n has characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n. Then for every j ≤ n the natural map ker((r(σ) − id_n)^j) ⊗_A k → ker((r̄(σ) − id_n)^j) is an isomorphism (equivalently, a surjection). Hence the R^1_v deformation problem coincides, under this assumption on r̄, with the minimally ramified condition of [20, Definition 2.4.14].
items.note: L7 and R08.2 plan the minimally ramified and the unipotent (R^1_v) conditions separately. Neither plans the lemma that the two coincide when r̄(σ) is a single Jordan block. The paper prints '⊗_R k'; ⊗_A k is meant. External input: Clozel–Harris–Taylor [20, Definition 2.4.14] (minimal condition)

items.name: Formal smoothness of the local deformation rings (Fontaine–Laffaille; minimally ramified)
items.statement: (i) For v | p with F_v/Q_p unramified and p > n, the Fontaine–Laffaille local deformation ring with weights [0, …, n−1] is formally smooth over O. (ii) The minimally ramified local deformation ring at v ∤ p is formally smooth over O. Consequently the local deformation rings in the Betti-case definition of R are formally smooth.
items.note: Formal smoothness is planned for both local conditions. This matches PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/cht-prop-2-4-3-fl-smooth, planned at L7. The fixed-determinant dimension count must be recomputed there. External input: Clozel–Harris–Taylor [20, Corollary 2.4.3, Lemma 2.4.19] (as cited)

items.name: CG18 Theorem 5.16: conditional modularity lifting for GL(n) over a number field
items.statement: ([16, Theorem 5.16].) Assume [16, Conjecture B]. Let F/Q be a number field, n ≥ 1, and p > n a prime unramified in F. Let r: G_F → GL_n(O) be continuous and unramified outside finitely many primes, with reduction r̄: G_F → GL_n(k). Suppose: (1) for v | p, r|D_v is crystalline; (2) for v | p, gr^i(r ⊗_{Z_p} B_dR)^{D_v} = 0 unless i ∈ {0,1,…,n−1}, in which case it is free of rank 1 over O ⊗_{Z_p} F_v; (3) r̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} is absolutely irreducible and F(ad^0 r̄) does not contain F(ζ_p); (4) r̄ is big in the sense of [CHT, Definition 2.5.1]; (5) r|G_{F_v} is odd for every real place v; (6) if r is ramified at x then r|I_x is unipotent, and if moreover r̄ is unramified at x then N(x) ≡ 1 mod p; (7) det r = ε^{n(n−1)/2}; (8) either (a) there is a cuspidal automorphic representation π_0 of GL_n(A_F) with trivial infinitesimal character at all v | ∞ and good reduction at all v | p, whose p-adic Galois representation satisfies (6) and has reduction r̄, or (b) r̄ is Serre modular of minimal level N(r̄) and r is ramified only at primes where r̄ is ramified. Then r is modular: there is a regular algebraic cusp form π for GL_n(A_F) with trivial infinitesimal character and L(r,s) = L(π,s). The theorem follows from [16, Theorem 9.19]: H^{q_0}(Y,K/O)^∨_m is a nearly faithful R_S-module. The isomorphism R_S ≅ T_m, with freeness, which Theorem A.2 uses, comes from [16, Theorem 6.4(1)] when the local deformation rings are formally smooth. (Theorem A.2 writes det r = ε^{n(1−n)/2}. That is the sign forced by (2) under the standard B_dR convention.)
items.locator: §A.4, p. 888 ('Theorem A.2 is now a consequence of [16, Theorems 5.16 and 6.4]')
items.note: This is PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/thm-5-16, which is missing ('No layer states a GL_n modularity lifting theorem over an arbitrary number field conditional on Conjecture B') and routed to AutomorphyLiftingBeyondTaylorWiles. External input: Calegari–Geraghty [16], Theorem 5.16, pp. 383–384 (proved via Theorem 9.19)

items.name: CG18 Theorem 6.4: freeness and R = T when the patched ring is formally smooth
items.statement: ([16, Theorem 6.4].) Keep the situation of [16, Theorem 6.3]: patched perfect complexes of length l_0 over S_N = O[(Z/p^N)^q], R_∞ ∈ C_O of Krull dimension 1 + j + q − l_0, O′ = O[[z_1,…,z_j]], a patched complex P_∞ with ψ_∞: H^{l_0}(P′_∞)/a ≅ H, and φ_∞: R_∞ ↠ R. Suppose in addition that R_∞ is p-torsion free. (1) If R_∞ is formally smooth over O (R_∞ ≅ O[[x_1,…,x_{q+j−l_0}]]), then H is a free R-module. In the proof, H^{l_0}(P′_∞) is free over R′_∞ and ker(φ_∞) = ı(a)R′_∞. (2) If R_∞[1/p] is irreducible, H is a nearly faithful R-module. (3) More generally, H is nearly faithful over R if every irreducible component of Spec R_∞[1/p] lies in the support of H^{l_0}(P_∞)[1/p]. Consequence: in case (1), R acts faithfully on H. If the R-action factors through a quotient T of R (e.g. a Hecke algebra), then R ≅ T.
items.note: This is planned in the reviewed R03.6 node, whose sources cite 'CalegariGeraghty-2018, §6.1, Theorem 6.4 with proof'. It matches PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/thm-6-4-1-freeness (planned R03.6, including ker φ∞ = ı(a)R∞). External input: Calegari–Geraghty [16], Theorem 6.4(1), p. 389

items.name: R ≅ T and T ≅ O imply vanishing of the adjoint Selmer group
items.statement: If R ≅ T for all sufficiently large p satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem A.1 (resp. A.2), then, since also T ≅ O for such p, the tangent space of R along the projection R → O is trivial: with p_R = ker(R → O), Hom_O(p_R/p_R², K/O) = 0. Hence the corresponding adjoint Selmer group, H^1_f(Q, asp^0(r) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p) (resp. H^1_f(F, ad^0(r) ⊗ K/O)), is trivial.
items.note: Residual tangent spaces are planned: GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3 ('Prove tangent and obstruction descriptions by the actual adjoint cohomology and the local conditions') and ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.5 ('Relate tangent conditions of finite-flat, ordinary and fixed-type deformation problems to the corresponding local H¹ subspaces'). What is missing is the identification at a characteristic-zero point, Hom_O(p_R/p_R², K/O) ≅ H^1_f(ad^0 r ⊗ K/O) (resp. asp^0), with the deformation conditions matched to Bloch–Kato's: Fontaine–Laffaille or ordinary at p, minimal at ℓ ≠ p.

items.name: Application of Theorem 9.1 in weight (2,2) to prove Theorem A.1
items.statement: Theorem A.1 follows 'as in Theorem 1.2', i.e. from Theorem 9.1 with a = 2: for r̄ = r̄_p of A, which for large p is odd and absolutely irreducible, has similitude ε^{−1}, big image (Assumption 4.1), is neat (Assumption 4.2), has ramification of types U1/U2 at ℓ | N (Assumption 4.3; Lemma A.7(1)), is ordinary with the α,β condition (Lemma A.7(2)) and is Katz modular of weight (2,2) (A is modular), and with hypothesis (6) supplied by Lemma A.6 'in place of the vanishing results of Lan and Suh [53]', one gets R^min ≅ T^{α,β}_{σ,m_∅}.
items.note: This applies the paper's main theorem. It needs Lemma A.6 to replace Lan–Suh vanishing, and Lemma A.7 for Assumptions 4.1 and 4.3 and the ordinary condition. Nothing is planned.

items.name: Lemma A.7(1): surjective residual image with minimal conductor
items.statement: Let A be a semistable abelian surface over Q of conductor N with End(A) = Z. Then for all sufficiently large p the residual representation r̄_p: G_Q → GSp_4(F_p) is surjective and has minimal conductor N, i.e. its Artin conductor equals the conductor N of A.
items.note: The lemma combines Serre's open-image theorem (missing, see ext-serre-open-image-gsp4) with the component-group conductor comparison (missing, see conductor-of-A-p-equals-conductor-of-A).

items.name: Lemma A.7(2): the ordinary p-distinguished condition holds for a density-one set of primes
items.statement: Let A be a semistable abelian surface over Q of conductor N with End(A) = Z. For p ∤ N let α, β, p/α, p/β be the roots of the Frobenius characteristic polynomial X^4 + a_pX^3 + (2p + b_p)X^2 + p a_pX + p², labelled so that α and β are p-adic units whenever two roots are, i.e. whenever A is ordinary at p. Then for a set of primes p of density 1: αβ(α² − 1)(β² − 1)(α − β)(α²β² − 1) ≢ 0 mod p (modulo a prime of Z̄ above p). In particular A is ordinary at p (αβ ≢ 0) and condition (2) of Theorem A.1 holds for a density-one set of p.
items.note: This is a paper-specific density argument (Lemma A.8, the Weil bounds and the case analysis). The Weil bounds and Frobenius polynomials are planned (DWP.1, R01.6); the rest is missing.

items.name: Serre: open (maximal) image for abelian surfaces with End = Z
items.statement: Let A/Q be an abelian surface with End_{Q̄}(A) = Z. Then for all sufficiently large primes ℓ the image of G_Q on the ℓ-adic Tate module is GSp_4(Z_ℓ); in particular the residual image is GSp_4(F_ℓ).
items.locator: §A.4, proof of Lemma A.7(1), p. 889; proof of Lemma A.8, p. 890
items.note: No layer plans open or surjective ℓ-adic images for abelian varieties. FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.6 avoids it explicitly: 'without requiring the full Serre open-image theorem'. The source is Serre's letter to Vignéras [62], Corollaire au Théorème 3, which assumes End_{Q̄}(A) = Z. The paper assumes End(A) = Z for semistable A/Q. The two conditions agree, since endomorphisms of a semistable abelian variety are defined over an extension unramified at its semistable primes (Ribet 1975) and Q has no everywhere-unramified extension. This bridge is not stated in the paper. External input: Serre, Lettre à Marie-France Vignéras du 10/2/1986 [62], Corollaire au Théorème 3 (Œuvres IV, 38–55)

items.name: Residual conductor equals the conductor of A when p is prime to the component group
items.statement: Let A/Q be semistable at ℓ, with Néron component group Φ at ℓ (the paper takes Φ_A of the Néron model of A^∨; by Grothendieck's pairing, perfect in the semistable case, Φ(A) and Φ(A^∨) have the same order). For a prime p ≠ ℓ with p ∤ |Φ|, dim_{F_p} A[p]^{I_ℓ} = dim_{Q_p} (V_pA)^{I_ℓ}, so the (tame) conductor exponent of r̄_p at ℓ equals that of A, namely the toric rank.
items.note: Nearby layers are planned: NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.2 ('Construct the identity component, toric and abelian parts, character groups and component group'), R11.5 ('Relate monodromy and component data to the characteristic-zero local Euler polynomial'), and ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3 ('Prove that reduction cannot increase the conductor at a prime different from p'). None plans the mod-p equality dim A[p]^{I_ℓ} = dim V_p^{I_ℓ} for p ∤ |Φ| (SGA 7 IX), which is what makes the residual conductor equal N. External input: Grothendieck, SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (not cited in the paper)

items.name: Frobenius invariants a_p, b_p of an abelian surface
items.statement: For a prime p ∤ N of good reduction for A and any prime ℓ ≠ p, write the characteristic polynomial of (geometric) Frobenius Frob_p on V_ℓ = H^1(A_{Q̄}, Q_ℓ) as X^4 + a_pX^3 + (2p + b_p)X^2 + p a_pX + p², with a_p, b_p ∈ Z independent of ℓ and roots α, β, p/α, p/β. Then 2p + b_p = tr(Frob_p | ∧²V_ℓ) and a_p² = tr(Frob_p | V_ℓ ⊗ V_ℓ). With this sign convention, a_p = −tr(Frob_p | V_ℓ), and b_p = αβ + p²/(αβ) + p(α/β + β/α).
items.note: The integral, ℓ-independent Frobenius polynomial of an abelian variety with good reduction is planned. The a_p, b_p parametrisation is notation. I checked the identity b_p = αβ + p²/(αβ) + p(α/β + β/α) from the X² coefficient.

items.name: Weil bounds: |a_p|² ≤ 16p and |b_p| ≤ 4p
items.statement: For p ∤ N, all roots α, β, p/α, p/β of the Frobenius characteristic polynomial have complex absolute value √p, by Weil's Riemann hypothesis for abelian varieties over finite fields (printed 'for curves'). Hence |a_p|² ≤ 16p and |b_p| ≤ 4p.
items.note: Weil's Riemann hypothesis for abelian varieties is planned. The paper prints 'for curves'. The bounds follow at once: |a_p| ≤ 4√p, and |b_p| ≤ p + p + 2p = 4p. External input: Weil (Riemann hypothesis for abelian varieties over finite fields)

items.name: A linear congruence mod p on a positive-density set gives an exact linear relation
items.statement: Let c_0, c_1, c_2, c_3 be fixed integers. If c_0 + c_1a_p + c_2a_p² + c_3b_p ≡ 0 mod p for all p in a set of positive density, then, since |c_0 + c_1a_p + c_2a_p² + c_3b_p| ≤ Cp for a constant C (Weil bounds), there is a fixed integer k with c_0 + c_1a_p + c_2a_p² + c_3b_p = kp for all p in a subset of positive density. This is a fixed linear relation among 1, p, b_p, a_p, a_p², contradicting Lemma A.8 unless it is trivial.
items.note: This is an elementary pigeonhole step. If |x_p| ≤ Cp and p | x_p, then x_p = kp with |k| ≤ C, so some k occurs on a subset of positive density. No layer or library states it.

items.name: Lemma A.8: no fixed linear relation among 1, p, b_p, a_p, a_p² on a set of positive density
items.statement: Let A be as in Lemma A.7 (semistable abelian surface over Q with End(A) = Z). There is no fixed linear relation c_0 + c_1p + c_2b_p + c_3a_p + c_4a_p² = 0, with constant rational coefficients not all zero, that holds for all p in a set S of primes of positive density.
items.note: The paper attributes it to Deligne–Milne–Ogus–Shih [22, Proposition 2.7(1)]. The proof needs ℓ-adic Chebotarev (missing), Serre's open image (missing) and the torus independence lemma (missing).

items.name: A positive-density set of primes has a positive-density subset inert in some quadratic field
items.statement: If S is a set of primes of positive (upper) density, then there is a quadratic field K such that the primes of S inert in K have positive (upper) density.
items.locator: §A.4, proof of Lemma A.8, p. 890 ('There must be at least one quadratic field with a positive density of inert primes in S')
items.note: Proof: if S were almost entirely split in every quadratic field, Chebotarev in multiquadratic fields would bound its upper density by 2^{−k} for every k. Chebotarev for finite Galois extensions is planned in Tau Ceti Chebotarev (layer 10 'hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet', layer 14 natural density). The lemma itself is not planned. It needs the same notion of density as the rest of Lemma A.8.

items.name: Chebotarev density for ℓ-adic images (Frobenius equidistribution in Haar measure)
items.statement: Let ρ: G_Q → G be a continuous representation, unramified outside a finite set, onto a compact ℓ-adic Lie group G ⊂ GL_N(Z_ℓ) (here V_ℓ, possibly twisted by a quadratic character, with image containing GSp_4(Z_ℓ) with index ≤ 2). If Z ⊂ G is closed, conjugation-stable and of Haar measure 0, then the set of primes p with ρ(Frob_p) ∈ Z has density 0. Equivalently, a conjugation-invariant polynomial identity satisfied by ρ(Frob_p) for all p in a set of positive (upper) density holds on a subset of G of positive Haar measure.
items.locator: §A.4, proof of Lemma A.8, p. 890 ('By Chebotarev, it follows that the appropriate identity must also hold on a subset of these groups of positive measure')
items.note: The Tau Ceti Chebotarev roadmap covers finite Galois extensions only. No layer plans the ℓ-adic Haar-measure form (Serre, IHÉS 54, 1981). DWP.3 remarks, in the function-field setting, 'Number-field Chebotarev is not automatically this theorem'. ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5 plans Chebotarev density for continuous ℓ-adic representations, but only for recognition by Frobenius polynomials. External input: Chebotarev density theorem; ℓ-adic form: Serre, 'Quelques applications du théorème de densité de Chebotarev', Publ. Math. IHÉS 54 (1981) (not cited in the paper)

items.name: Linear independence of the trace functions 1, δ, tr∧² − 2δ, tr, tr² on the GSp_4 torus
items.statement: Write the eigenvalues of an element of the maximal torus of GSp_4 as x, y, δ/x, δ/y, with δ the similitude. The functions 1, δ, xy + δx/y + δy/x + δ²/(xy) (= tr ∧² − 2δ), x + y + δ/x + δ/y (= tr) and (x + y + δ/x + δ/y)² are linearly independent over Q as Laurent polynomials. Hence no non-trivial linear relation among them holds on a Zariski-dense subset of GSp_4, in particular on a subset of GSp_4(Z_ℓ) of positive Haar measure.
items.locator: §A.4, proof of Lemma A.8, p. 890 ('There are no such relations by inspection')
items.note: The linear independence of the Laurent polynomials is an elementary check. The step from 'holds on a subset of positive Haar measure' to 'holds on the torus' needs two facts: proper Zariski-closed subsets of GSp4(Z_ℓ) have Haar measure 0, and class functions are determined by their restriction to the torus. Neither is planned in this form. Mathlib has LaurentPolynomial and Matrix.symplecticGroup but nothing of this kind.

items.name: Case analysis: each vanishing factor forces a congruence on a_p, b_p
items.statement: Let p ∤ N, with a_p, b_p, α, β as in item def-frobenius-charpoly-ap-bp and congruences taken modulo a prime of Z̄ above p. Modulo p, X^4 + a_pX^3 + (2p + b_p)X^2 + p a_pX + p² ≡ X²(X² + a_pX + b_p), so A is ordinary at p iff b_p ≢ 0 mod p, and then the unit roots satisfy α + β ≡ −a_p and αβ ≡ b_p. (1) If neither β nor p/β is a p-adic unit (A not ordinary), then b_p ≡ 0 mod p. (2) If αβ ≡ ε mod p for a fixed ε ∈ {±1} (the case α²β² ≡ 1), then b_p ≡ ε mod p. (3) If α ≡ ε mod p for a fixed ε ∈ {±1} (the case α² ≡ 1; β is symmetric), then b_p + εa_p + 1 ≡ 0 mod p (printed 'b_p − εa_p + 1 ≡ 0'). (4) If α ≡ β mod p, then 4b_p − a_p² ≡ 0 mod p.
items.locator: §A.4, proof of Lemma A.7(2), cases (1)–(4), p. 890
items.note: I checked this on p. 890. Mod p the polynomial reduces to X²(X² + a_p X + b_p), so α + β ≡ −a_p and αβ ≡ b_p. Case (3) then gives b_p + εa_p + 1 ≡ 0; the paper prints 'b_p − εa_p + 1 ≡ 0'. The density argument is unaffected because ε ranges over ±1.

items.name: Odd GSp4-valued Galois representation
items.statement: For p > 2, a continuous representation r̄ : G_Q → GSp4(k) is odd if ν(r̄)(c) = −1 for a complex conjugation c. Then r̄(c) is conjugate to diag(1, 1, −1, −1): its ±1-eigenspaces are complementary isotropic planes, because ⟨cv, cw⟩ = −⟨v, w⟩. Its centraliser in sp4 is a Siegel Levi ≅ gl2, so dim_k H^0(G_∞, ad^0(r̄)) = 4. When ν(r̄) = ε̄^{−(a−1)}, oddness forces a to be even, since ε̄(c) = −1.
items.locator: §4, p. 812 (the word 'odd' is used without definition); used in the proof of Proposition 4.9, p. 817
items.note: The paper uses 'odd' without defining it: §4, p. 812 (image checked, 'a continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible Galois representation'); Remark 8.2, p. 857 ('the oddness condition forces the congruence j ≡ k mod 2'); Theorem 9.1(1), p. 878. The reading ν(r̄)(c) = −1 is supported by Remark 4.4, p. 814: 'representations r̄ with more general (odd) similitude characters'. I checked the proposed consequences. ⟨cv,cw⟩ = ν(c)⟨v,w⟩ = −⟨v,w⟩ with p > 2 makes the ±1-eigenspaces isotropic, hence both Lagrangian. The centraliser in sp4 is the Siegel Levi gl2, which gives the last bullet of the proof of Proposition 4.9, p. 817 (image checked, 'dim_k H^0(G_∞, ad^0(r̄)) = 4'). Since ε̄(c) = −1, ν(c) = (−1)^{a−1} = −1 forces a to be even; with ν = ε^{j+k−3} it forces j ≡ k mod 2, as in Remark 8.2. The proposal's 'why' is inaccurate: residual-rbar-standing-hypotheses already discusses this reading in its xnote and routes oddness to G7, but no item defines it. Library: declarations.tsv has no oddness of Galois representations and no GSp or multiplier (Mathlib's Matrix.symplecticGroup is Sp). Not planned. ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7 plans only 'polarizations rᶜ ≅ r∨⊗μ for CM fields using an actual pairing and multiplier; ... Oddness for polarized dimension n is specified by the sign at each real place'. R01.4 keeps the rank-two case ('GL₂ ... oddness calculations remain the rank-two specialization R01.4'). The CG18 precedent PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/odd-representation was likewise marked missing.

items.name: A quadratic twist relating two finite flat mod p representations is unramified at p (Raynaud)
items.statement: Let p ≥ 5 and let v | p be a place of K unramified over p. Let ρ̄, ρ̄′ : G_{K_v} → GL2(F_p) both be finite flat, or both be duals of finite flat representations. If ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄′ ⊗ χ with χ quadratic, then χ is unramified. Reason (Raynaud, e = 1 < p − 1): tame inertia acts on the semisimplification through fundamental characters with exponents in {0, 1} at level 1, or {1, p} at level 2 (negated for duals). A ramified quadratic χ restricts to inertia as ω^{(p−1)/2}, and for p ≥ 5 twisting by it moves these exponents out of the allowed set.
items.locator: §4, Remark 4.12, p. 820 ('ρ̄_p and ρ̄_p^c are both finite flat at v | p, which forces χ_p to be unramified at all primes above p')
items.note: This is an external input used without citation in Remark 4.12, p. 820 (image checked): 'Then ρ̄_p and ρ̄_p^c are both finite flat at v | p, which forces χ_p to be unramified at all primes above p.' It has no item. The xnotes of remark-4-12-elliptic-curves-big-image ('uses that a ramified quadratic twist of a finite flat representation is not finite flat, by Raynaud for e = 1 < p − 1; this is not stated') and remark-4-12-weil-restriction-big-image list it only as an input. It is distinct from ext-finite-flat-vs-galois. I checked the statement. A ramified quadratic χ restricts to inertia as ω^{(p−1)/2}. At level 1 the exponents 0, 1 move to (p−1)/2 and (p+1)/2, which lie in {0,1} mod p−1 only for p = 3. At level 2 the exponents 1, p move to (p²+1)/2 and (p²+2p−1)/2, which lie outside {0, 1, p, p+1} mod p²−1. So the claim holds for p ≥ 5 and fails at p = 3. It also holds when both representations are the same twist of finite flat ones, which covers the paper's 'duals of E[p]'. Planned coverage: R07.1, 'for finite flat commutative p-primary group schemes over a mixed-characteristic DVR with absolute ramification e<p−1 ... construct the (p,…,p)-type classification and its tame inertia characters used in R07.5 (Bull. SMF 102 (1974), §§2–3, especially Theorems 3.4.1/3.4.3)'; R07.6, 'Compare finite-flat models under field extension and twisting, and state exactly when a local deformation condition is stable under those operations'; R01.2, 'Construct tame characters and fundamental characters of levels one and two'. Library: none. declarations.tsv has no Raynaud theorem, no finite flat group schemes over Z_p (only the unrelated TauCeti.SpecialLinear center finite-flatness) and no fundamental characters.

items.name: Galois representations attached to mod-p weight-one eigenclasses
items.statement: A non-Eisenstein Hecke eigenclass in H^0(X_1(N), ω_k), or in H^1(X(Γ), ω_k) with Γ = Γ_1(N) ∩ Γ_0(x), gives rise to an irreducible Galois representation r̄ : G_Q → GL_2(k) (Deligne–Serre/Katz). A class new of level x has r̄|_{I_x} unipotent.
items.note:
This is an external input to the §5.4 heuristic (p. 831: 'A non-Eisenstein Hecke eigenclass in H^0(X_1(N), ω_k) gives rise to an irreducible Galois representation r̄'). It is not a duplicate. ext-deligne-serre-weight-one covers the characteristic-0 statement and presupposes this r̄. The H^0 case is planned in the same way as PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/residual-galois-rep-m-empty (planned at R15.5/R19.1/R15.3). The route is Gross's multiplication by the Hasse invariant, Deligne–Serre lifting with a weight change, then Deligne's representations. The covering phrases are:
- R15.3: 'Construct the Hasse invariant, Frobenius/Verschiebung and theta operator with their q-expansion formulas and Hecke compatibilities'.
- R15.5: 'Establish the passage from a mod-p eigensystem at controlled weight and level to a characteristic-zero normalised eigenform … not every Katz weight-one eigenform has a weight-one characteristic-zero lift'.
- R19.1: 'Construct the weight-two representation … and the higher-weight representation'.
- R19.4, for 'new of level x ⇒ r̄|I_x unipotent' (lift at level Γ_1(N) ∩ Γ_0(x), then reduce): 'Prove compatibility of Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representations with local Langlands, including monodromy and the special/Steinberg case'.
Not covered: the paper's H^1(X(Γ), ω_k) variant also needs Hecke-equivariant weight-one Serre duality. That is PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/hecke-equivariant-duality-H0-H1-weight-one, which is missing.
Caution: the proposed statement correctly says only 'unipotent'. The paper's §5.4 deduction ('ρ | I_x would be unipotent and hence infinite') needs r̄|I_x to be nontrivial. Newness at x alone does not obviously give that, because level-raising congruences can occur; I did not check this in weight one. The passage is heuristic, so this affects nothing.

items.name: Deligne–Serre lifting: characteristic-zero eigenforms lifting a mod-ϖ eigensystem in high weight
items.statement: Let T be a commutative O-algebra, finite over O, acting faithfully on a finite free O-module M, and let 𝔪 be a maximal ideal of T. Then T_𝔪 is O-torsion-free and each of its minimal primes is the kernel of a K̄-valued eigensystem occurring in M ⊗ K̄. In particular there is an eigenvector in M ⊗_O K̄ whose eigenvalues reduce to T → T/𝔪 ↪ k̄. Applied with M = H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a+t,b+t)(−∞)) and t ≥ N(μ): here M ⊗ K/O = H^0(…_{K/O}) (Def. 6.3), and the 𝔪-part is nonzero by Lemma 6.4 and Remark 6.5.
items.locator: §6.2, proof of Lemma 6.9, p. 840; §6.3, proof of Theorem 6.13, p. 843
items.note: No existing item states the Deligne–Serre lifting lemma. It is used implicitly on p. 840 (Lemma 6.9: 'Let f ∈ H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a+t,b+t)(−∞)) ⊗ K̄ be an eigenform for T̃_{μ′}(Q)_m') and on p. 843 ('Each such minimal prime corresponds to an eigenform f_i'). residual-galois-rep-of-maximal-ideal mentions it in its xnote ('implicitly, the Deligne–Serre lifting lemma'). R15.5 plans it: 'Prove the Deligne–Serre eigenvalue-lifting lemma for a finite Hecke algebra and its application to the relevant modular-form modules'. The decomposition node is AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.5/deligne-serre-eigenvalue-lifting-lemma: 'M a finitely generated free module over a discrete valuation ring O … commuting endomorphisms … there exist … O′ … and a nonzero element f′ of O′ ⊗_O M which is an eigenvector … with eigenvalues a′_T ≡ a_T'. The proposed minimal-prime form follows by standard commutative algebra, and I checked it. T is contained in End_O(M), so T is O-torsion-free, and T_𝔪 is a direct factor of T. A minimal prime ℘ of T_𝔪 does not contain ϖ, which is a nonzerodivisor. M ⊗ K is faithful over the Artinian ring T ⊗ K, so ℘ is an associated prime of M ⊗ K and gives an eigenvector over K̄. The Siegel application (M = H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a+t,b+t)(−∞)), free over O, with t ≥ N(μ)) belongs to the existing missing items residual-galois-rep-of-maximal-ideal and hecke-algebra-embeds-in-product-over-eigenforms. It is not part of this lemma. Neither library has the lemma: I searched the declaration index for Deligne–Serre and eigenvalue-lifting names.

items.name: Brauer–Nesbitt: semisimple representations are determined by characteristic polynomials
items.statement: Two semisimple finite-dimensional representations of a group over a field with the same characteristic polynomial for every element are isomorphic. For continuous representations of G_Q unramified outside a finite set, equality at Frob_x for x outside a finite set suffices, by Chebotarev and continuity.
items.locator: §6.2, Lemma 6.9 and Definition 6.11, p. 840; §6.3, p. 841 ('The representations r̄_m, r̄_{m_∅}, and r̄ are all isomorphic')
items.note:
This is an implicit external input. It makes r̄_m in Lemma 6.9 well defined up to isomorphism (the lemma specifies only 'semisimple' and the Frobenius characteristic polynomials, p. 840). Definition 6.11 depends on that. So does p. 841, 'The representations r̄_m, r̄_{m_∅}, and r̄ are all isomorphic'. Planned stages:
- R01.1: 'prove independence of lattice by characteristic polynomials and the characteristic-p Brauer–Nesbitt theorem'.
- R01.5: 'Prove Chebotarev recognition for semisimple continuous characteristic-zero and residual representations … Use characteristic polynomials, not traces alone in small characteristic'. The reviewed node for R01.5 cites Brauer–Nesbitt (Curtis–Reiner 30.16).
The Frobenius form also needs Chebotarev, which is the existing item ext-chebotarev-density (planned in Tau Ceti Chebotarev Layer 10). Not in the libraries. Tau Ceti has only Representation.nonempty_equiv_of_character_eq (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/Determined.lean, 'For a finite group over a field of characteristic zero, finite-dimensional representations are determined by their characters'). That covers neither characteristic p nor profinite G_Q.

items.name: Carayol: lifts of an absolutely irreducible r̄ with equal Frobenius characteristic polynomials are conjugate; compatible lifts glue
items.statement: Let R be a complete local Noetherian O-algebra with residue field k and r̄: G_Q → GSp4(k) absolutely irreducible. If r, r′: G_Q → GSp4(R) are continuous lifts of r̄ whose characteristic polynomials agree at Frob_x for all x outside a finite set, then r′ = grg^{−1} for some g ∈ ker(GSp4(R) → GSp4(k)). Consequently, if R = lim R/𝔞_m for a decreasing chain of ideals and the r_m: G_Q → GSp4(R/𝔞_m) are lifts with characteristic polynomials in the images of fixed elements of R, then the r_m can be conjugated to be compatible, and they glue to a lift over R.
items.locator: §6.3, proof of Theorem 6.13, p. 842 ('it suffices to construct, for each m > 0, a representation r_m'); §6.4, proof of Theorem 6.17, p. 846 (the α- and β-surjections)
items.note: No existing item states this. thm-6-13-hecke-valued-lift-regular-weight's xnote says 'compatibility up to conjugation by Carayol's lemma, implicit'. doubling-unramified-plane-from-alpha-and-beta-lines's xnote says 'Carayol's lemma identifies the two representations'. ext-gluing-galois-reps-over-hecke-algebra is existence inside ∏ O_{K_i}, not uniqueness. The GL_n content is planned. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/carayol-trace-uniqueness is planned at R01.5/IHG.1/R19.6. IHG.1 plans reconstruction 'over complete local rings when residual absolute irreducibility supplies an actual representation'. IHG.4 plans 'uniqueness from Frobenius density using Chebotarev and continuity' and 'passage to inverse limits'. Not planned: the GSp4 form, in which the conjugating g can be taken in ker(GSp4(R) → GSp4(k)). That is needed because deformations in §4 are ker(GSp4(R)→GSp4(k))-conjugacy classes (p. 815), and because the r_m of p. 842 must glue as GSp4-valued lifts. The refinement is Schur's lemma: if r̄ is absolutely irreducible, the r-invariant alternating forms with fixed multiplier form a free rank-one R-module, so a GL4-conjugator g satisfies g^T J g = cJ with c ≡ 1. I checked the statement and it is correct. No stage plans GSp_{2n}- or similitude-valued Galois representations: an atlas search for GSp/symplectic finds only G7's CM-field polarizations.

items.name: Square roots of characters that are trivial modulo the maximal ideal (p odd)
items.statement: Let p be odd, R a complete local Noetherian O-algebra with residue field of characteristic p, and χ: G → R^× a continuous character with χ ≡ 1 mod 𝔪_R. Then there is a unique continuous ψ: G → R^× with ψ² = χ and ψ ≡ 1 mod 𝔪_R, since squaring is an automorphism of the pro-p group 1 + 𝔪_R. If χ has finite order, so does ψ. If χ is trivial on a subgroup (e.g. an inertia group), so is ψ.
items.locator: §6.3, Theorem 6.13(4), p. 842; §6.4, proof of Theorem 6.17, p. 846 ('Since p is odd, we can find a square root of χ_Q')
items.note:
This construction is used in the statement of Theorem 6.13(4) (p. 842, 'After twisting by the unique square-root of χ_{μ,0} which is trivial modulo m'). It is also used in the proof of Theorem 6.17 (p. 846, 'Since p is odd, we can find a square root of χ_Q'). thm-6-13-4-weakly-minimal-after-twist and thm-6-17-construction-of-r-m use it but do not state it. I checked the statement, including the uniqueness and inertia-triviality clauses.
The libraries have the pointwise core:
- TauCeti.HenselianRing.exists_pow_eq_and_sub_one_mem_of_sub_one_mem (TauCeti/RingTheory/Henselian.lean): 'if n is invertible, I ≤ J and w ≡ 1 mod I, then w = a ^ n for some a ≡ 1 mod I'.
- Mathlib's IsAdicComplete.henselianRing (Mathlib/RingTheory/Henselian.lean).
- IsLocalRing.eq_of_eval_eq_zero_of_not_isUnit_sub (same file), which gives uniqueness of a root in a residue class with unit derivative 2a, for p odd.
The character-level statement is in neither library: multiplicativity of ψ from uniqueness, continuity of ψ, finite order, and triviality on subgroups where χ is trivial. No stage plans it. The analogous CG18 note (thm-3-11-minimal-twist) says 'Not planned: the p-power-order square root η (p > 2)'.

items.name: Borel–Casselman: Iwahori-spherical representations are subquotients of unramified principal series
items.statement: An irreducible admissible representation of GSp4(Q_x) with nonzero vectors fixed by the Iwahori subgroup I(x) is a subquotient of a principal series induced from an unramified character of the diagonal torus. In particular this holds when π_x has nonzero Π(x)-fixed vectors, since I(x) ⊂ Π(x).
items.locator: §6.3, proof of Theorem 6.13, p. 844 ('Then π_x is a subquotient of an unramified principal series')
items.note: This is an uncited external input on p. 844: 'Consider first the case where π_x has nontrivial Π(x)-invariants. Then π_x is a subquotient of an unramified principal series.' ext-genestier-tilouine-unramified-at-TW-primes names the consequence only in a parenthetical ('so that it is a subquotient of an unramified principal series'). remark-gsp4-parahoric-oldforms cites Borel–Casselman for fixed-vector counts. No item states the theorem. I checked the statement: Borel 1976 and Casselman 1980, with I(x) ⊂ Π(x). The atlas does not plan it. SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups plans induction and Jacquet functors (SR.2), 'the subquotient description by supercuspidal support' (SR.3), and Satake for hyperspecial K (SR.4). None of these names Iwahori-fixed vectors or Borel's theorem, and no decomposition node mentions Casselman or Iwahori-fixed vectors in this sense. The libraries have only finite-field GL2 principal series (TauCeti.GL2BorelRep and related), not p-adic groups.

items.name: Galois representations are defined over a finite extension and admit an integral symplectic model
items.statement: A continuous representation G_Q → GL4(K̄) takes values in GL4(K′) for some finite extension K′/K (Baire category). If it preserves a symplectic form up to a similitude character and its residual representation is absolutely irreducible, then it is GSp4(K′)-conjugate to a representation into GSp4(O_{K′}). Proof sketch: take a stable lattice. Its dual is stable, hence homothetic to it, so after rescaling the form it is perfect on the lattice.
items.locator: §6.2, proof of Proposition 6.8, p. 839 ('The usual Baire category argument implies that r_f can be defined over a finite extension of K'); §6.3, proof of Theorem 6.13, p. 843 ('r_{f_i}: G_Q → GSp4(O_{K′_i})')
items.note: Keep only the integral-model half. The Baire half is already in galois-rep-of-regular-weight-cuspidal-eigenform. Its statement reads 'r_f: G_Q → GSp4(K′), for a finite extension K′/K', and its xnote says 'A Baire category argument gives a finite field of definition'. The integral half is used silently on p. 843: 'The eigenform f_i has an associated Galois representation r_{f_i}: G_Q → GSp4(O_{K′_i}) … by Proposition 6.8'. But Proposition 6.8 (p. 839) gives only 'r_f : G_Q → GSp4(K′)'. ext-gluing-galois-reps-over-hecke-algebra needs the GSp4(O_{K′_i}) form as a hypothesis. I checked the proposed proof and it is correct. The multiplier takes values in O^× by compactness. The dual lattice is stable. Stable lattices are homothetic because r̄ is irreducible. A perfect alternating form over a DVR has a symplectic basis. R01.1 plans only the GL_n part: 'For field coefficients construct invariant lattices using compactness'. No stage plans the symplectic/similitude refinement: an atlas search for GSp/symplectic finds only G7's CM-field polarizations.

items.name: The cuspidal automorphic representation π attached to a Siegel eigenform f
items.statement: Fix ι: K ↪ C. For a cuspidal eigenform f ∈ H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)) with a ≥ b ≥ 3, let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GSp4(A_Q) that contributes to the f-part of H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_C) under the isomorphism of Theorem 5.2(1), with σ = (−b, −a; 6−a−b) as in Remark 5.10. Then r_f is defined as R_p(π) of [55, Theorem 3.5].
items.note:
Kept as a construction. The paper uses it at three points, but no existing item isolates it; it appears only inside galois-rep-of-regular-weight-cuspidal-eigenform's xnote and in the wording of ext-arthur-transfer-GSp4-to-GL4.

Where it is used (checked on the p. 839, 840 and 844 texts):
- p. 839, proof of Prop. 6.8: 'let π be an cuspidal automorphic representation of GSp4(A_Q) which contributes to the f-part of H^0(X_1(Q), ω(a,b)(−∞)_C) under the isomorphism of Theorem 5.2(1) (with σ = (−b,−a;6−a−b), as in Remark 5.10)'.
- p. 840, Lemma 6.9: 'the transfer to GL4 (given by [3]) of the automorphic representation generated by f'.
- p. 844, Theorem 6.13: 'Let π be the automorphic representation generated by f_i', followed by the analysis of π_x at x ∈ S(r̄) ∪ Q.

Mathematically this is the degree-0 case of thm-5-2-1: there H^0_cusp maps isomorphically onto H̄^0 = H^0(ω(a,b)(−∞)). It also uses the restricted tensor factorisation π = ⊗'π_x.

Reading note: GSp4 has no strong multiplicity one (Arthur packets share almost all Hecke eigenvalues). So 'the automorphic representation generated by f' must mean an irreducible cuspidal constituent, which is how p. 839 phrases it. Each constituent receives a nonzero K-fixed, Hecke-eigen component of f, and that is all the proofs use.

Why missing: nothing plans the Siegel classical-to-adelic dictionary.
- AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.5 plans only 'the GL_2/Q dictionary with classical modular forms, slash actions, central character and normalized Hecke operators'.
- AutomorphicBundles:B4 plans Siegel forms as sections ('For Siegel data, identify the Hodge vector bundle, its determinant, and Schur-functor weights') but not the passage to automorphic representations.
- Harris's comparison theorem (thm-5-2-1) is missing.

items.name: The trace map tr for X_0(Q) → X and the constant d_Q
items.statement:
tr is the trace for the finite covering X_0(Q) → X, which is étale over Y. It acts as tr : H^i(X_0(Q), W^sub_{μ,M}) → H^i(X, W^sub_{μ,M}), and likewise for S_0(Q) → S.
- tr∘i = d_Q, where d_Q := ∏_{x∈Q}[GSp4(Z_x) : Π(x)] = ∏_{x∈Q}(1 + x + x² + x³), the number of lines in F_x^4.
- Since x ≡ 1 mod p, d_Q ≡ 4^{|Q|} mod p, which is prime to p because p is odd.
- tr commutes with multiplication by h and h̃ and with Hecke operators away from Q.
The paper gives only the name and '(which is prime to p)'. The index formula and the congruence are our computation.
items.locator: §7.1, Theorem 7.3, p. 847; used in Lemmas 7.4–7.6, pp. 848–850
items.note:
Kept as a construction, in line with how taylor-wiles-projector-pr-Q was split off from Theorem 7.2.

The paper only names tr. p. 847 (image), Theorem 7.3: 'd_Q = ∏_{x∈Q}[GSp4(Z_x) : Π(x)] (which is prime to p) and tr is the trace map associated to X_0(Q) → X'. It then uses d_Q^{-1}tr as a vertical map in Lemmas 7.4–7.6 (pp. 848–850), including for S_0(Q) → S on the nonordinary loci (Lemma 7.5, p. 849).

What is already in the extraction: thm-7-3-high-weight-genestier-tilouine defines d_Q and tr inline, and its xnote has the count. This item adds tr as a construction, together with tr∘i = d_Q and the compatibilities of tr with h, h̃ and the Hecke operators away from Q. The corrected inverse c_Q^{-1}d_Q^{-1}tr needs all of these.

Checks:
- GSp4(F_x) acts transitively on the lines of F_x^4 (every line is isotropic), and Π(x) is the preimage of the stabiliser of a line. So the index is 1+x+x²+x³ = (x+1)(x²+1). For x ≡ 1 mod p this is ≡ 4, a unit since p is odd.
- Correction to the proposed statement: the paper never says X_0(Q) → X is finite. §5.2 (p. 822) only chooses toroidal compactifications 'so that the natural map Y_{K_0(Q)} → Y_K extends'. Over Y the map is finite étale of degree d_Q (the level is neat). So tr∘i = d_Q holds on Y, and it extends to X because W^sub is locally free on an O-flat scheme in which Y is fibrewise dense.

Why planned:
- B5: 'Construct pullback, coefficient identification, and trace along Hecke correspondences. State all scalar normalizations … Treat non-neat levels through equivariance/descent, not division by a group order that may be noninvertible.'
- B5's completion condition: 'Classical forms are usable over number fields and the specified integral PEL/Hilbert models.' Its handoff also covers 'When coefficients have torsion'.
- C3: 'For a morphism of data or a Hecke translation, choose compatible source and target fans and construct the extension.'
- The affine-local identity tr∘i = rank is mathlib:Algebra.trace_algebraMap (Mathlib/RingTheory/Trace/Defs.lean:111: trace R S (algebraMap R S x) = finrank R S • x).

Caveat for the reviewer: existing items (thm-7-3-high-weight-genestier-tilouine, lemma-8-8, hecke-operators-at-p-on-M-mod-p) read B5 as characteristic 0 only. The completion condition quoted above contradicts that reading, and the two should be reconciled.

items.name: Weight-one mod p eigenforms: ρ̄ unramified at p with T_p = trace (Gross; Coleman–Voloch)
items.statement: Let f be a mod p Katz eigenform of weight one and level N prime to p, with Galois representation ρ̄_f. Then ρ̄_f is unramified at p, and ρ̄_f(Frob_p) has characteristic polynomial X² − a_p(f)X + ⟨p⟩ (Gross for a_p² ≠ 4⟨p⟩, Coleman–Voloch in general). Consequently T_p − (α+β) and ⟨p⟩ − αβ are nilpotent on H^0(X_1(N), ω_{O/ϖ})_m.
items.locator: used implicitly in §8.6, statement and proof of Lemma 8.14, pp. 865–866
items.note:
Kept. This is an uncited external input to Lemma 8.14, and no item in items_merged covers it:
- gross-weight-one-Tp-q-expansion is only T = U + ⟨p⟩V on q-expansions;
- ext-deligne-serre-weight-one is characteristic 0.

How Lemma 8.14 uses it:
- The statement (p. 865, image) says 'ρ̄(Frob_p) has eigenvalues α and β', which presupposes that ρ̄ is unramified at p.
- The proof (p. 866) needs T ≡ α+β on M_m to get M ⊂ N_α ⊕ N_β, and ⟨p⟩ ≡ αβ to reduce to ⟨p⟩F = αβF.

CG20 cites Gross [35] only on p. 860 (the bibliography says '(60)'), for Prop. 4.1 in the proof of Lemma 8.8, and does not cite Coleman–Voloch at all. Lemma 8.14 assumes α ≠ β, so only Gross's p-distinguished case is needed. The Gross / Coleman–Voloch attribution is the standard one; it was not checked against either source.

Why missing:
- PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/gross-Up-eigenvalues: 'They also use Gross's Proposition 12.1: the representation of a mod-p weight-one eigenform is unramified at p, with the expected Frobenius polynomial. No layer plans Proposition 12.1'.
- SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.5: 'Do not claim this layer proves the general Katz weight-one refinement.'
- AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.5 only flags that 'not every Katz weight-one eigenform has a weight-one characteristic-zero lift'.

Overlaps: new raw item 13 (ext-mod-p-weight-one-galois-representations, §5.4) gives existence of r̄ but not unramifiedness at p. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/companion-forms is the converse direction (unramified at p ⇒ weight one).

items.name: The strata Y ⊃ Z ⊃ S of X ⊗ O/ϖ used in §8.4
items.statement: Y is the non-ordinary locus: the closed locus of p-rank ≤ 1, equal to the reduced zero locus of the Hasse invariant h, and called 'the rank 1 strata' in the paper. Z ⊂ Y is the supersingular locus (p-rank 0), a curve whose components are P¹'s. S ⊂ Z is the finite superspecial locus S_(0,0) (a(A) = 2). Y avoids the boundary, since h has q-expansion 1, so Y is proper. The restriction sequences are 0 → W ⊗ ω^{−(p−1)} → W → W|_Y → 0 on X and 0 → W ⊗ O_Y(−Z) → W|_Y → W|_Z → 0 on Y.
items.note:
Kept as the definition of the p-rank strata of X_k.

p. 862 (image): 'Let X = X_1(Q), and denote the rank 1 strata (resp., the supersingular locus, the superspecial locus) by Y, Z, and S'. The p-rank ≥ 1 locus is also used in Lemma 8.8 (p. 860). Y is the same object as §7's S in nonordinary-locus-S (the zero locus V(h)). Z and S are used by koblitz-supersingular-locus-cartier-in-p-rank-one, supersingular-components-P1-hodge-bundle, the two yamauchi-* items, theorem-8-10/8-11 and hecke-at-p-via-almost-ordinary-locus-and-hartogs, but no item defines them. That last item's note says the stratification is 'planned nowhere'.

Corrections to the proposed statement:
(1) 'Y avoids the boundary, since h has q-expansion 1, so Y is proper' is wrong. Over the 1-dimensional cusps the semi-abelian fibres are extensions of an elliptic curve by G_m. The Hasse invariant vanishes where that elliptic curve is supersingular, so the p-rank ≤ 1 locus meets the boundary. The paper itself says h̃ 'extends to the boundary (by the normality of the p-rank 1 locus)' (p. 849, image). Y is proper only because it is closed in the proper X_k. Z does avoid the boundary, since the toric part gives p-rank ≥ 1 there, and so Z lies in the open part.
(2) Agreed: 'rank 1 strata' must be read as the closed p-rank ≤ 1 locus V(h). This is needed for Z ⊂ Y and for the sequence on pp. 862–863, which comes from 0 → W⊗ω^{−(p−1)} →(h) W → W|_Y → 0 (cf. hasse-multiplication-exact-sequences). The sequence on Y with O_Y(−Z) ≅ ω^{−(p²−1)/2}|_Y is the Koblitz item.

Why missing: nothing plans Siegel p-rank strata.
- IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.0 builds Newton strata only for its CSnc unitary datum ('Instantiate PELModuli M0–M3's actual integral-model objects for this split datum').
- An atlas search for p-rank, supersingular and superspecial found no Siegel layer.
